subject: she's thrilled
preview: she wrote a christmas poem about charlie's neck
html:
It started like a Christmas poem…

A college girl stepped up to the mic at the University of Texas at San Antonio.

A perfectly normal-looking girl. Could be your sister, your daughter, your granddaughter.

She smiled. It’s a nice smile. Warm… happy…

Then she started to read.

It was the night before the Kirkiversary, and all through the house,
not a creature was stirring, not even a mouse.
The flags were hung proudly, the memes all on deck,
as we solemnly remembered a shot to the neck.

She was still smiling.

Then she invited everyone to the party… she called it “Squirt for Kirk.”

She stood in front of a Turning Point card table… the same kind that Charlie used to sit behind before… well… you know.

Behind the table sat a man named Christian Collins. I don't really know anything about him, but he seems like a good man. A Christian, like Charlie. He's obviously there to carry on Charlie's work in the best way he knows how.

He asked her if she was happy with herself.

"I'm thrilled," she said.

She meant it… you can tell. She’s proud of herself.

Then she looked at him, and with glee told him he was brave for being out there with no protection…

No neck brace.

He told her he'd pray for her… and that was it. The interaction was over.

You can watch it for yourself here.

She'll go back to her friends a hero. In her world, what she just did was brave… and cool. The fact that we're all sharing it on social media, appalled, is the icing on her cake.

This wasn't just a one-off. Today, on the same tour, at the University of Oregon, a protester held up a sign:

"Fuck him right in the neck hole."

He was sipping on his drink like he was waiting for the bus. No one around him seemed bothered. Even the sign was completely normal on that campus. Hardly even worth a look.

Back in August, I shared a quote from Sam Hyde with you. He’s a popular comedian and commentator who a lot of the younger, right-wing guys like.

"When we win, do not forget that these people want you broke, dead, your kids raped and brainwashed, and they think it's funny."

Some people think this goes too far. I don't. This week proved him right… again.

So here we are. These people want us dead. And they think it's funny. It's cool. On campus, behaving this way gets you social status.

They've been trained to believe they're rebels fighting the system… but they're the regime's shock troops, and they don't even realize it.

The Flock… remember The Flock? I wrote about it in my piece “The Desecration of Charlie Kirk.”

Picture a murmuration: thousands of birds moving through the sky like one giant shape, with no leader. Here's how I described it:

Every single bird in that flock is doing one simple thing: watching the few birds closest to it and matching them. That's it. No bird sees the whole shape, or gets to decide what form it takes.

There was no coordination between the girl in Texas and the guy in Oregon making the same joke. There didn't need to be. That's the Flock.

That’s the thing that rules America. It answers to no one.

And it's not just college kids. Two days after Charlie was killed, Ilhan Omar shared a video that called him "Dr. Frankenstein" and said "his monster shot him through the neck." Then she went on CNN to defend it.

A sitting congresswoman… on national television… murmuring with the Flock… as one.

So what do we do about it?

Christian Collins, after he heard that poem… he said he’d pray for her. He’s receiving a lot of criticism for that, from our people… on the right. I saw dozens of posts like this one:

"If your only reaction is 'I will pray for you' then they most assuredly will get their wish."

I get it. I kind of felt the same way, if I’m being honest. I'm not criticizing him. I don't know how I'd respond in that situation. But it did read as kind of weak.

I don’t want to just pray my way to my grave. I want to win. I want to defeat this thing. This… Flock.

In the Desecration piece, my last words were “Bear your cross, soldier.”

A cross, and a soldier. A prayer, and a sword. The prayer keeps the sword true. The sword gives the prayer teeth. You need both.

Who holds the sword? The prosecutors… the judges… the people who write the laws.

The people who hold the sword fund the universities and decide what is acceptable there. They decided Iryna Zarutska had to ride a train with a man who'd been arrested 14 times.

The universities are the front lines of this war. Charlie knew that. So does the Flock.

On Tuesday, you decide whether the man trying to take back the sword keeps the Senate he needs to do it.

Vote Republican down the ticket. Bring your friends. Do it for Charlie and Iryna.

stay close,
~ Clay

subject: nathan
preview: he thinks his candidate is a criminal
html:
"I think he's a criminal and a cheater."

That's what Nathan, one of my readers, told me about the man he's voting for next week.

I told him I’m proud of him.

Sounds a bit strange, doesn’t it? Why would I encourage my audience to vote for someone they view as a criminal and a cheater?

Here’s what he wrote to me:

You've been instrumental in a decision I was trying to make. I live in Texas. I'm in the middle of the Talarico/Paxton race. And from some of my emails to you, you might know I care a lot about values and morality. It makes it hard for me to support some candidates.

But because of you I decided my vote will go to Paxton, despite the fact that I think he's a criminal and a cheater. You convinced me that this election is about more than my dislike of a person on moral grounds. I was never going to vote Talarico in a million years, but I realized that not voting for either was to allow the murder-and-regime party to take the Senate, and I won't do that.

I have to tell you, this was one of the best emails I've received in a while. It's the kind that reminds me why I do this.

I was interviewed on a podcast recently, and in that interview I said there are plenty of people in the MAGA coalition who disgust me. The panel agreed with me.

Here’s what I said next:

"It's okay to vote Republican down ticket in the midterms. Even if you don't like that guy that's running in your local area, just swallow your pride and do it anyway. And maybe next time, try to primary him."

This is something that my libertarian heart would have fought against tooth and nail. A few years ago, I would’ve looked at someone like Nathan as a sellout. "Where are your principles?!"

Then Charlie got shot, and I stopped caring about having clean hands. Have you seen what we’re up against?

This isn't a debate club anymore. If the other side holds the power, guess how much your moral principles are worth?

Sure, there are scoundrels on our side. Scammers… warmongers… some real nasty folks. Some of them are probably even snakes in the grass, just waiting for their moment to betray us.

Welcome to politics. It’s full of cheaters, criminals, adulterers, alcoholics and all kinds of other degenerates. Nobody thinks this is an honest business.

Even the founding fathers were not innocent of this. Alexander Hamilton had an affair and paid blackmail to the woman's husband. Thomas Jefferson tried to seduce a close friend's wife. Ben Franklin wrote a letter advising young men on how to choose a mistress.

And yet, most Americans still hold these men in high regard... why? Because they won. If they'd lost, their sins would be all anyone talked about… if we talked about them at all.

It’s not about the individuals, it’s about the coalition.

The winner gets to write the history books.

Do you want the people who celebrated Charlie's murder deciding what your grandkids learn about him? Do you want Luigi Mangione remembered as a folk hero? George Floyd as a saint?

“There are no solutions. There are only trade-offs.” ~ Thomas Sowell

Nathan made his trade-off. He has no illusions about what he’s doing anymore. He’s playing the game with the cards he was dealt, not the cards he wanted.

Next Tuesday, play the cards you've got.

Support the MAGA coalition down the ticket… and bring a friend or two with you.

stay close,
~ Clay

subject: i didn't go far enough
preview: six months ago I called them criminals
html:
I posted a question on my Sowell page tonight:

Is the Democratic Party a criminal organization?
Yes or No

It’s only been up for an hour or two as I write this, but hundreds of people have answered already. The overwhelming consensus of that audience is… yes. Absolutely.

Six months ago, I told you to stop treating Democrats like a political opponent. Here's what I wrote:

Democrats are a murderous criminal organization... that's the new frame. I'm not joking, I'm not being hyperbolic. Embrace this. Not "democrats are the real racists," not "democrats don't understand economics"... not even "democrats are communists." No... it's much more base than that. They are criminals. They are killers. They are liars. And anyone who votes for them at this point is complicit. Do you think this is too harsh? Write to me if you do, I want to hear you out.

You're not debating them anymore. You're pursuing an indictment...

That was early in our relationship. Many of you were not on the list yet. To those that were… you are the OGs. Thank you for staying with me.

Now, here we are… six months later… I’m re-reading what I wrote, and I don’t think I went far enough. "Criminal" makes them sound small.

What is a criminal? Someone who breaks the law. These people write the laws.

A real criminal runs from the courts… these people sic them on their enemies. Ask Trump about that… or Douglass Mackey, convicted for posting a meme… the J6 grandmas, or the pro-lifers that Biden’s DOJ put in prison for blocking an abortion clinic. I could go on for pages… but you get the point.

Remember Senator Slotkin? I wrote about her recently… she told a room full of students she wants to prosecute the people who worked for Trump, so the next generation is too scared to. She called it a "deterrence message."

So what do you call that?

A regime… and regimes don’t lose power when they lose an election.

Our friends, the progressives, like to call the Trump administration “The Regime” now…

I’ll concede that Trump wants to be the regime… is trying to be the regime… but he’s not. Not even close. What he is is a thorn in the regime’s side. So are you, and everyone on board with the MAGA coalition.

But do not kid yourself and assume Trump and MAGA are the ones in power just because we won an election or two.

We are something to be purged. They showed you what they think of you by how they responded to Charlie’s assassination… and how they wished Trump didn’t turn his head at Butler.

That's the bad news… the good news is they're scared of us too… that's why they're trying so hard. This is why I’m optimistic. They don’t act like Slotkin when they don’t feel threatened.

Prey doesn't see the predator coming… but you see it now. So, lock in… you’re in it now. We are happy warriors.

The next fight is in front of us. November 3rd. Vote, and bring someone with you.

I’ll keep working on our friends, the libertarians. I know for a fact I’ve flipped some… and I’ll keep working to flip more.

That’s the best I can do up here in Snow Mexico.

The rest is up to you.

stay close,
~ Clay

subject: i want to leave
preview: but I can't
html:
I’m as Canadian as they come. Born and raised.

On the podcast I was on the other night, after I introduced myself, Matt… one of the hosts, said, “I hear the Canadian accent coming through.”

I’ve always been proud to be a Canadian… well, most of my life. I’m finding it much more challenging these days. The country I live in now is not the country I grew up in.

My grandfather was a WW2 combat veteran who fought alongside Americans, and spent his military career working with them on missile defense systems. My dad even grew up living in Texas for part of his childhood.

Our countries have had one of the strongest relationships the world has ever seen, but that’s over now… and I don’t blame Trump, as most Canadians do. I blame our leadership, and every single person who voted for them.

Just this week, our prime minister posted a clip of a speech he gave at Davos and called it “Canada’s path.”

We are ruled by the Davos crowd, and they’re managing our decline like it’s a business plan. It’s all about benefiting the European powers, and being a thorn in the side of the Trump administration. What’s good for Canadians like me is a secondary thought, at best.

I’ve thought about leaving this country, many times over the last few years. I still think about it. I don’t want to do it, honestly. Canada is my home. My family is here… everyone I love.

My parents are elderly, and I want to be close for when they need me.

But I also don’t want to sit and watch everything I loved about this country decay around me and turn into something else.

That’s why I perk up whenever Trump jokes about making us the 51st state. I’d sign up tomorrow. But please, whatever you do, don’t let us vote.

This is a fantasy. I can’t see it happening anytime soon… if ever… but a boy can dream, can’t he?

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: don't you dare
preview: she said she'd reply less
html:
I have quite a few Marys in my audience. Never met a Mary I didn’t like. As a general rule, if I meet a lady named Mary, I know she’s one of the good ones.

There’s gotta be at least one bad one out there somewhere, right? Haven’t met her yet.

Anyway, one of my favorite Marys wrote me this morning. She responds to most of my emails, and I look forward to each one. She calls herself my #1 fan, and I believe her.

But today she wrote, “Maybe I should reply less.” She was responding to my recent email about getting overwhelmed by replies and struggling to give all of you the attention I think you deserve.

My heart sank a little. That’s the last thing I wanted.

I wrote back right away: “Don’t you dare.”

Her emails are one of the best parts of my day.

So let me be clear: keep writing. All of you. I’d rather be buried in your emails than live without them. I may not be able to respond to all of them sometimes, but you have my word that I read every single one.

So, Mary... don’t you dare stop. That goes for the rest of you too.

This connection we have, it’s important to me.

subject: i shook his hand
preview: one of the most powerful men in Canada
html:
This morning I shook hands with one of the most powerful progressive politicians in Canada.

He’s in my extended family through marriage, and we were both at the same funeral. It’s not a name Americans are likely to recognize, but I would bet most Canadians would. For privacy’s sake, I’ll leave it at that.

He was kind and gracious. He didn’t really seem to want to talk to me, but I wasn’t offended.

On TV he’s a force… like a supervillain… someone who can piss off legions of conservatives without breaking a sweat.

In real life? He was frail, he was very old… and utterly human.

That frail old man has more power than every libertarian podcaster in America combined.

Tonight, I went on a podcast to talk about exactly that. It was my first interview ever. It started at 6pm Eastern, so maybe a few of you found it and watched.

Before it started, I was nervous… like really nervous. I was lying on my bed desperately trying to get my resting heart rate below 100, and failing. When the host sent me the link, it jumped to 135.

Now it’s over, and I’m sitting here writing you this email with a heart rate of about 65-70.

I think it went okay. Maybe even good. I stumbled a few times, lost my train of thought once… and the other guys talked a lot more than I did, but I had a really good time. It was fun.

I don’t think it was the disaster I feared… phew.

It’s almost two hours long, and it’s a different crowd than you’re used to from me.

The hosts are both Orthodox Christians, and they’re deep in what’s called the post-libertarian world. They’re not afraid of ideas that make people uncomfortable, so there may be a few moments that make some of you squirm. That’s okay, we’re all adults here, right?

I might try to pull a couple clips tomorrow and get them up on Twitter, if I can find the time. There were some moments I really enjoyed… got a few laughs, which is always a good sign.

If you want to hear it before then, here’s the whole thing.

I timestamped it to start when I introduce myself.

Maybe say something nice about me in the comments, if you want to make me feel good, haha.

Funny thing is… I was more scared of that podcast than I was of shaking hands with one of the most powerful men in Canada. Strange, right?

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I’d really like to hear your thoughts if you watched it. Even if you didn’t like it, I can handle it.

subject: i can’t keep up
preview: you broke my inbox
html:
What an absolutely insane response to yesterday’s email. I mean that in the best possible way.

I can’t keep up with all of you, no matter how desperately I try. I reply to one email, and then I have 3 more pop up. I’m being overrun with prayers, stories, and reading recommendations.

One man told me he was saved at 42… almost exactly my age. A grandmother told me she wanted to hug me after reading. Another reader sent me a few private notes about God that he’d never shared with anyone. And so many of you promised never to tell my niece, haha. I loved that most of all.

All of this is a good problem to have, but it frustrates me. Each and every one of you deserves a thoughtful reply… and I work very hard to give it to you, but at this rate… just replying to emails is going to become my full-time job, especially as the list continues to grow.

And the emails are only part of what I do… I run the Sowell page, and I’ve started a Clarence Thomas page too. I have my own community at StopBeingPrey.com where I build and code everything myself. On top of all that, I always have a few cornerstone pieces in progress, which I research, write and promote all by myself. And I'm working on a book.

But you are my priority. These emails and my connection to you are the heart and soul of everything I do.

Still, I'm a mere mortal, with only so much time… but I know who buys me that time. My patrons.

They're the ones who hold me up on their shoulders. None of this is possible, at this scale, without them. Otherwise, I’d have to focus my time on other work… probably building software for clients.

It really is so crazy to me that I have ‘fans’. I’ve always been a fan of others, but I’ve never been in a position to have fans myself. I don’t think I’ll ever get used to it.

And not just fans, but people who are willing to pay me to keep going. I can’t tell you how much this means to me. This work, and my relationship with you, is among the most meaningful things I’ve ever done with my life.

You made me into a writer. Thank you and God bless you.

subject: don't tell anyone
preview: i pray a lot
html:
I pray a lot. Only in the last year or so, though…

Since Charlie was killed, it’s something I just started doing intuitively. What happened to him scared me so bad, and I had no one who really understood what I was feeling.

And so, I started talking to God… not even sure if He exists. I reached for Him in desperation. What did I have to lose?

Sometimes I just go for a walk in nature, and basically shout at the sky. I express gratitude for the things I have. I talk about loved ones who have passed, the ones I miss. I ask God to tell them I love them… I often end up in tears.

Don’t tell anyone. No one has seen me cry in decades. My 12-year-old niece is puzzled by it. She’s never seen me cry, and she wonders if I ever have. I'm trying to keep it that way.

I’m not even sure why I’m telling you this. It’s very personal to me. I know many of you are deeply Christian, and you’ve held onto your faith for a long time. Your faith is developed, it is old… mine is not. It is young, it is confused… it is curious.

I have faith… but faith is a weird concept for me. I think like an engineer. I like science. The miracles are hard for me to accept without evidence I can test or see with my own eyes.

I was a fan of Richard Dawkins, Christopher Hitchens and Sam Harris… three of the “Four Horsemen” of the new atheism, as they were called.

So believe me when I say... I didn't expect to end up here. The young version of me would be embarrassed to see me now. He would’ve told you, “If anyone ever tells you I found God on my deathbed... they’re lying.”

I thought I’d be an atheist for life… taking it right into my grave.

And now here I am, praying to God every single day. Strange, isn’t it?

My mantra has become the Jesus Prayer. It is my rock. The thing I lean on when I feel lost.

“Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me… a sinner.”

I probably say this, at minimum, a dozen times a day. Usually more. Sometimes I'll just stand there and say it like 30 times in a row. If a stranger stumbles upon me in those moments, they’ll probably think I’m nuts.

And you know what happens when I say it? I start seeing my flaws clearly. My memory fires up like a hard drive reading files from a folder I forgot even existed.

Maybe I raised my voice to someone who didn’t deserve it, maybe I was being a little manipulative with my sister when we argued… maybe I didn’t show enough gratitude when someone did something kind for me… maybe I can do a lot better.

It never fails. I say that prayer and the things I need to work on start sticking out in my mind like a sore thumb. I can’t avoid them anymore, and the work begins.

It has helped me heal many relationships in my life. My relationship with my parents, in particular, has never been stronger. For most of my adult life, my Dad and I would fight often… over the stupidest things. But now, it's healed… we've never gotten along better, and I can’t express to you with words how much I love that man.

I’m proud of him.

I don't know what all this means. I don’t understand my faith… maybe I'm not meant to... but I know that I'm going to keep praying. I'm going to keep inviting God into my life.

And honestly… this entire thing we’re doing here… me writing… you reading. I don’t think it would’ve happened without prayer. It guided me here.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. Seriously, nobody tell my niece.

subject: i almost didn't write this
preview: There's something you deserve to hear.
html:
I’ve been in a rut the last couple of days. I’m not even sure why. I sit down to write to you, and I’m just drawing blanks. I’m letting the worst news in my feed get to me… I get emotional, I get angry and I get a little sad… I’m feeling like prey.

Recently, a new patron wrote to me and said:

“You’re a brilliant writer, Clay. You’re one of the few brilliant writers I still read because you don’t steal my peace… you give me peace.”

It’s about the highest compliment I can receive. But yesterday, when I tried to write… I didn’t feel that peace. I felt the fires of hell consuming me. I was viewing everything in a negative light. You’ve probably been there before, haven’t you?

So I didn’t write. I didn’t want to drag you down with me. I didn’t want to take your peace away from you.

But if I’m being realistic… there’s something you must know.

We might lose.

And I mean more than the midterms. I mean the whole game… the big one. Most people on our side won't say that out loud.

I think you deserve to hear it.

We're up against something very serious, and very old. They run the schools, the newsrooms, the universities and HR. Even the platforms I use to talk to you are ultimately regulated by them.

Just yesterday, my Thomas Sowell page had its reach limited over a ‘fact check’ on one phrase in a meme. Ten years of work, punished over something trivial.

They have every advantage in every fight.

Sure, we can win an election here or there… but they win everything else. The truth is, I'm not sure our side has the heart to do what needs to be done to win… and even if we did, I'm not sure we have the power.

Progressives understand the game better than we do. For us, power is an intellectual exercise. An argument. For them, it’s a thirst… an addiction. It’s the purpose of life itself.

We can win all of the arguments. I’ve shown you how… receipts and all. And none of it matters to them.

Arguments don't decide who runs the schools. They don’t decide whether Charlie Kirk gets to live or die. You could probably destroy Tyler Robinson in an argument about any of the issues he believes in… and yet…

It’s pretty bleak, isn’t it? What’s the point? Where’s the peace that my patron thanked me for?

Well, for me, the peace is in knowing that what we’re doing is right. That we are in pursuit of the good, the true and the beautiful. We want order, we want a high trust society… and we want peace. Whether we will get it is another question, but we don’t have the option to stop fighting for it, do we?

I suppose we do… but where is the honor in that?

In AD 79, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii in ash. The whole city ran for its life. Thousands never made it out.

Legend says one Roman soldier didn't run. He was standing guard at the city gate, and nobody came to relieve him… so he stayed at his post until the ash consumed him.

Maybe that's foolish. But nobody tells stories about the men who left their posts. Everyone remembers the one who stayed.

Why? Because it’s honorable. Because in the face of doom, you still have a duty to stand your ground.

So vote. Bring someone with you. And whatever happens on November 3rd, I don't want to hear any 'woe is me.' I don't want to hear despair. Stand at your post. Keep your head high.

Charlie stood at his post until he was consumed. That’s what I’m going to do too. That’s what these emails are all about.

Bear your cross, and do your duty.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: divorce your wife
preview: In 82 BC, the dictator of Rome ordered an 18-year-old to divorce his wife.
html:
In 82 BC, the dictator of Rome ordered an 18-year-old to divorce his wife. Her father was on the wrong side of a civil war… the losing side.

He refused. Said no to the most powerful and dangerous man in Rome, a man who could have his head displayed in the Forum on command.

He lost everything and went into hiding, sick with a fever, sleeping somewhere new almost every night. Powerless.

His name was Julius Caesar.

His family begged for his life, and the dictator, a man named Sulla, finally gave in. But he warned them the boy would be the ruin of them.

Sulla was right. That boy grew up to end the Roman Republic.

Caesar got lucky. Thousands of others didn't.

Sulla posted lists of names in the Forum. If your name was on it, anyone could kill you and collect a reward by bringing your head to the dictator. Your property was sold off... your sons were banned from public office for life, and your family was left destitute.

The point was to scare anyone from ever choosing the wrong side again.

Of course, a United States senator is not a Roman dictator. She doesn't want heads. She only wants prosecutions.

Progress.

“I want to look at these signature cases and not just focus on the president, but on the people who enabled him.

I want young people coming out of school to say, should I go work for the Trump administration? Like, that sounds fun. I might get an opportunity. I want them to be like, Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want. And so let me avoid participating in that. I want that deterrence message.”

That's Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, a former CIA analyst and one of the Democrats' "moderates," speaking at the University of Chicago.

She didn't shout it. She didn't slam her hand on a desk like an angry dictator… She said it calmly, sitting in a leather chair… like a school teacher giving a lesson.

Sulla wanted to scare anyone from ever choosing the wrong side again. She wants a "deterrence message.” She's not asking for any heads to be cut off… she's just asking for their careers instead. And their freedom.

She's not bluffing, either. Peter Navarro and Steve Bannon both went to federal prison in 2024. Three lawyers who fought for Trump in 2020 were charged in Georgia and pleaded guilty. Douglass Mackey was prosecuted for posting a joke meme. I won’t even get into the J6 grandmas. Trump himself was prosecuted repeatedly as he was running for President.

They couldn't legally take a President's head… so they took his mug shot.

She says "signature cases." But according to a memo from the chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, Jack Smith's team had already collected data on 639,000 Republicans... including, reportedly, the home addresses of people who bought a red hat.

I wonder how many of you are on that list…

What do you think he wanted to do with all that data? Should we give him the benefit of the doubt?

Sulla posted his list on a wall in the Forum. Today, it's an Excel spreadsheet.

So what's the right doing about it? What they do best. Strongly worded letters. And tweets.

Senator Mike Lee, a member of the majority party, tweeted: "Today's Democrats embrace fascistic tactics."

I know calling them fascists feels good. But "fascist" is their word, not yours. Ask any professor in America who the real fascists are... it won't be Slotkin and Jack Smith.

Words don't scare Slotkin. Her side decides who the fascists are... and who gets prosecuted. To them, Charlie Kirk was a fascist. Progressivism is about health care and human rights.

And remember where she said all this... at a university, in front of the next generation of leaders.

Slotkin isn't breaking the rules. She's telling you what they are.

Sulla's lists weren't illegal. He made sure of that. When you hold power, you don't break the rules. You write them.

But winning an election isn't the same as holding power. Republicans hold the White House and both houses of Congress right now... and a Democratic senator still talks like she's the one in charge.

This isn't what your public school taught you about how power works. I know. It's unsettling.

Right now, the one writing the rules is the flock I wrote about in "The Desecration of Charlie Kirk"... the thing that rules America and answers to nobody in it. Slotkin represents the flock. Those kids she’s talking to are being trained to be the next generation of it…

And you, dear reader... probably know a young man about the age Caesar was when Sulla came for him. That’s who her message is for.

She wants him saying, "Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems." She wants him so afraid of being associated with you that he walks away.

That's exactly what Sulla demanded of Caesar. Divorce your wife. Walk away from the losing side.

Caesar said no.

Nobody remembers Sulla. Everyone remembers Caesar.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: i'm stupid
preview: ...at least, i am when i get mad
html:
I can be an absolute moron sometimes.

I've broken video game controllers and computer mice by getting so mad when I lose. I’m not proud of it, and I haven’t done it in a while… but I’m not going to lie to you about it. I have it in me.

There's a game my friends and I play online together called Escape from Tarkov. We all live far apart now, and it's how we stay in touch. It gives us a reason to talk without just having to call each other.

It's a very intense military shooter where there's a lot at stake. There are no respawns. When you're dead you're dead and it's over. And not just that, you lose resources that you worked to earn over time. And the guy who killed you gets to take them from you… if he survives.

The thought of losing what I've earned to somebody who outplayed me is so infuriating that it makes me angry… and anger makes me stupid. So I break my own mouse and hurt nobody but myself.

And I bet you've felt it too.

When someone says something designed to get under your skin, that's them playing a game with you. They're trying to make you do something stupid.

That's exactly what Bob wrote to me about this morning. I've told you about Bob before. One of my founding patrons… he's quite a character.

His emails show up in my inbox as 'Bob Master of the Universe' and when he talks about his age, he doesn't say a number. He tells me: "I'm at the end of my toilet paper roll."

Most of his emails are like that. But every once in a while, he drops a truth bomb in between the humor that knocks me off my feet.

Here's what he wrote:

"Grace and kindness gives superior intelligence. Why? Because the minute you get mad you get stupid at the same time. People make the stupidest decisions when they are mad."

I have several dead computer mice to prove Bob right. But Bob’s not really talking about video games. He’s talking about the fight we’re in, the one that got Tyler Robinson to do the stupidest thing he could have done. He threw his entire life away to silence a man who pissed him off.

When's the last time you read a comment online, fought with a relative, or watched a video and felt nothing but pure rage? Be honest.

That rage is the hook. It's the devil's temptation. As I wrote on Thursday, it's exactly what the Lord's Prayer asks God to protect us from.

"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."

I've built Facebook pages with hundreds of thousands of followers. I know what makes people tick. And nothing works better than rage bait.

Every media company knows it. Every politician knows it. They're not trying to inform you. They're trying to make you stupid… so that you do something stupid and they can use it against you.

That's why grace isn't a weakness. It’s intelligence. Superior intelligence, as Bob put it.

So the next time you feel that rage, and your instinct is telling you to respond in that moment… say the Lord's Prayer. Even if you're an atheist. Try it.

It takes about twenty seconds. By the time you finish, the hook is gone… you can think again.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. If you've ever broken something or done something you deeply regret in a fit of rage, reply and confess. I know I'm not the only one.

subject: hasan piker designed it
preview: a car flew over a semi truck last night
html:
Last night around 9:30, I watched a car fly over a semi truck. It felt like science fiction… but it was very real. What a privilege it is to be alive right now, to witness such a miracle of science and engineering.

Star Trek gave Captain Kirk a flip phone that could only make calls. Your phone does more than his communicator ever could.

The device you're reading this on right now has millions of times more computing power than the computer that landed men on the moon.

And we all just go about our days, taking all of this for granted.

Some people do worse than take it for granted… They seethe with envy and resentment.

Hasan Piker… remember that name? I've written about him a little bit before. He's one of the biggest streamers on Twitch, and politicians like AOC and Ilhan Omar have come on his stream to play video games with him. Millions of young people take their politics from him.

He's an open Marxist, and he goes around giving speeches and interviews wearing a Mao Zedong costume. Theater kid politics.

The moment I saw that car fly, I remembered something Hasan once said about the man who built it:

“The problem with Elon Musk is that he doesn’t know anything. Like he literally doesn’t know anything. He doesn’t know how to f***ing run a company either. It’s crazy.”
~ Hasan Piker

So I shared the video of the flying car with his quote on top. Not a word of my own.

As of writing this, it's had over 1.6k likes and been seen by over 22,000 people.

Small potatoes compared to the type of reach I get on my Thomas Sowell page, but the biggest I've ever had on Twitter/X so far.

Then the experts arrived. The anointed ones, as Sowell would say. The ones who come to tell me that Elon didn’t build anything.

His engineers did. Here are my two favorites:

One asked me:

"you think Elon personally designed this?"

I said:

"no, i think hasan designed it."

Of course Elon didn’t design it himself. Neither did Henry Ford with the Model T.

Another told me:

"Walking into a room of engineers and saying 'get on it!' isn't knowing anything"

I said:

"try it. walk into a room of engineers, say 'get on it,' and let me know how it goes."

See what I did?

You don't argue with people who came to dunk on you. That puts you in their frame.

You make a joke of it. Perform for the audience. They're the prize. The opponent is the specimen.

My replies got 86 and 70 likes. Theirs got zero.

I believe this is what the kids call a brutal ratio.

So go watch that car fly. Be grateful you're alive to see it. Generations of people dreamed about this day and died waiting.

Some people will spend today seething about it.

Envy looks at a flying car and sees an insult. Gratitude sees a miracle. Choose gratitude.

stay close,
~ Clay

The prayer wall I built for Mike Sullivan raised $232 overnight. Donations are still coming in, each one attached to a prayer for Mike… a man who came to spit on Charlie Kirk's grave.

One of my haters said that proves I'm a grifter... "following in the footsteps of your favorite Nazi grifter."

Just like Charlie.

If the same men who spit on a murdered father's grave on his birthday are spitting on me, I must be doing something right.

I don't let their hate get to me. I let it fuel me… and my work.

Here's what it fuels. Trish, one of my founding patrons, hosts the Guild for my patrons and runs our Question of the Week. She wrote to me there this morning:

“Clay, I owe you thanks. Between learning principles re: successful exchange and articulating my positions safely here, I am growing intellectually.”

That's what the money buys. Yes, it helps pay my bills. That's what gives me the power to spend my days doing this, instead of squeezing it into my evenings after a day of other work.

So call me a grifter. I'll keep turning grave-spitters into fuel for people like Trish.

This is the whole point of my project. I love conservatives. I love libertarians. But if I'm being honest, a lot of you fall into their traps. I see it every day in my comment section. I was the same way for years.

But then I found a better way… something that works. Grace.

I realized that the anger I felt when I read their comments was the temptation. That's exactly what the Lord's Prayer tries to protect us from. We all know how to say it, or at least most of us do, but how many of us actually take it seriously in our day-to-day lives?

"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."

The temptation isn't the hate they throw at us. It's the hate it stirs up in us. They are trying to drag you into hell with them.

Don't let them. Pray for them instead. It sharpens your sword, and it's what keeps you from becoming like them.

It's the one thing they can't use against you, and the one thing they'll never do for us. That's what makes us different. That's how we know we're on the side of the good, the true, and the beautiful.

subject: mike
preview: he came to charlie's birthday to spit on his grave
html:
Do you know what today is?

Today would have been Charlie Kirk's 33rd birthday. He was murdered just before his 32nd. And on his 31st birthday, his last one on this earth, this is what he said he wanted you to do:

"Yes, for all of you emailing and texting, today is my birthday. Thank you for all of the kind notes.

All I want for my birthday is for YOU to go vote, and to bring a friend or family member with you.

VOTE!!"

The midterms are three weeks away. Charlie can't ask anymore, so I'll ask for him: go vote, and bring someone with you.

And since I'm Canadian and can't vote myself, I'm doing my part. I spent nearly twenty years as a libertarian, and now I'm using that to win them over to vote Republican. I like to think Charlie would approve.

But not everyone came to honour Charlie today. On my Thomas Sowell quotes page, I posted a tribute to Charlie, for my readers to come mourn and pray with me on his birthday.

Then a man named Mike Sullivan showed up. Here's what he wrote:

“He was a racist, misogynist, and a grifter. Awful he was shot. It was also awful that he claimed that gun deaths were worth it to preserve the 2nd amendment. Surely you all agree, right? Are you celebrating?”

Mike is a regular on my page. I don't block him because I love my haters and I pray for them and they teach me lessons.

So I answered him. Here’s what I wrote:

Mike... welcome back. Today would have been Charlie's 33rd birthday, and this is what you came to say.

You’ve really made a habit out of this haven’t you? How many times have we been through this now, Mike? Seems like every time we publicly mourn Charlie on my page, you show up to spit on his grave.

And what’s worse, is that you’re not even living in reality. That quote you just gave… you didn't even bother to look up what Charlie actually said, did you?

Or maybe you did, and you’re just lying about a murdered father on his birthday.

Which is it?

Don’t answer, it doesn’t matter to me. That’s for your conscience to figure out.

Let me give everyone the part you cut, where he compares it to driving:

“Fifty thousand people die on the road every year. That’s a price... we have decided that the benefit of driving, speed, accessibility, mobility, is worth the cost of 50,000 people dying on the road.”

You know what's funny, Mike? You're not even original. These aren’t even your thoughts. You've been handed a script, and you're reading it back.

So now, the question is why? Why do you do this, Mike? I know you’re not a bot, and yet you run the same scripts as the bots that come to my page.

I looked at your profile. You seem like a good man, Mike. You love your family. You love old music. You notice the little things in life.

You're a father, Mike. So was Charlie.

Somebody convinced a good man that this murdered father is worthy of contempt, and the best reason you could bring was a cropped quote. The same one every bot brings.

That's what should worry all of us.

But you know what Mike? I don’t hate you, and neither would Charlie. You know what he would do? He’d pray for you.

And if it were your family grieving today, he'd be praying for them too.

But that’s not what you do, is it, Mike? You came to his birthday to call him a racist and a grifter, in front of all of us who mourn him. You are pissing on his grave. You do it repeatedly. I expect you to do it again in the future.

But you’re not a bot, I know you’re not a bot… you just behave like one whenever Charlie comes up on your feed.

And so, in the spirit of Charlie’s birthday, I’m going to do something I think he would have approved of. I’m going to turn you into money to fund my work. You are going to be an example that lives on my website forever.

My readers are going to leave you notes on a wall built just for you. Every one comes with a few dollars to keep this work going, and every one will be written with the grace Charlie would have shown you.

I know that you’ll never pray for us. If I were to meet the same fate as Charlie, I’d fully expect you to run the same script on me and piss on my grave. That’s okay.

I’ll pray for you anyway.

Here’s your wall, Mike: stopbeingprey.com/walls/prayers-for-mike-sullivan

Thank you for funding my work, and teaching my readers an important lesson.

God bless you,

~ Clay

Back in April, after another man spat on Charlie's memory, I wrote you a line that's become the heart of this whole project:

We pray for our prey.

They don't pray for us. They never will. That's the difference between us and them.

So today, let's pray for Mike. I’m going to make sure he sees it.

stopbeingprey.com/walls/prayers-for-mike-sullivan

Every prayer you leave him funds this work, and he gets to read every single one.

stay close,

subject: i can't stop

Last night I told you I was going to write about my fights with libertarians. Then RJ Mitte died, and I couldn't.

Today, I spent most of my day "fighting" with them. I created my very first Twitter/X thread, and it made a little noise. Got quite a bit of attention from libertarians across the spectrum. Want to see it? Here you go.

Some of them are quite nasty to me. They come into my thread, insult me and then hit me with a block before I can reply. How rude!

And yet… I can't stop replying to my dear libertarians. I love them so. They are all so sincere, they've put a lot of thought into this stuff… and I'm raining on their parade.

I know that parade well. I marched in it for nearly twenty years.

It's a very strange thing… I almost feel like I'm arguing with my former self. What happened to Charlie Kirk changed how I see everything. It apparently did not have the same effect on them.

But I think I'm winning some of them over. A few have told me so directly… but many more are reading silently. Those are the people I'm really talking to.

Rule #2 of my doctrine… The audience is the prize. The opponent is the demonstration.

Later on in the evening… just an hour before I wrote this… I posted this to my feed:

Question for Libertarians:
What do you think the progressives want you to do this November?
Stay home or vote R?

One of them replied. Calls himself the Anarcho Family Man. I kind of respect it. I always respect a good family man.

But what I don’t respect is the posture of his answer.

He said:

Libertarians should spend zero time thinking about what some group or other wants them to do.

I said:

The gazelle spends zero time thinking about what the lion wants, too.

A family man, of all people, should know better. You lock your door at night because you've thought about what someone else wants.

Refusing to think about what your enemy wants isn't independent thinking… it's prey thinking.

Sun Tzu knew this 2,500 years ago:

"If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles."

subject: i changed my mind
preview: a dying murderer's last words showed me why.
html:
Last Wednesday night in Huntsville, Texas, a man strapped to a gurney apologized to a family watching him through a window.

He was about to be executed for killing a convenience store clerk named Vickie Swartout during a robbery in Silsbee, Texas, in 2000. The family on the other side of the glass was hers.

He was asked if he had any last words.

This is what he chose:

Yes sir, so I apologize Swartout family for my cause the death of your loved one, and I wish you had closure and peace for the rest you know that you can live the rest of your life with. I wish that you accept my apology, and I wish for your forgiveness. I’m sorry for what happened, I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days. I wish you had closure and your heart and I am just sorry you know so shout out to y’all.

To my family Sheanna, thanks for holding me down, Jerry Jr., Treci, my dad, Tirurus and thank you and I love you too. Thank you, Ms. Natalie, for helping me come out of my darkness, the deepest times in my life. I love y’all. Jeff, you came a long way, so shout out to you, without you I wouldn’t probably be in a good state of mind to find peace and the lord, so I thank y’all.

Hey enjoy life, and peace to y’all. Warden, that’s it, I’m ready Warden.

Nineteen minutes later, he was dead. His name was Jamaal Howard.

I don’t know if he meant it. My gut tells me he did… what does yours tell you?

The truth is only between God and Jamaal now.

Here’s what I can’t help but wonder after reading that… Would he have found those words in a cell, with forty more years ahead of him? Maybe. But facing death, with nothing left to gain, is when he found them. And that’s what makes my gut think it’s sincere.

There was no earthly benefit for him to say such things.

I used to be against the death penalty. As a libertarian the idea of state-sanctioned executions really rubbed me the wrong way.

Libertarians understand that The State is inherently violent. It is, quite literally, the Monopoly on Violence.

I didn't trust the state to get it right. Granting them the power over life and death just felt wrong. Especially when I'm acutely aware of just how corrupt it is.

If the State gets it wrong, and kills an innocent person… that makes all of us complicit in a murder.

This is what I believed for years… and I still do, to some extent… but over the last couple of years, my thinking has started to change.

I watched Charlie Kirk get executed publicly... not legally. Assassination is the word. But it's fundamentally the same thing. I've seen countless videos of war and murder… The real kind that keeps you up at night and makes you feel sick. I don’t recommend it.

But I’m glad I watched, because it taught me something important about the world.

Most people have never really looked at violence. Maybe they've scrolled past a clip... flinched... and kept scrolling. They've never let it sink in. They don’t spend a whole weekend watching bodycam footage of trench warfare from the Ukrainian/Russian war.

I’ve had nightmares about some of the things I’ve seen in that footage.

The news talks about wars, but never shows you what it really looks like. The movies give you a cartoon version that can feel real… but as soon as you see the real thing, you realize how fake the movies are.

War is just politics with the mask off. Every law, even something as innocent sounding as a "minimum wage," sits on the same chain... a fine, then a cop, then a gun.

Once you've seen what's at the end of that chain, you can't unsee it.

We've been pacified into not seeing it. We’re told that it’s about ‘public service’ and the ‘greater good’ and all of these nice sounding euphemisms.

No, that’s not the truth. Violence is the heart and soul of all politics.

Even our executions are hidden… as though the killers deserve privacy.

A needle, in a back room, like a medical procedure for your sick dog… most people never think about it at all.

Jamaal didn't apologize to an empty room. Vickie's family was on the other side of that glass.

That's why I think executions should be public. If we're going to have the death penalty, then we're all part of it. Not encouraged... but available, like bodycam footage, for anyone who chooses to look.

And it might finally happen. Trump just approved a firing squad for the Fort Hood shooter, who murdered 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009. The Pentagon says it'll be livestreamed.

Trump was asked if he approved. "Absolutely."

I'm not saying we should execute every murderer. If there's any reasonable doubt that someone might be innocent, we can't do it. That's a hard standard to live up to... but it's the only one I can accept.

But if there’s no doubt, then the question isn’t whether they deserve it. It’s whether we have the stomach to do it.

And is the other option really any more kind? Any less barbaric? A cage until you die of old age is still a death sentence. It just takes longer, and nobody has to look.

Send them back to God, they don’t belong here.

One of my founding patrons, Trish, wrote the case against the death penalty in the Guild this week. Funny enough, she flipped on it too... just in the opposite direction. She wrote:

"I had to acknowledge then and now that the impulse to support capital punishment was more vengeful than it was practical."

I used to agree with her. I still think she has a point… for some people, it is about revenge as much as it is about justice. That’s the temptation… it’s easy to feel a strong desire for revenge when you witness such a wicked act.

For me, it’s just about justice. I have no hate in my heart for these people, I just believe they made a choice that sacrificed their own right to life. I've made my peace with that.

Where do you land on this? Hit reply and tell me, especially if you disagree.

And if you're a patron… Trish's thread is open in the Guild. Go hash it out with her, me and the other members on the inside.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: maybe i'm in a cult
preview: that's what my haters say. you tell me.
html:
Donald Trump has declared a new enemy. It's not a country, it's not a politician... it's anyone who uses the term "artificial intelligence."

I’m not joking. He really said this.

"The White House considers anyone that uses the term, "Artificial Intelligence," as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, "Super Intelligence," THE ENEMY!"
~ President Donald J. Trump

Seems a little unhinged, right? What’s going on here? Is the man just firing from the hip? Winging it… like usual.

or…

Is he playing a game that most of us can’t see yet?

A lot of my favorite commentators on the right think it’s the former. They think Trump is being stupid and petty.

Matt Walsh, who I love, called it one of the dumbest things imaginable to be focused on before the midterms. He’s far from alone.

Some even said Trump is acting like a leftist… Forcing everyone to use his preferred words. His pronouns.

And guess who else hated it? MSNBC. Their legal analyst Joyce Vance asked why nobody in Trump's own party will "do something about it."

I get the reaction. But I think they’re missing something…

Remember "fake news"? Do you remember how that term started spreading? Back in 2016, it was aimed at Trump and his supporters. We were the ones spreading fake news, according to the narrative.

Hillary Clinton gave a whole speech about the "epidemic" of fake news a month after she lost. Of course, she didn’t lose fair and square… she lost because us deplorables were tricked by fake news.

Two days later, Trump tweeted it right back at CNN: "FAKE NEWS!"

A month after that, at his first press conference as President-elect, CNN's Jim Acosta tried to ask him a question. The night before, CNN had pushed the Russia dossier story... the one that was never verified and later fell apart in front of all of us.

Trump wouldn't let him speak.

"Not you. Your organization is terrible... You are fake news."

And just like that... CNN was staring down the barrel of a weapon of their own making. Trump took it, made it his own… and the rest is history. Fake News is our term now.

Trump is a branding expert. That's his whole business. For decades, people paid him just to put his name on their buildings.

Maybe he isn't firing from the hip. Maybe there's a plan. Maybe the man who survived two impeachments, four indictments and a bullet, then took the White House back in the greatest comeback in American presidential history, knows a thing or two about words.

But sure... maybe the podcasters know better.

Look at what he posted the same day:

"The Fake and Artificial News is out there trying to say that I'm inviting the enemy to bomb San Diego and Los Angeles... these people are Degenerates, and think they can continuously get away with Fake News!"

Do you see what he’s doing?

The fake AND artificial news.

He's welding the two words together. Fake... artificial. Artificial... fake. They’re synonyms… it works.

Every time you hear "artificial" now, a little part of your brain hears "fake."

So, he is beginning to brand "artificial intelligence" as a cheap knockoff.

But "super intelligence"? That sounds like something you'd want your country to have first… before China or Russia figure it out, right? That’s the real product he’s selling.

Now look at who's sitting on the other side of this debate.

The left is going all in on limiting this technology. Obama is telling Democrats to put AI regulation at the center of their agenda. Is that someone you want on your team? Bernie Sanders wants to ban "artificial superintelligence" outright, and is suggesting prison time for anyone building it… that’s a real thing.

One side wants to pause it. The other wants to wield it to cure cancer, beat the diseases of old age, take us to the stars and make America the world superpower for centuries to come. The new Rome.

"Artificial" is their word. It's the scary word. It’s the one that makes people think about a Terminator coming to execute your family. Trump is taking it away from them.

So when Matt Walsh and MSNBC (sorry, "MS NOW") are rolling their eyes at the same thing, somebody's missing something.

And you know what I don't think you should do four weeks before the midterms? Mock your own leader in front of millions of followers. Do you think that drives people to the polls?

Trump fires from the hip. He's just a really good shot... and he's aiming more often than we realize.

Maybe I’m just a cult member… a sycophant. That’s what my haters say.

What do you think?

I spent the last day being called all these things, and more, on Twitter/X. I was getting some reps in, arguing with people, putting what I teach to work.

But now? It's fun for me. I feel like Muhammad Ali doing the rope-a-dope. Lean back, let them swing, and wait for them to punch themselves out.

"I know you will, Duke, and yet I'll pray for the salvation of your soul anyway.

God bless you. I hope your day is full of joy and love, just like mine is."

Duke was the nastiest of them all. The most unwilling to have a conversation with me. But others actually talked to me. And some of them came around.

"You semi like pretty articulated, intelligent guy yourself." ~ Pili, who called me a clown earlier

Many of my actual friends are libs. I do not hate these people. Most of them are just being perpetually gaslit by the very system you and I seek to expose.

None of this is a gift. I wasn’t born with this ability… quite the opposite.

subject: i was never a real libertarian
preview: at least, that's what they're telling me now
html:
A few libertarians in my comments told me I was "never a real libertarian."

They're not arguing with me. They're revoking my membership card.

When people in my real life find out I've become a political writer, they always want to know what perspective I'm coming from.

Over the years, I've described myself as a libertarian, a conservative, a classical liberal, an Anarcho-Capitalist, an Anarchist and a Minarchist.

I'm not sure any of these were ever accurate summations of my beliefs. The truth is, they were labels I adopted to be accepted by a group. I was looking for some kind of belonging, not the truth.

But now? I don't care about the social clubs. This isn't a hobby for me anymore.

So what am I? How do I describe myself?

To put it simply, I try not to. I do occasionally refer to myself as right-wing but that's as close as I'll get.

Although... I'll be honest. I've called myself a "Trump loyalist" more than once recently. That's probably just another label. Another club… and it's an odd one for a Canadian to be in, isn't it?

Here's the trouble I have with all of these labels… they box me in. They create a perception and a prejudice towards my perspective, before I even express it. They make me easy to dismiss, or worse… easy to herd. Prey.

When I was a libertarian, I believed all the libertarian things… before I even understood them, or the strongest arguments against them. I felt some kind of duty to defend the viewpoint. Likewise with any of the other labels.

I wasn't a mindless drone just accepting the party line, but I was directionally compelled to be in line with the general view.

That's one reason you don't see me attach a label to myself anymore. It unshackles my brain, gets it out of the box so it can think more clearly.

That's the function of labels. They are categories for in-group and out-group preferences.

So, to my libertarian friends revoking my card... fine. Take it. I don't want that thing anywhere near me. I don't want to be part of your club… I just want to win. I just don't want the rules written by people who hate me and everyone I care about.

I don't want people who are happy Charlie's dead to be wielding any power over us at all.

Put whatever label on that you want. I know what I am now.

What are you?

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I won't put a label on you. Just your name... in the front of my book when it comes out (it’ll be a bit). A permanent record of who stood with this work when it counted.

subject: i miss scott
preview: especially on days like today
html:
On days like today, I miss Scott Adams more than ever.

If you've found my work to be persuasive, then understand that's the Scott Adams influence. I am constantly referencing his book “Win Bigly” when I write.

So, why am I thinking about Scott today? Well… do you remember the Fine People Hoax? Of course you do, how could you forget?

Nobody, and I mean nobody, fought against that lie harder than Scott did. He’s even the one who popularized the term "Fine People Hoax" and kept coming back to it, for years, on his daily livestream, Coffee with Scott Adams.

The Simultaneous Sip.

Why am I bringing this up? Because yesterday, it happened again. A new hoax has emerged just in time for the midterms.

Have you heard?

The LA Times: "Trump suggests letting Iran 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego"

Gavin Newsom: "just invited Iran to take out Los Angeles and San Diego"

Jim Acosta: "Trump fantasizes about LA and San Diego being wiped out by a nuclear attack"

Oh no, how awful! Why would Trump say this?

It's everywhere today. The newspapers, the activists, the mayors, the governor of California. Everyone's picking up this ball and running with it.

And they're all saying the same thing:

“There were very fine people on both sides”...no wait... that was the other one. Sorry... Trump wants Iran to nuke Los Angeles and San Diego.

So, is it true?

Well, he really did say "Let them take out Los Angeles." Just as he really did say there were “very fine people on both sides”.

Yesterday, he was at a rally in Nebraska, talking about how the war with Iran has pushed up gas and diesel prices. He'd signed an order on diesel at that same rally. Then he said this:

"And again, remember, with the war, it's just artificial. It's a little bit high. It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon."

~ President Trump, Grand Island, Nebraska, October 5, 2026

What's "a little bit high"? Your gas. That's the price he’s talking about. Not the cities.

And the corporate media knows this. Many of them even mention it in their articles... just never in the headline. Just like the Fine People Hoax.

They include the truth in the article, knowing full well most people only see the headline.

And now, every progressive commentator is pushing it, and their audiences are eating up the lie.

Do you see the trick?

They’re being factual, but not truthful, as Michael Malice likes to say.

What they’re saying is a fact. They are quoting Trump accurately. The deception is in the omission. What they leave out.

And the sad thing is, this stuff works. It’s effective. It could even be the catalyst that wins them the midterms… and they know it. Why do you think they’re running so hard with it?

Scott isn't here to fight this one anymore. So we'll have to do it for him.

He named the last one the “Fine People Hoax.” What do you think we should call this one? Reply and tell me.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. When newspapers dropped Dilbert, Scott kept going because his audience paid for it directly. That's how this works too. I'm following the Scott Adams model.

subject: i made a mistake
preview: and thousands of people saw it
html:
I posted a Sowell quote today on my Sowell page. A popular quote, about Obama.

“One of the reasons it has taken so long for some people to finally see through Barack Obama is that people do not like to admit, even to themselves, that they have been played for fools by a slick-talking politician.”

~ Thomas Sowell, Random Thoughts (2001)

Do you see the error? I didn’t. I created an image meme out of it, shared it on my page and now it’s been seen by thousands of people.

Other people caught it. As one reader wrote:

2001? He wasn't even in National politics yet. He gave the keynote speech at the DNC in 2004

Busted!

The problem was, the software that I built to manage my quote database had a bug in it. I won’t bore you with the technical details, but the source ended up getting tagged as 2001, when it was really from a column in 2013. And I didn’t catch it.

Funny thing about that quote. It's about people who can't admit they got it wrong. And I got it wrong… so here I am admitting it.

It stings a little. When you get something wrong in front of a large audience. Especially when you’ve built your entire reputation on getting it right. ReadSowell.com is all about properly sourcing Sowell, linking every quote back to its source.

And so, that’s one of my rules that I wanted to tell you about.

Never be wrong. And when you are, own it the moment you find out.

This is easy to do on something as simple as the date on a source. It's much more difficult when you were wrong about something you believed in. A cause, a hero... a politician you voted for.

But you have to do it. Owning it buys you trust. People respect it. What they don't respect is someone who gets angry, or shifts the blame when he's caught.

I just wanted to get that off my chest.

When's the last time you admitted you got something wrong?

stay close,

~ Clay

Like most people who read me, you probably found me through my Thomas Sowell Quotes page… one of my passion projects for over 10 years, which has somehow evolved into this strange and amazing new life as a full-time writer. Thanks to you.

Well, that's not the only page I've built over the years… far from it. If you read "The Thomas Massie Problem," you might remember me mentioning that I built one of Dave Smith's first fan pages.

That’s true. And you know what? I still have it. 7.2k followers.

It’s a tiny sliver of Dave’s audience… but I can speak to them now. I just realized. And these are the OGs so to speak. His early supporters.

I posted a poll on it today, to see if it’s still active.

Be honest. What's your current opinion on Dave Smith?

It got quite a few responses. They’re still coming in.

It’s a mixed bag. Some people still love him.

"Dead to me for endorsing Trump." ~ Mike

And then there are others who are just bored of him carrying on about all the same libertarian theories like a broken record.

"Stopped listening to him years ago. If you've heard one take you've heard them all." ~ Frank

I was reading all this, kind of surprised the page was still active. I didn’t expect to hear anything. People are still dropping in comments as I write this, and will probably continue over the next day or two.

So, I thought maybe I’d write to them… kind of like how I write to you. From the heart.

And so, I came up with this draft. I haven’t posted it. I’m not sure if I will. I’m thinking about it.

I built this page years ago, as one of Dave's first fans.

I still love Dave. I think he's funny, I miss his Luis impression on LOS, and I wish him and his family nothing but the best.

Dave is a good dude. He's taught me a lot and given me countless hours of entertainment.

He even gave me a shoutout on his show for this page, years ago. I'd managed to get hundreds of thousands of views on the promotional clips for his first special, and Luis called me and talked to me for about an hour.

It was an awesome experience. Both of those guys were nothing but cool to me.

Which is why it hurts to say that I can't listen to Dave anymore. I find it painful. Cringe... even.

These days, it feels like he'd rather be right than win. He'd rather fight his own side than work with it... effectively doing his part to hand the progressive coalition another win this November, and beyond.

And look, Dave fought for Ross for years. I'll never forget that. Which is what makes it so hard to watch him get the knives out for the coalition that actually got Ross out.

And I'll just say it... I'm tired of Dave's obsession with Israel. Anytime I click on a new video of his, there's something like an 80% chance it's about Israel. Any time he goes viral... it's Israel.

He had Saifedean on his podcast, the author of The Bitcoin Standard, and what did they talk about? Israel. He never had him back on to talk Bitcoin. The man literally wrote the book on it.

I'm not saying he can't talk about Israel and give his take... but of all the fights he could pick, he keeps picking the one that splits the right down the middle. He's relentless about it.

I mean... am I wrong? Is this what you guys signed up for?

I wrote about all of this in "The Prisoner and the Podcasters." It's about Ross, Dave, Clint Russell, and the choice libertarians have to make this November.

If you follow this page, you are an OG Dave Smith fan. Your opinion carries a lot of weight on this one. I want to hear it, even if I won't like it. Hit me in the comments when you're done reading.

preview: is it a bribe?
html:
Have you heard about Trump's $5,000 promise? If Republicans win the House and the Senate in November, he's going to give every adult citizen $5,000.

That's what he's saying.

Look, I'm not going to patronize you. I'm not going to come up with rationalizations to make it sound nicer than what it is. We're Sowell readers… we deal with harsh reality. We don't need the truth to be softened… right?

Okay, so here it is:

He's buying votes. Openly.

"...is creating more recipients of government handouts, at no cost to themselves, simply a strategy to gain more votes?"
~ Thomas Sowell, 2012

The libertarians are calling Trump a communist all over my feed right now.

And do they have a point? Let's be honest… yes, kind of.

Let me put it this way… it's not exactly free-market capitalism we're witnessing here, is it?

So, why should we support it? Why shouldn't we act like the libertarians and scream "SOCIALIST!!!" at everyone who wants the $5,000 payout?

I'm not saying you should support it. I'm not saying you shouldn't support it either... and I'm certainly not saying you should go around yelling "SOCIALIST!" at everyone... so… what the hell am I even saying?

This:

The progressives have been bribing voters for generations. They've captured entire classes with welfare programs.

Food stamps. Medicaid. Public housing. Teachers' unions. Public sector unions. The federal bureaucracy. Grant-funded NGOs. Student loan forgiveness... need I keep going?

Millions of people who depend on the government every month. Every election, they vote to keep it that way... and nobody calls that a bribe. They call it compassion. To oppose it is cruelty.

But to oppose Trump's $5,000? Well, that's principled. Courageous, even! Downright heroic, actually!

Look at all of our progressive friends talking like they're against political bribery. And look at how angry the libertarians are about Trump's $5,000 right now, compared to the entire welfare state that the progressives run on.

One dwarfs the other… and yet the $5,000 is the one they're screaming about.

What does that tell you?

Here's what it tells me. No one is being honest, and everyone wants to win... well, except for the libertarians.

Progressives aren't being honest about being against bribery. It's okay when they do it, but not when we do it. Our principled libertarian friends yelling about socialism? Who cares?… they're correct, and they're irrelevant.

Me? Whatever it takes to beat the coalition that celebrated Charlie Kirk's murder, this November.

That's where I stand. What about you?

stay close,

~ Clay

I think a lot about Dave Smith, host of the biggest libertarian podcast in the world. He doesn’t think about me at all. I’m not sure he even remembers who I am…

I DM’d with him a few months ago… very briefly. He told me he read my Hasan piece. I’m not sure I believe him. I’m not even convinced I was talking to him, it was probably an intern or something. He’s very famous now.

I've been thinking about joining his private supporters group. Dave does members-only shows where he takes questions live. I want to get in there and ask him about Ross, directly.

As I was deciding which membership tier to sign up for, I noticed a line at the top of his page.

“7,000+ members have trusted us with their media diet.”

7,000+ patrons… I have about 200…

I’m not going to lie to you. My first thought was pure envy. The guy is making several tens of thousands of dollars per month… minimum.

He’s making money like a rockstar. He is, in a sense, a rockstar. The rockstar of libertarianism.

And this isn’t even his only source of income. On every episode, he runs sponsors. Constant interruptions with ad reads.

I’m not against podcasters doing these things, but I am kind of against it when you’re making $50k+ per month from patrons… and your whole reputation has been built on talking about deadly serious issues.

When you're talking about war, where children are being slaughtered... or about a man being assassinated... and then you cut to an ad for a gambling app? Something is wrong.

I don’t think this is my envy talking. It’s my desire for a higher standard of discourse. When we’re talking about life and death stuff… let’s have a little decorum. Let’s be serious.

Let’s not just use it as an opportunity to sell underwear.

I think you have that same desire… that’s why you’re here. I know this for a fact, actually… because yesterday I asked you why you bother reading me at all…

One of you wrote:

"You are out here sending personal emails, not a political opinion piece or fishing for clicks for ad revenue."

Another:

"Your site provides a community, a desperately-needed assurance that I'm not alone, when the powerful media forces are constantly telling me that I am."

That's what this is. I'm just a writer. No ads, no sponsors… ever.

I built a community for people who like my work. There are other perks... but mostly, the point is to support the writing, and to be around people who think like you do.

I’m not a rockstar. I have no desire to be a rockstar… but I would like to make a decent living doing this. I’m not there yet, but I get closer every month thanks to the graciousness of a small portion of my readership.
