The summer of 2020 was a fun one, wasn't it?

Lockdowns everywhere. Funerals capped at ten. Churches getting fined for holding a service in a parking lot. Kids forced to go to school over Zoom.

In New York, the mayor sent police to break up a rabbi's funeral in April. In June, he spoke at George Floyd's memorial in Brooklyn... in front of thousands.

But if you were out "protesting racism", you got to play by different rules.

Twelve hundred public health experts signed a letter saying it out loud.

"This should not be confused with a permissive stance on all gatherings, particularly protests against stay-home orders. Those actions not only oppose public health interventions, but are also rooted in white nationalism and run contrary to respect for Black lives."

The progressives had their expert-endorsed revolution.

Facebook profiles went black. Entire sports teams took a knee. A street was renamed. A permanent memorial went up where he died. Every major corporation in America rewrote its policies... new rules about what you could say at work. Statues started being torn down.

And sure... a couple dozen people had to die, and some buildings had to burn... but that was a small price to pay for progress, wasn't it?

The experts agree! The TV people told me so. You're not going to disagree with the experts, are you?

Six summers later, the richest man in the world is disagreeing with those experts.

Today, he posted this on X:

Derek Chauvin was unjustly convicted of murder, therefore he should be freed.

The facts show that he was not the cause of death, nor did he at any time intend for a death to occur.

Whatever else he may be, he is not a murderer. That is the truth.

~ Elon Musk

I'm going to be upfront with you. I am unequivocally in favor of freeing Chauvin.

For six years and counting, the right has been right about that summer. Correct about the lockdowns. Correct about the riots. Correct about the experts... and what did you get out of it? What did the progressives get?

They got to win. We got to be right.

Nothing from that summer has ever been taken back. This would be the first.

Do you think it can actually be done?

subject: rod serling
preview: have you heard of him?
html:
Rod Serling... have you heard of him? Of course you have... how could you not? One of the greatest storytellers of all time!

I stumbled upon his daughter's Facebook page recently. She's made a habit of regularly posting quotes from her dad.

How great is that, just on its own? What better achievement could a writer have in life than his own kids posting his words proudly, long after he's gone? I can only hope to be so fortunate.

So anyway... There I was, just casually scrolling my feed, minding my own business, when she threw a quote at me that hit me like a brick to the face.

"It has forever been thus: So long as men write what they think, then all of the other freedoms- all of them- may remain intact. And it is then that writing becomes a weapon of truth, an article of faith, an act of courage." ~ Rod Serling

An argument asks you to agree. You can always refuse. A story makes you feel something, and you cannot take that back.

Good storytelling is the most powerful political weapon there is. Our side barely touches it. We write position papers, win the intellectual arguments, and lose the room. I've done it myself for years.

This is the losertarian story. The conservative story isn't much different. Sowell is a great writer, but he isn't a storyteller. He's no Rod Serling. Sowell explains how people behave. Serling puts you inside their souls for 25 minutes.

Great thinkers like Sowell gave me the ideas... but it was the great storytellers like Serling who showed me how to deliver them. My job is putting them together.

When I wrote about Charlie, I could've written about him a hundred different ways. I didn't want to just recite the facts. I didn't want to argue with conspiracy theorists.

I wanted to tell a story. I wanted to make you feel something. I wanted the Flock to be a villain worth remembering.

Read it here: The Desecration of Charlie Kirk

Stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. They have a machine that finds their storytellers and feeds them. We don't have one. You're it. stopbeingprey.com/patronage

subject: they think it's funny...
preview: ... when our people get killed
html:
There's a comedian named Sam Hyde. He's a controversial character who is very popular among young men... young right-wing men, in particular.

He once said this:

"When we win, do not forget that these people want you broke, dead, your kids raped and brainwashed, and they think it's funny."

There was a time when I thought this was hyperbole. An exaggeration of the truth.

I no longer believe that. Haven't for some time. I've seen more than enough evidence over the last year to see that Sam was just ahead of his time with this one. He said it back in 2016.

I just spent my entire morning observing exactly this phenomenon on my Thomas Sowell page when I re-shared my memorial for Charlie Kirk.

Here's what a woman named Nadi came to my page to say:

I was at home while my kid was at school and my man was at work. I screamed and cheered for 5 minutes straight. That was before I knew he was gone.After they made it official I felt like "wow I was just watching him 2 weeks ago and literally said to the screen that I hope someone pops his ssa and then this happened". I wished for his demise soon before it happened. Lmao a dream come true tbh.

And it wasn't just a one-off. She's in there, harassing my readers. Letting them know she's laughing at us for mourning Charlie. Laughing at him for dying and laughing at his children for being fatherless.

One of my readers, Zak, a good man, came into the memorial to express his grief. Here's what Zak said:

11 years younger than my youngest child.

Nadi had a message for him:

3 years younger than me. Absolutely delicious. What a short life 😂

Nadi is not alone. She's one of dozens in my comments right now, brigading the memorial. Spitting on Charlie's grave, harassing my readers, and laughing at all of us for mourning him. The receipts are endless, and not all of them are bots. Some of them are very real people, with very real profiles. Families... children.

One of my readers, Katie, stepped in. She didn't argue with her. She just asked her a question.

"Did you hug your kid joyfully knowing that his kids would never get to hug their dad ever again?"

Katie asked her about her child. She answered:

"The world instantly became better for me and my kids. 😁"

Now here's the thing I want you to understand. Nadi is here to get a rise out of you. She wants you angry and upset. She wants you to respond in that state. She wants you to do battle on this ground. This is a predator that has come to lay traps and hunt you.

Are you going to give her what she wants? Unfortunately, and I say this with love, many of my readers are falling for her trap, and the traps of others like her. I get it. I feel the pull too. It's enraging, it's sick... You feel compelled to do something about it. To let them know how you really feel.

One of my readers did exactly that this morning

"I slept on the floor of my children's floor. I was devastated... When I saw the reactions of the nose ring crowd I permanently lost all hope. We are not the same species."

Watch what happened next.

A man named Daniel had been in that thread all morning, spitting on Charlie's grave and laughing at my readers.

Daniel went and found that comment, and replied:

"Do you realize how dangerous it is to dehumanize your enemies?"

And my reader took the bait...

"I do not care anymore. They dehumanized themselves. Look at the emojis I got to my post. They can all burn."

They laugh-react the mourners. That's it, that's the tactic.

Daniel was one of them. And it got a rise out of him, enough for him to dehumanize them all.

And I get it. They are dehumanizing us. They want to kill us, and laugh about it. That is real. If they feel that way about Charlie, they feel that way about you and me too.

But we are not them, and we must not become them. This is the great danger. I know it's tempting; I feel the temptation too... but remember the Lord's Prayer.

"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."

So what do you do instead?

Here's what I wrote to her this morning, after she told my readers that Charlie's murder was a dream come true.

"Nadi, welcome! It's a pleasure to have you here, genuinely!

I have to congratulate you on your honesty. Most people who come here to dunk on Charlie pretend they believe he shouldn't have been murdered... but not you. You just come out and say it.

You are a specimen that I value highly. Come back to my page, anytime. Show us all what you are."

Do you see the difference? My reader gave them what they came for. I gave them nothing and took something for myself, instead. Frame control.

But I'll tell you this. I wanted to respond the way he did. I felt the temptation. It would've felt good to post something nasty to these people. Cathartic.

That's the trap.

The last couple of months, I've focused on writing cornerstone pieces. Long articles that tackle hard subjects and take an enormous amount of time to get right. It's good work, I'm proud of it, and I know you value it too... but I think it's time for me to return to the fight.

To focus on engaging the enemy. Showing you how to stop being prey, and become their predators.

This is the purpose of this project, in the end. To give you something useful, something that makes us a much greater force to contend with.

And so, this is what's on my mind now. War. Taking the fight to these people. Devastating them gracefully. Use their hate to fund my work. Monetize the haters.

All of this happened because of one Facebook post this morning, meant to memorialize his life.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. The Desecration of Charlie Kirk is an important piece. Do what you can to keep spreading it. We're one month away from the Anniversary of Charlie's assassination. stopbeingprey.com/desecration

p.p.s. There's a whole industry of people who make a living spitting on the graves of our dead, laughing at us for mourning them... funded five and ten dollars at a time by their own audience. Their side pays for what they want more of. Are you going to fund yours? stopbeingprey.com/patronage

subject: a stray kitten...
preview: ... spent my entire evening chasing it
html:
I went out for a quick walk with my dog this evening, and as I came home, I saw one of my neighbors poking around a bush while she was on her phone.

It was a stray kitten. The cutest little thing I've ever seen. He was scared, and he wouldn't let us get close.

I tried luring him with food for a while, but no luck. One by one, the neighborhood started to get involved. We were working together, trying to trap him and lead him towards the net or a cage. We spent well over an hour doing this. No luck.

It was nice to see the neighbors working together, trying to do something good... it made me realize I should probably try to do more nice things for my neighbors.

In the end... we failed. The kitten got away, and we don't know where he went. And now, I'm a little sad... thinking about the dark fate that may be awaiting that poor little guy. We get a lot of coyotes around here.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: birds of a feather...
preview: ...flock together
html:
I've come to accept that I'm going to be talking about Charlie Kirk for a long time. My last piece will not be the last time I write about him, I can promise you that.

I've been absorbing the feedback. It's overwhelmingly positive... but where there is criticism and hate, it is severe. And it's coming from a particular group of people. A particular faction of the flock, you might say.

The left comes into my posts about Charlie, as they always do, to spit on his grave and tell us all how evil we are for mourning him. But you know what? They are the minority this time around. Now, I'm facing a much more hostile crowd. Imagine that... a crowd more hostile than the one spitting on a dead man's grave... lucky me!

These aren't progressives... these are people who think of themselves as conservatives, right-wing or libertarian. They say they loved Charlie. Some of them wept when he was killed.

And they're the ones telling me I'm the one dishonouring him. That I'm covering something up. Perhaps I should be sued for my piece about Charlie, for what I said about Candace. Yes, these threats are coming to me now...

This is okay, I've been expecting this. Their audience is massive. It dwarfs mine, and I did poke the bear deliberately.

So I've been looking into them, doing my due diligence. I found something I think you should know about...

Here's a name you probably haven't heard of. Zee Cohen-Sanchez. A Democratic strategist who worked for Bernie. In November of 2024, she started a PAC. Then she launched a campus tour with one job... counter Turning Point USA. It followed them around the country. She called it the "Unf*ck America Tour".

Did you know about this? I'm just learning about it tonight.

In June, she posted this.

"@RealCandaceO started with one question: Who killed Charlie Kirk? I started by uncovering what appeared to be a network of completely fake chapters at @TPUSA. Then came Part 2. Then Part 3. Now every lead points to the same place. The deeper I dig, the more it feels like Candace and I are chasing the same answer. Something tells me we're going to find it together."

I'm not claiming any kind of conspiracy between Candace and Zee, of course. What I'm noticing is the consensus....

The flock is selecting its next targets. Turning Point... Erika... do you see it?

The Machinery that Charlie built. The Legacy he left. It has to go. The flock demands it.

stay close,

~ Clay

P.S. This is going to get uglier before it gets better. stopbeingprey.com/patronage is where you can have my back.

subject: Nobody gave the order
preview: What happened to Charlie Kirk after he died.
html:
🎧 Audio version available at stopbeingprey.com/desecration

THE DESECRATION OF CHARLIE KIRK

Tyler Robinson didn't kill Charlie Kirk. He just pulled the trigger.

The truth is, Charlie was already marked for death by a class of people. The same people who marked Donald Trump for death. The same people who will mark you and those you love for death, if you become too much of a problem for them.

They don't really want to kill you. In fact, they'd rather not.

It's a messy business, this whole murder thing.

It's just, you really need to submit.

And by submission, I don't mean agreement. They really couldn't care less if you're a total goose-stepping fascist posting to 300 followers on twitter or a classical liberal sipping wine while you read Sowell by your fireplace. You're allowed to have whatever opinions you want.

What you're not allowed to have is power. Charlie got a little too close, and so he had to go.

It's not personal. It's politics.

Act 1

The tyrant dies and his rule is over, the martyr dies and his rule begins.

~ Soren Kierkegaard • journals • 1848

That's what I posted to my Facebook page the day Charlie Kirk was assassinated. I didn't explain it, I didn't post a comment… I just posted that quote above a picture of Charlie, memorializing his life.

I still can't decide if that quote is cope or not. I posted it because I wanted it to be true. If Charlie's gone, then his death must mean something. We have to make it mean something!

I've never felt so much righteous indignation in my life.

And I know that millions of you feel the same, because that post went viral in a way I've never experienced before, and am unlikely to ever experience again. I felt the raw power of Charlie's influence moving through my page the day he died.

I had been a fan of Charlie for years, passively consuming his content for entertainment. I liked him, but I was also critical of him. I was still very much in my losertarian phase. So focused on my principles that I couldn't see reality, and had zero sense of political strategy.

I actually thought I knew better than Charlie. I really believed that.

Then, they killed him, and it's like a switch flipped in my brain. The world started to make sense. The reality of politics became clear. And for the first time, I could actually see what Charlie was building.

I was born 8 years before Charlie, but he was somehow 100 years wiser than I was.

The so-called 'marketplace of ideas' is, in fact, not a marketplace at all. It is a battlefield. Charlie was fighting the real war, trying to take real ground, while my libertarian friends and I argued in the halls of a marketplace that doesn't even exist.

I watched his memorial… that enormous event in the stadium, with hundreds of thousands of people. I watched the people who loved him try to put his life into words. I mourned him for months. I'm still mourning him now.

So, who was this man they were so desperate to defeat?

The most dangerous man in American politics ran on Starbucks mint tea. Mint Majesty, two honeys, all day long… because he talked so much, it was the only thing that kept him from losing his voice.

He stood at 6'5" tall, and he liked to joke about how he had descended from the Nephilim, the giants of the Old Testament.

He could effortlessly throw a football 50 yards just to show everyone who said he couldn't, that he could… and he had a big smile that spawned a million memes, most of them unkind. He kept smiling anyway.

So how does a goofy giant with a big smile and an odd Starbucks habit become the most dangerous man in American politics?

It started with a folding card table lodged in the basement of his parents' house. He lugged that thing to the nearest university with a homemade sign that said BIG GOVERNMENT SUCKS.

He was 18 years old, the age men can be drafted into war.

That little card table was the entire operation. That was Turning Point USA in 2012.

A decade later, that card table had become the largest conservative youth machine in America. Seven hundred employees. Seventy million dollars a year. Hundreds of chapters.

He filled arenas with the same kids the experts swore were gone for good. He turned out the youth vote that helped put Trump back in the White House… the President credited him for it himself.

Every year, those campuses produce the next generation of the progressive militia. The teachers, the journalists, the bureaucrats, the politicians, the judges… whoever holds this territory writes the future, and it was theirs, unchallenged for sixty years.

But then there was this damn kid, and his damn card table, setting up shop right in the middle of their territory…

And he just would not go away.

Act 2

Transphobe. Racist. Far-right Extremist. White Supremacist. Fascist.

And those were the polite ones.

The Sacramento Bee said Charlie "called for the lynching of trans people" while he was still alive. They were forced to apologize after he challenged it.

Called for the lynching of trans people. Quite an accusation.

So, is there any truth to it? Did Charlie hate trans people?

Let me show what happened when one of them stepped up to his microphone.

A few months before Charlie was killed, a young woman named Sebastian did exactly that. She said she was transgender, and started to ask her question, something about what age kids should be able to start taking hormones. Charlie's own crowd started heckling and talking over her.

Charlie stopped them.

Please give our speaker some uninterrupted speaking time.

~ Charlie Kirk

Before Charlie said a single word about the issue itself, his first instinct was to protect her voice… from his own crowd.

When she was done, Charlie didn't lie to her, or try to soften his message to win her over. He told her he's against giving hormones to children, and went further, telling her that he'd lost trust in the medical industry to prescribe any of it in a way that actually helps the patient.

Sebastian didn't push back. She agreed with him. "I get that", she said. "I'm scared too, because I don't know what's true, what's not. Would this even help me?" And Charlie, instead of pressing the point and taking the political victory, he softened his voice… "Tell me," he said "Are you comfortable telling me your story?"

And she told him. She'd known since the third grade, she said. She was nineteen now, almost twenty. She'd been going by a different name since middle school. But she didn't know what was true about the medical side of it. She'd heard a hundred different opinions from a hundred different people… and she wanted to hear Charlie's.

"First of all" Charlie said, "thank you so much for that." And then he gave her the hard truth, gently. He told her he was about to say something that almost no one in her life would ever tell her… and he asked her to think and pray about it.

I actually want to see you be comfortable in how you were born. I know you might not feel that way, but I think that's something you can achieve. I think that with the right team and the right people, you don't have to wage war on your body. You can learn to love your body.

~ Charlie Kirk

There's your transphobic bigot.

But the Sacramento Bee was far from alone…

The day after Charlie was murdered, Stephen King said Charlie "advocated stoning gays to death". He too was later forced to apologize.

One of the best selling authors in human history, repeating a lie about a dead man to his massive audience. What was he thinking? Only Stephen can answer that for himself.

I can speculate.

I'm not convinced that Stephen King is an evil man. I don't think he woke up that morning intending to tell a lie about a murdered father. In fact, I wish that was all this was. That's much easier to explain.

The truth is more chilling… he really believed it. He thought he was telling the truth. Stephen didn't decide for himself that Charlie was a monster. He didn't spend his time watching his videos, or listening to him on the radio. He had no idea who Charlie was, or what he was like.

So, how did Stephen King know that Charlie "advocated stoning gays to death"? Did he come up with that idea all on his own?

No, he was told.

He was told a man was a monster, over and over, by everyone he trusts, until it stopped feeling like something he'd been told and started feeling like something he knew. Like the sky is blue. You don't fact check the sky.

Everybody knows the sky is blue!

Everybody knows Charlie is a hateful person.

Stephen King knew it. Your aunt who shares NPR articles knew it. The HR lady at your office knew it. Your kid's teacher with the rainbow flag on her desk knew it. The barista with the pronoun pin knew it. The people celebrating his murder knew it.

Tyler Robinson knew it.

Hey fascist! Catch!

~ engraved on ammunition recovered at the scene • charging documents • Utah County • September 2025

So Tyler is a hero in this world. He killed a fascist. A monster.

Whatever happens to him, his story is over. He's not important.

Charlie was convicted and sentenced to death long before he was shot. Not by a court. Not by a jury… by a class of people who consider themselves to be the rightful managers of America. The class that has ruled unopposed since at least FDR.

This is who told Stephen King that Charlie wanted to stone gays and convinced Tyler Robinson that Charlie was a fascist.

It's not a conspiracy, it's a consensus.

Have you ever watched a flock of birds? A murmuration.

Thousands of them, turning in the sky at once.

Where's the leader?

Go ahead and look for it. You won't find one. Every single bird in that flock is doing one simple thing: watching the few birds closest to it and matching them. That's it. No bird sees the whole shape, or gets to decide what form it takes.

That's the consensus. That's why Stephen King believed Charlie wanted to stone gays, and it's why Tyler Robinson killed Charlie Kirk. Nobody gave either of them an order. The flock doesn't give orders… it murmurs. And every bird adjusts.

They're just flying with their flock.

You probably know what this is like. If you are human, you are a social creature. You flock too. It's okay. We all do.

Tyler and Stephen weren't aware of this. They convinced themselves they were in control. That they had a firm grasp of the facts. They never saw the flock feeding them those facts… and those 'facts' turned one of them into a liar in front of millions, and the other into a corpse-maker in front of the world.

So who answers for it?

Robinson goes to prison. Fine. But the thing that made him, the thing that put the lie in Stephen's mouth and the target on Charlie's back… that thing gets to walk away clean and pick its next target. It always does.

The flock flies on.

Why does it get to keep flying? Why can't anyone stop it?

Because there's nothing to stop. The flock isn't physical, it's spiritual.

You can shoot a bird out of the sky. You can't shoot a belief. Kill the man who holds it, and it just moves to the man beside him. That's why the flock never breaks. You took Robinson out of it and it didn't even flinch.

The flock took out our most effective general, and your reward is locking up one confused young man who happened to pull the trigger. And even that, for you, is a struggle. You are tormented for months. Hoping you can get some small hint of justice… eventually.

This isn't the system failing you. It's the system telling you the truth. It's letting you know your place.

The one who can kill and answer to no one, that's the sovereign. That's who rules you. The one who has to beg the courts for months to sentence a single pawn… that's the subject. That's who is ruled.

The flock is your real Government, and it doesn't have a President or a Congress.

It has a vibe.

And sometimes, when that vibe feels threatened… it turns murderous.

Charlie threatened the vibe, so the vibe killed him.

Act 3

Charlie didn't just threaten the vibe. He was pulling people out of the flock. And it gets worse for them…

The martyr dies, and his rule begins.

Nobody knows the power of a martyr better than our friends, the progressives.

They are always fishing for a new one that they can use for themselves. Sometimes they even try to manufacture them. Have you noticed this? It never stops.

Smollett, the Bubba Wallace rope, the UVA hoax, hands-up-don't shoot… do I need to keep going? I haven't even gotten to the heavy hitters yet.

Let's start with Saint George Floyd.

Do you think a single solitary leftist or democrat politician genuinely gave a shit about George Floyd? Do you think Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer were just so full of grief for poor George, that they couldn't help but take a knee in Kente cloth in front of all those cameras in D.C.? It's just a matter of basic decency! These are decent people, doing decent things… can't you tell?

Look at Mayor Jacob Frey crying over George's coffin. Weeping like a baby. It's because he just cares so much about black lives, you see. He's really broken up about poor George.

It's not grief… it's politics.

This is what progressives do... this is how they operate. They are fishing for a martyr that they can use to ram their agenda down your throat… and they'll never stop fishing.

Floyd is already fading. Six years later, even their own side is quietly moving on. The progressives already milked that cow for all the political capital it's worth, and now, it's starting to become a liability. Time to look away, pretend it never happened.

But not all of them fade. Floyd lasted six years. Their masterpiece has lasted sixty and counting.

Martin Luther King Jr.

The founding Saint of the Civil Rights religion. Complete with a holy day, scripture and heresy. To disagree isn't to be wrong, it's to be evil. Progressives finally secured the power to define all opposition as a moral crime. Racism.

Every institution in America bent the knee. Some of them literally, on television, before a football game.

It's taught to your children as gospel.

You've felt it. That little flinch when the subject comes up. You have to be careful with your words all of a sudden. You can smell the power lurking around you, watching you.

So, the progressives know the power of a good martyr, quite intimately. And you can bet that they know the danger of handing one to their enemies… their subjects, who they intend to rule.

And with Charlie, they know exactly what they've done. They handed us one.

If Charlie was the monster they said he was, the people who celebrated his murder are just normal people. Relieved. A bad man died.

But if he wasn't... then they cheered the murder of a father of two.

There is no third option… and they know which version they need for their story to work.

And so, he has to stay a monster. They can never let your grandchildren meet the man. The one that Sebastian met.

They have to kill him twice.

Act 4

"1 Nazi down." An art teacher in Iowa posted that within hours of the murder.

Have you noticed how many teachers hate Charlie? Some of them have the good sense to keep it to themselves, but a lot of them wanted you to know. They wanted your children to know.

"Thoughts and prayers to his children, but America became greater today." A social studies teacher in South Carolina said that proudly, right there on his Facebook page.

In Texas alone, the state moved to suspend the teaching licenses of more than a hundred of them.

Those are just the ones who got caught, because they said it out loud, under their own names. That's the only reason we even know about them. Nobody knows how many teachers felt exactly the same way and said nothing. That number is bigger… much bigger. And every one of them went to work the next morning raising the next generation of the flock.

That classroom is the battleground Charlie spent his life trying to take.

He had to drive across the country and fight for every minute, in front of kids who'd been taught to hate him before he arrived.

These teachers don't have to do any of that. They get handed a classroom with a government paycheck, and the culture tells them they're the real heroes.

The flock flies on.

And it didn't stop at the teachers. It went all the way up to Washington DC.

Days after Charlie was murdered, the House brought up a resolution to honor him. Nothing complicated, just basic decency. Honor the dead man, a good friend of the sitting President.

Well, that offended some people. AOC, a sitting Congresswoman, voted no on the resolution, and walked up to the microphone.

She called the murder horrific and vile. Then she read the charges.

We should be clear about who Charlie Kirk was; a man who believed that the Civil Rights Act that granted Black Americans the right to vote was a mistake.

~ Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez • House floor • September 19, 2025

She's got the wrong law. The voting one came a year later, and it's called the Voting Rights Act. She didn't do a basic fact check, she just uncritically fused two laws together to put the worst possible case against Charlie into the public record.

His body was barely cold.

She wasn't there to be fair. She was there, at the hour meant to mourn him, to desecrate his corpse.

Death was not enough.

Three weeks later, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar sat down with Don Lemon and said this.

But there is no legacy to honor. It was a legacy filled with bigotry, hatred, and White supremacy. And as a Black woman and as a Muslim in this country, I refuse to join the chorus that changes the history of what is on the record from this man.

~ Ilhan Omar • on Don Lemon's show • September 2025

That's on the record now too.

A sitting Congresswoman. A schoolteacher in Iowa. A kid on a roof in Utah.

Tyler Robinson wasn't uniquely evil. He was the only man on that roof. He was not the only one who wanted Charlie dead.

The kid who carved "hey fascist" into the bullets believed the exact same thing as the teacher who typed "1 Nazi down." Same ideology. Same hatred.

The only difference between them is one trigger pull.

And that's how the flock operates. They're not all killers. They don't need to be. The signal goes out, and the ones who'll do it find their way to the target eventually.

That's exactly what they did to Charlie. They'd been screaming "fascist" at him for years. It's on their media feeds, in their classrooms, their newspapers, their Discord servers… then one of them carved the word into a bullet and put it through his neck.

Signal sent. Signal received. One less effective enemy to contend with.

The flock flies on.

So, that's how Charlie's enemies have treated him. It's to be expected, that's what enemies do… but now we have to talk about one of his "friends."

Candace Owens.

And to understand what she's doing, you first have to be clear on what she's looking at. What actually happened to Charlie, because it was never a mystery.

We have all the evidence you could ever want to convict Tyler Robinson.

It was his own father who recognized him, and turned him in.

He confessed to his parents. He confessed again in texts to his boyfriend, the night of the murder. His DNA was on the towel the rifle was wrapped in. There's camera footage of him on the roof.

And the motive? He carved that into the bullets himself. Weeks before, he sat down with an engraving tool and etched his slogans into the ammunition. "Hey fascist! Catch!" "Bella ciao," the old antifascist anthem.

Candace knew Charlie. She built her career inside his movement.

And she looked at every last piece of what you just read. A father turning in his own son. The confession. The texts. The bullets he engraved with his own hands.

And she decided none of it was real.

She even became a ballistics expert in the process.

So, if it wasn't the confessed leftist with a trans boyfriend who killed Charlie, who was it? Well, Candace is just asking questions, you see.

Was it Israel? Just wondering! And Erika, his widow, standing over his casket… how much did she really know? Was somebody on his own security team in on it? And is there even a body? Was he quietly cremated to destroy the evidence?

She's just curious. She wants to get at the truth. No question is off the table!

Or…

She's not curious. She's casting doubt. Building a defense, not just for the killer, but for the whole flock he flew with.

She looked at Tyler, confessed, his own father turning him in, motive carved into the bullets, his DNA on the towel the rifle was wrapped in, and called him innocent. She offered to help his defense.

If Tyler Robinson's defense would like to contact me, I'd be happy to supply them the folder of the maroon boys that I began archiving when I noticed the bizarre fashion trend.

~ Candace Owens • July 9, 2026

His own lawyers wouldn't touch a word of it. Why do you think that is? Are they in on the conspiracy too?

I'm not going after her for being wrong. Wrong is allowed. Questions are allowed.

Her crime is what the questions are for.

She's not looking for answers. She took the one thing that could make Charlie's death mean something… a good man, murdered by the left for telling the truth… and she buried it in a fog of doubt. She handed his real killers their alibi. She turned our martyr into a mystery.

People love a good mystery. Mix in some true crime and drama, and you have a hit story for YouTube that can pay out millions in ad revenue. It's one of the most watched things on the internet.

But a mystery organizes no one… it changes nothing… it just fades when people get bored and find the next shiny conspiracy video to pursue. Which is exactly what the flock wanted all along.

The flock marked him. Tyler Robinson pulled the trigger. And it's Candace Owens and her supporters covering the killers' tracks.

It's not curiosity. It's politics.

Act 5

You can tell a lot about a person by how they react when someone dies.

~Charlie Kirk • 2016

Not long before he was murdered, Charlie Kirk sat down for an interview. He had no idea it would be his last.

The last question: What is a quote that you live by?

He talks about his faith, then he says this:

There is a God, and I am not him, and I surrender to His will.

~ Charlie Kirk • in his final interview • September 10, 2025

Charlie would never submit to the flock, because he had already submitted to a power that sits above it.

He had less than an hour left.

He walks out to that campus in Utah.

That big goofy smile on full display, mint teas sitting on the card table in front of him, while a huge crowd of patriots and progressives congregate to see him.

Everyone knew who the man of power on campus was, instinctively. All eyes were upon him.

For twelve years he would not go away.

So that's it. His story ends here. Charlie Kirk doesn't get to see his kids grow up. He doesn't get to grow old with Erika.

Then there's us. We lost our best General. The man who would walk into enemy territory and start recruiting the flock's most precious asset. Its youth.

Now what? Do we all set up our own card tables at the universities and copy what Charlie did?

Anybody can buy a card table, set it up on a campus and start talking to students. Plenty of people are doing that now, in Charlie's honor… but that was never the magic.

A kid argues with you for a few minutes then walks away. Maybe you get a viral clip. Okay. That's energy. But where does that energy go?

What made Charlie dangerous is that he was converting that energy into power. There was somewhere for that kid to go next. Campus chapters, staff jobs, and a national conference every year. Something that kept moving after the card table was folded up and put back in the closet.

The magic was in what Charlie was building. The machinery. That's what scared the flock.

We want to be an institution in this country that is as well-known and as powerful as The New York Times, Harvard and tech companies. And we believe we're creating that.

~ Charlie Kirk • Deseret News • August 19, 2025

An institution that reliably turns the flock's own heirs into a coalition that refuses to submit to it.

Do you see why he had to go?

And now, the flock moves on to its next targets. His family. His supporters. His institution. It all has to go. You have to go.

You can keep moving forward, but you will be punished. Shamed. If you become too effective, you will be shot at. That's the game. That's your "marketplace of ideas."

If nobody wants you dead, you're not playing.

You are in a spiritual war against a thing that rules America and answers to nobody in it. There is no court above it. There is no election that removes it.

So the question is. Who are you going to submit to?

There's a reader of mine. His name is John. He watched Charlie get shot while sitting on a nursing home bed, next to his dying mother.

She died that Thanksgiving.

At her burial, John stood up and spoke to her. This is part of what he said.

And the truth is, on one September afternoon, I was sitting with you in the nursing home and we saw the murder of Charlie Kirk. He was a truth teller. A soldier of God. You saw how it moved me and it did. Since then I've been going to church. Trying to renew my faith. Trying to be the person you always knew I could be... The next time I visited you, in October, I was wearing a cross... You seemed happier for me than I've seen you in a while. I will keep trying to make you proud. I love you mom.

~ John • at his mother's burial

A Soldier of God.

Bear your cross, soldier.

~ Clay


p.s. If this landed for you, share it with someone who needs to hear it. Shareable version on the website.

p.p.s. A hundred and forty people fund this work. They're the only reason it exists. If you'd like to join them, here.

subject: let's get physical
preview: thomas sowell published collections of essays
html:
Whenever I finish a cornerstone piece, I feel like a weight has been lifted off my shoulders. Like I'm suddenly free to start working on all of the other things I've been wanting to do, but couldn't find the time for, because the piece took priority above all.

I've been thinking about what to spend my time on next. Should I get back into code? Make some improvements to the website and the membership area? Yea, probably... those are living projects, they could always use the attention.

Should I get started on my next big piece? Maybe... but I think I need to decompress a bit first.

Here's what I'm thinking right now... it might be time to move from the digital world into the physical one.

The Book. Remember how I've been promising a book?

When I started this project, the plan was that I was writing one. I never abandoned that, but I never had a clear vision of what it should actually be. I had plenty of ideas. Most of them were incompatible with each other, and I didn't know how to choose.

And if I'm going to write a book, it can't just be for the sake of writing one. I have to have something real to put down on paper.

Well, last night... I think I figured it out. The answer was obvious the whole time, I just didn't see it. Thomas Sowell already showed me how.

A Collection of Essays.

That's what a lot of his books are. Controversial Essays. Dismantling America. Barbarians Inside the Gates. Ever Wonder Why? He spent years writing columns, and then he gathered up the ones that still mattered and put them between two covers.

And so, the idea is this. I'm going to start putting out volumes. Right now we're in my first era as a writer, and I think the second one is coming. The time is coming to put this era into a volume.

Stop Being Prey: Volume I

I'll collect my best essays and emails from this era in a beautiful hardcover that'll look great on our shelves. I'll also write some commentary about each piece.

I'm still fleshing out the idea, but this is what's on my mind.

What do you think? Would you buy one?

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I've got another idea for getting this into the physical world. You know how the founding fathers wrote pamphlets and handed them around? Cheap, printed, meant to be given to somebody. I think it can still work if there's an audience interested enough in spreading them.

subject: no big sacrifice
preview: do you remember bob?
html:
Do you remember Bob? I wrote about him a while back.

Bob's been here since the beginning. He's a founder. He works on aircraft. He cuts gems. He sometimes shows us the stuff he's worked on in my lounge.

He once emailed to tell me he's a cheapskate who doesn't donate enough, and then asked me where I needed the money most.

Bob's a character. Every time I get an email from him, I know I'm in for a good chuckle or two.

He wrote me this morning about the Charlie piece.

He told me that he figures I'll end up with a target on me as big as Charlie's one day. An odd way to compliment someone... isn't it? Telling them they're going to get shot if they keep it up... but then Bob immediately followed up by telling me that he'll stand next to me and take the bullet.

"My life is at its end anyway so no big sacrifice."

That's word for word.

And then, because he's Bob, he apologized for it. "This is just my emotions writing."

But he does this all the time. He shows up, hands me everything he's got, and then tells me it isn't worth much. The cheapskate who gives generously. Says he'd take a bullet for me and calls it no big deal.

I believe this is what they call humility.

Bob is a good man. Lifts people up around him, and then gets out of the way. He often tells me to not bother replying to him... after he sends me one of the heaviest emails I've ever read in my life.

That's Bob.

He's the type of guy who keeps this project alive. Who makes sure I have what I need to keep writing. He checks in on me, he gives me material support, and most importantly... he makes me laugh.

I have somewhere around 150 patrons now, supporting me. They're the only reason I could spend a full month on the Charlie piece instead of rushing something out in three days.

If you're like Bob, and you believe in what I'm doing, the patronage is where you belong.

stopbeingprey.com/patronage

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. if you haven't read the piece Bob was writing to me about, it's here. He said it gave him goosebumps.stopbeingprey.com/desecration

subject: The Desecration of Charlie Kirk
preview: It's not a conspiracy, it's a consensus.
html:
🎧 Audio version available at stopbeingprey.com/desecration



Tyler Robinson didn't kill Charlie Kirk. He just pulled the trigger.

The truth is, Charlie was already marked for death by a class of people. The same people who marked Donald Trump for death. The same people who will mark you and those you love for death, if you become too much of a problem for them.

They don't really want to kill you. In fact, they'd rather not.

It's a messy business, this whole murder thing.

It's just, you really need to submit.

And by submission, I don't mean agreement. They really couldn't care less if you're a total goose-stepping fascist posting to 300 followers on twitter or a classical liberal sipping wine while you read Sowell by your fireplace. You're allowed to have whatever opinions you want.

What you're not allowed to have is power. Charlie got a little too close, and so he had to go.

It's not personal. It's politics.

Act 1

The tyrant dies and his rule is over, the martyr dies and his rule begins.

~ Soren Kierkegaard • journals • 1848

That's what I posted to my Facebook page the day Charlie Kirk was assassinated. I didn't explain it, I didn't post a comment… I just posted that quote above a picture of Charlie, memorializing his life.

I still can't decide if that quote is cope or not. I posted it because I wanted it to be true. If Charlie's gone, then his death must mean something. We have to make it mean something!

I've never felt so much righteous indignation in my life.

And I know that millions of you feel the same, because that post went viral in a way I've never experienced before, and am unlikely to ever experience again. I felt the raw power of Charlie's influence moving through my page the day he died.

I had been a fan of Charlie for years, passively consuming his content for entertainment. I liked him, but I was also critical of him. I was still very much in my losertarian phase. So focused on my principles that I couldn't see reality, and had zero sense of political strategy.

I actually thought I knew better than Charlie. I really believed that.

Then, they killed him, and it's like a switch flipped in my brain. The world started to make sense. The reality of politics became clear. And for the first time, I could actually see what Charlie was building.

I was born 8 years before Charlie, but he was somehow 100 years wiser than I was.

The so-called 'marketplace of ideas' is, in fact, not a marketplace at all. It is a battlefield. Charlie was fighting the real war, trying to take real ground, while my libertarian friends and I argued in the halls of a marketplace that doesn't even exist.

I watched his memorial… that enormous event in the stadium, with hundreds of thousands of people. I watched the people who loved him try to put his life into words. I mourned him for months. I'm still mourning him now.

So, who was this man they were so desperate to defeat?

The most dangerous man in American politics ran on Starbucks mint tea. Mint Majesty, two honeys, all day long… because he talked so much, it was the only thing that kept him from losing his voice.

He stood at 6'5" tall, and he liked to joke about how he had descended from the Nephilim, the giants of the Old Testament.

He could effortlessly throw a football 50 yards just to show everyone who said he couldn't, that he could… and he had a big smile that spawned a million memes, most of them unkind. He kept smiling anyway.

So how does a goofy giant with a big smile and an odd Starbucks habit become the most dangerous man in American politics?

It started with a folding card table lodged in the basement of his parents' house. He lugged that thing to the nearest university with a homemade sign that said BIG GOVERNMENT SUCKS.

He was 18 years old, the age men can be drafted into war.

That little card table was the entire operation. That was Turning Point USA in 2012.

A decade later, that card table had become the largest conservative youth machine in America. Seven hundred employees. Seventy million dollars a year. Hundreds of chapters.

He filled arenas with the same kids the experts swore were gone for good. He turned out the youth vote that helped put Trump back in the White House… the President credited him for it himself.

Every year, those campuses produce the next generation of the progressive militia. The teachers, the journalists, the bureaucrats, the politicians, the judges… whoever holds this territory writes the future, and it was theirs, unchallenged for sixty years.

But then there was this damn kid, and his damn card table, setting up shop right in the middle of their territory…

And he just would not go away.

Act 2

Transphobe. Racist. Far-right Extremist. White Supremacist. Fascist.

And those were the polite ones.

The Sacramento Bee said Charlie "called for the lynching of trans people" while he was still alive. They were forced to apologize after he challenged it.

Called for the lynching of trans people. Quite an accusation.

So, is there any truth to it? Did Charlie hate trans people?

Let me show what happened when one of them stepped up to his microphone.

A few months before Charlie was killed, a young woman named Sebastian did exactly that. She said she was transgender, and started to ask her question, something about what age kids should be able to start taking hormones. Charlie's own crowd started heckling and talking over her.

Charlie stopped them.

Please give our speaker some uninterrupted speaking time.

~ Charlie Kirk

Before Charlie said a single word about the issue itself, his first instinct was to protect her voice… from his own crowd.

When she was done, Charlie didn't lie to her, or try to soften his message to win her over. He told her he's against giving hormones to children, and went further, telling her that he'd lost trust in the medical industry to prescribe any of it in a way that actually helps the patient.

Sebastian didn't push back. She agreed with him. "I get that", she said. "I'm scared too, because I don't know what's true, what's not. Would this even help me?" And Charlie, instead of pressing the point and taking the political victory, he softened his voice… "Tell me," he said "Are you comfortable telling me your story?"

And she told him. She'd known since the third grade, she said. She was nineteen now, almost twenty. She'd been going by a different name since middle school. But she didn't know what was true about the medical side of it. She'd heard a hundred different opinions from a hundred different people… and she wanted to hear Charlie's.

"First of all" Charlie said, "thank you so much for that." And then he gave her the hard truth, gently. He told her he was about to say something that almost no one in her life would ever tell her… and he asked her to think and pray about it.

I actually want to see you be comfortable in how you were born. I know you might not feel that way, but I think that's something you can achieve. I think that with the right team and the right people, you don't have to wage war on your body. You can learn to love your body.

~ Charlie Kirk

There's your transphobic bigot.

But the Sacramento Bee was far from alone…

The day after Charlie was murdered, Stephen King said Charlie "advocated stoning gays to death". He too was later forced to apologize.

One of the best selling authors in human history, repeating a lie about a dead man to his massive audience. What was he thinking? Only Stephen can answer that for himself.

I can speculate.

I'm not convinced that Stephen King is an evil man. I don't think he woke up that morning intending to tell a lie about a murdered father. In fact, I wish that was all this was. That's much easier to explain.

The truth is more chilling… he really believed it. He thought he was telling the truth. Stephen didn't decide for himself that Charlie was a monster. He didn't spend his time watching his videos, or listening to him on the radio. He had no idea who Charlie was, or what he was like.

So, how did Stephen King know that Charlie "advocated stoning gays to death"? Did he come up with that idea all on his own?

No, he was told.

He was told a man was a monster, over and over, by everyone he trusts, until it stopped feeling like something he'd been told and started feeling like something he knew. Like the sky is blue. You don't fact check the sky.

Everybody knows the sky is blue!

Everybody knows Charlie is a hateful person.

Stephen King knew it. Your aunt who shares NPR articles knew it. The HR lady at your office knew it. Your kid's teacher with the rainbow flag on her desk knew it. The barista with the pronoun pin knew it. The people celebrating his murder knew it.

Tyler Robinson knew it.

Hey fascist! Catch!

~ engraved on ammunition recovered at the scene • charging documents • Utah County • September 2025

So Tyler is a hero in this world. He killed a fascist. A monster.

Whatever happens to him, his story is over. He's not important.

Charlie was convicted and sentenced to death long before he was shot. Not by a court. Not by a jury… by a class of people who consider themselves to be the rightful managers of America. The class that has ruled unopposed since at least FDR.

This is who told Stephen King that Charlie wanted to stone gays and convinced Tyler Robinson that Charlie was a fascist.

It's not a conspiracy, it's a consensus.

Have you ever watched a flock of birds? A murmuration.

Thousands of them, turning in the sky at once.

Where's the leader?

Go ahead and look for it. You won't find one. Every single bird in that flock is doing one simple thing: watching the few birds closest to it and matching them. That's it. No bird sees the whole shape, or gets to decide what form it takes.

That's the consensus. That's why Stephen King believed Charlie wanted to stone gays, and it's why Tyler Robinson killed Charlie Kirk. Nobody gave either of them an order. The flock doesn't give orders… it murmurs. And every bird adjusts.

They're just flying with their flock.

You probably know what this is like. If you are human, you are a social creature. You flock too. It's okay. We all do.

Tyler and Stephen weren't aware of this. They convinced themselves they were in control. That they had a firm grasp of the facts. They never saw the flock feeding them those facts… and those 'facts' turned one of them into a liar in front of millions, and the other into a corpse-maker in front of the world.

So who answers for it?

Robinson goes to prison. Fine. But the thing that made him, the thing that put the lie in Stephen's mouth and the target on Charlie's back… that thing gets to walk away clean and pick its next target. It always does.

The flock flies on.

Why does it get to keep flying? Why can't anyone stop it?

Because there's nothing to stop. The flock isn't physical, it's spiritual.

You can shoot a bird out of the sky. You can't shoot a belief. Kill the man who holds it, and it just moves to the man beside him. That's why the flock never breaks. You took Robinson out of it and it didn't even flinch.

The flock took out our most effective general, and your reward is locking up one confused young man who happened to pull the trigger. And even that, for you, is a struggle. You are tormented for months. Hoping you can get some small hint of justice… eventually.

This isn't the system failing you. It's the system telling you the truth. It's letting you know your place.

The one who can kill and answer to no one, that's the sovereign. That's who rules you. The one who has to beg the courts for months to sentence a single pawn… that's the subject. That's who is ruled.

The flock is your real Government, and it doesn't have a President or a Congress.

It has a vibe.

And sometimes, when that vibe feels threatened… it turns murderous.

Charlie threatened the vibe, so the vibe killed him.

Act 3

Charlie didn't just threaten the vibe. He was pulling people out of the flock. And it gets worse for them…

The martyr dies, and his rule begins.

Nobody knows the power of a martyr better than our friends, the progressives.

They are always fishing for a new one that they can use for themselves. Sometimes they even try to manufacture them. Have you noticed this? It never stops.

Smollett, the Bubba Wallace rope, the UVA hoax, hands-up-don't shoot… do I need to keep going? I haven't even gotten to the heavy hitters yet.

Let's start with Saint George Floyd.

Do you think a single solitary leftist or democrat politician genuinely gave a shit about George Floyd? Do you think Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer were just so full of grief for poor George, that they couldn't help but take a knee in Kente cloth in front of all those cameras in D.C.? It's just a matter of basic decency! These are decent people, doing decent things… can't you tell?

Look at Mayor Jacob Frey crying over George's coffin. Weeping like a baby. It's because he just cares so much about black lives, you see. He's really broken up about poor George.

It's not grief… it's politics.

This is what progressives do... this is how they operate. They are fishing for a martyr that they can use to ram their agenda down your throat… and they'll never stop fishing.

Floyd is already fading. Six years later, even their own side is quietly moving on. The progressives already milked that cow for all the political capital it's worth, and now, it's starting to become a liability. Time to look away, pretend it never happened.

But not all of them fade. Floyd lasted six years. Their masterpiece has lasted sixty and counting.

Martin Luther King Jr.

The founding Saint of the Civil Rights religion. Complete with a holy day, scripture and heresy. To disagree isn't to be wrong, it's to be evil. Progressives finally secured the power to define all opposition as a moral crime. Racism.

Every institution in America bent the knee. Some of them literally, on television, before a football game.

It's taught to your children as gospel.

You've felt it. That little flinch when the subject comes up. You have to be careful with your words all of a sudden. You can smell the power lurking around you, watching you.

So, the progressives know the power of a good martyr, quite intimately. And you can bet that they know the danger of handing one to their enemies… their subjects, who they intend to rule.

And with Charlie, they know exactly what they've done. They handed us one.

If Charlie was the monster they said he was, the people who celebrated his murder are just normal people. Relieved. A bad man died.

But if he wasn't... then they cheered the murder of a father of two.

There is no third option… and they know which version they need for their story to work.

And so, he has to stay a monster. They can never let your grandchildren meet the man. The one that Sebastian met.

They have to kill him twice.

Act 4

"1 Nazi down." An art teacher in Iowa posted that within hours of the murder.

Have you noticed how many teachers hate Charlie? Some of them have the good sense to keep it to themselves, but a lot of them wanted you to know. They wanted your children to know.

"Thoughts and prayers to his children, but America became greater today." A social studies teacher in South Carolina said that proudly, right there on his Facebook page.

In Texas alone, the state moved to suspend the teaching licenses of more than a hundred of them.

Those are just the ones who got caught, because they said it out loud, under their own names. That's the only reason we even know about them. Nobody knows how many teachers felt exactly the same way and said nothing. That number is bigger… much bigger. And every one of them went to work the next morning raising the next generation of the flock.

That classroom is the battleground Charlie spent his life trying to take.

He had to drive across the country and fight for every minute, in front of kids who'd been taught to hate him before he arrived.

These teachers don't have to do any of that. They get handed a classroom with a government paycheck, and the culture tells them they're the real heroes.

The flock flies on.

And it didn't stop at the teachers. It went all the way up to Washington DC.

Days after Charlie was murdered, the House brought up a resolution to honor him. Nothing complicated, just basic decency. Honor the dead man, a good friend of the sitting President.

Well, that offended some people. AOC, a sitting Congresswoman, voted no on the resolution, and walked up to the microphone.

She called the murder horrific and vile. Then she read the charges.

We should be clear about who Charlie Kirk was; a man who believed that the Civil Rights Act that granted Black Americans the right to vote was a mistake.

~ Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez • House floor • September 19, 2025

She's got the wrong law. The voting one came a year later, and it's called the Voting Rights Act. She didn't do a basic fact check, she just uncritically fused two laws together to put the worst possible case against Charlie into the public record.

His body was barely cold.

She wasn't there to be fair. She was there, at the hour meant to mourn him, to desecrate his corpse.

Death was not enough.

Three weeks later, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar sat down with Don Lemon and said this.

But there is no legacy to honor. It was a legacy filled with bigotry, hatred, and White supremacy. And as a Black woman and as a Muslim in this country, I refuse to join the chorus that changes the history of what is on the record from this man.

~ Ilhan Omar • on Don Lemon's show • September 2025

That's on the record now too.

A sitting Congresswoman. A schoolteacher in Iowa. A kid on a roof in Utah.

Tyler Robinson wasn't uniquely evil. He was the only man on that roof. He was not the only one who wanted Charlie dead.

The kid who carved "hey fascist" into the bullets believed the exact same thing as the teacher who typed "1 Nazi down." Same ideology. Same hatred.

The only difference between them is one trigger pull.

And that's how the flock operates. They're not all killers. They don't need to be. The signal goes out, and the ones who'll do it find their way to the target eventually.

That's exactly what they did to Charlie. They'd been screaming "fascist" at him for years. It's on their media feeds, in their classrooms, their newspapers, their Discord servers… then one of them carved the word into a bullet and put it through his neck.

Signal sent. Signal received. One less effective enemy to contend with.

The flock flies on.

So, that's how Charlie's enemies have treated him. It's to be expected, that's what enemies do… but now we have to talk about one of his "friends."

Candace Owens.

And to understand what she's doing, you first have to be clear on what she's looking at. What actually happened to Charlie, because it was never a mystery.

We have all the evidence you could ever want to convict Tyler Robinson.

It was his own father who recognized him, and turned him in.

He confessed to his parents. He confessed again in texts to his boyfriend, the night of the murder. His DNA was on the towel the rifle was wrapped in. There's camera footage of him on the roof.

And the motive? He carved that into the bullets himself. Weeks before, he sat down with an engraving tool and etched his slogans into the ammunition. "Hey fascist! Catch!" "Bella ciao," the old antifascist anthem.

Candace knew Charlie. She built her career inside his movement.

And she looked at every last piece of what you just read. A father turning in his own son. The confession. The texts. The bullets he engraved with his own hands.

And she decided none of it was real.

She even became a ballistics expert in the process.

So, if it wasn't the confessed leftist with a trans boyfriend who killed Charlie, who was it? Well, Candace is just asking questions, you see.

Was it Israel? Just wondering! And Erika, his widow, standing over his casket… how much did she really know? Was somebody on his own security team in on it? And is there even a body? Was he quietly cremated to destroy the evidence?

She's just curious. She wants to get at the truth. No question is off the table!

Or…

She's not curious. She's casting doubt. Building a defense, not just for the killer, but for the whole flock he flew with.

She looked at Tyler, confessed, his own father turning him in, motive carved into the bullets, his DNA on the towel the rifle was wrapped in, and called him innocent. She offered to help his defense.

If Tyler Robinson's defense would like to contact me, I'd be happy to supply them the folder of the maroon boys that I began archiving when I noticed the bizarre fashion trend.

~ Candace Owens • July 9, 2026

His own lawyers wouldn't touch a word of it. Why do you think that is? Are they in on the conspiracy too?

I'm not going after her for being wrong. Wrong is allowed. Questions are allowed.

Her crime is what the questions are for.

She's not looking for answers. She took the one thing that could make Charlie's death mean something… a good man, murdered by the left for telling the truth… and she buried it in a fog of doubt. She handed his real killers their alibi. She turned our martyr into a mystery.

People love a good mystery. Mix in some true crime and drama, and you have a hit story for YouTube that can pay out millions in ad revenue. It's one of the most watched things on the internet.

But a mystery organizes no one… it changes nothing… it just fades when people get bored and find the next shiny conspiracy video to pursue. Which is exactly what the flock wanted all along.

The flock marked him. Tyler Robinson pulled the trigger. And it's Candace Owens and her supporters covering the killers' tracks.

It's not curiosity. It's politics.

Act 5

You can tell a lot about a person by how they react when someone dies.

~Charlie Kirk • 2016

Not long before he was murdered, Charlie Kirk sat down for an interview. He had no idea it would be his last.

The last question: What is a quote that you live by?

He talks about his faith, then he says this:

There is a God, and I am not him, and I surrender to His will.

~ Charlie Kirk • in his final interview • September 10, 2025

Charlie would never submit to the flock, because he had already submitted to a power that sits above it.

He had less than an hour left.

He walks out to that campus in Utah.

That big goofy smile on full display, mint teas sitting on the card table in front of him, while a huge crowd of patriots and progressives congregate to see him.

Everyone knew who the man of power on campus was, instinctively. All eyes were upon him.

For twelve years he would not go away.

So that's it. His story ends here. Charlie Kirk doesn't get to see his kids grow up. He doesn't get to grow old with Erika.

Then there's us. We lost our best General. The man who would walk into enemy territory and start recruiting the flock's most precious asset. Its youth.

Now what? Do we all set up our own card tables at the universities and copy what Charlie did?

Anybody can buy a card table, set it up on a campus and start talking to students. Plenty of people are doing that now, in Charlie's honor… but that was never the magic.

A kid argues with you for a few minutes then walks away. Maybe you get a viral clip. Okay. That's energy. But where does that energy go?

What made Charlie dangerous is that he was converting that energy into power. There was somewhere for that kid to go next. Campus chapters, staff jobs, and a national conference every year. Something that kept moving after the card table was folded up and put back in the closet.

The magic was in what Charlie was building. The machinery. That's what scared the flock.

We want to be an institution in this country that is as well-known and as powerful as The New York Times, Harvard and tech companies. And we believe we're creating that.

~ Charlie Kirk • Deseret News • August 19, 2025

An institution that reliably turns the flock's own heirs into a coalition that refuses to submit to it.

Do you see why he had to go?

And now, the flock moves on to its next targets. His family. His supporters. His institution. It all has to go. You have to go.

You can keep moving forward, but you will be punished. Shamed. If you become too effective, you will be shot at. That's the game. That's your "marketplace of ideas."

If nobody wants you dead, you're not playing.

You are in a spiritual war against a thing that rules America and answers to nobody in it. There is no court above it. There is no election that removes it.

So the question is. Who are you going to submit to?

There's a reader of mine. His name is John. He watched Charlie get shot while sitting on a nursing home bed, next to his dying mother.

She died that Thanksgiving.

At her burial, John stood up and spoke to her. This is part of what he said.

And the truth is, on one September afternoon, I was sitting with you in the nursing home and we saw the murder of Charlie Kirk. He was a truth teller. A soldier of God. You saw how it moved me and it did. Since then I've been going to church. Trying to renew my faith. Trying to be the person you always knew I could be... The next time I visited you, in October, I was wearing a cross... You seemed happier for me than I've seen you in a while. I will keep trying to make you proud. I love you mom.

~ John • at his mother's burial

A Soldier of God.

Bear your cross, soldier.

~ Clay

subject: good ideas, bad software
preview: I was the one running it.
html:
I write a lot about Charlie Kirk. It's because of that moment when I watched him get shot. For me, that was a life-changing moment, and I don't just say that for effect. It really was. I wouldn't be here, talking to you right now if not for that day.

As a libertarian, I actually thought I knew better than Charlie Kirk. I really believed that.

But I didn't know better. Not even close. That's why no one was shooting at me and my libertarian friends. They were shooting at Donald Trump and Charlie Kirk.

I'm a software engineer by trade. I'm good at noticing bugs in the systems I build, but for some reason, I was powerless to notice the bugs in my own software. Then Charlie was shot, and they were suddenly obvious.

My writing is how I debug my own brain. That's what this whole thing is. I'm identifying the errors in my thinking, and fleshing out a better way to think. Writing better code.

My goal is to build better software for our minds. So we can see the rules of the game clearly and stop getting ourselves hurt.

The Desecration of Charlie Kirk is the patch. It goes out tomorrow morning.

subject: the rainbow flag
preview: in my doctors office
html:
A few days ago, I was sitting in my doctor's office, waiting to see her. I had the Charlie Kirk piece running around in my head. I've been working on it all month.

Then, I looked over at the wall beside me...

"Positive Space" it said in big bold letters.

Then a picture of the rainbow flag with the following text, verbatim:

This is a place where human rights are respected and where Two Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans and queer people, and their friends and allies, are welcomed and supported

I just kept staring at it... reading it. I took a picture of it.

This sort of thing isn't unusual in Canada... I see it in the grocery store. In the public schools. On police cars. In the halls of Parliament.

And now on the wall beside me, while I wait to see my doctor.

I'm not allowed to do a simple thing, like sit and talk to my doctor, without a political movement watching over my shoulder, telling me to be kind...

Or else.

And this political movement likes to portray itself as the oppressed. It's the victim who needs protection. The thing that somehow is in every single institution needs protection, from me, a guy who just wants to talk to his doctor about headaches. A guy who pays a bunch of taxes for all of these systems to exist. I'm one mean word away from becoming the oppressor, you see.

I wasn't looking at a welcome sign. I was sitting next to a threat.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: thomas sowell wrote a book about his own son.
preview: most of his readers haven't heard of this one
html:
I posted about it again this morning on my Facebook page. It's a short story I wrote a few months ago about why Thomas Sowell wrote the book "Late Talking Children".

Short version: Sowell's son John didn't talk until he was almost four. The experts had a wall of diagnoses ready for him and not one of them fit. Years later, once John was grown, Sowell wrote about it in his newspaper column.

Parents started writing to him from all over the country. He had to ask himself... If so many people had this experience, why was there nothing out there for them to read? And so, he wrote the book himself. Late Talking Children.

You know what's fascinating? Every time I post that story, a small version of what happened to Sowell starts happening to me. People start writing to me in droves with their experiences of late talking children.

Comments like these:

"My mom. Didn't start speaking until 4 or 5, when she said a full sentence to ask where the dog had gone. They asked in astonishment why she hadn't spoken until then, and she said, 'I didn't need to.'"

"I am a primary care physician with a nephew who was not speaking after age 3. I was really concerned but held off offering advice. Within 2 years he was doing sudoku on his own, still with minimal conversations. Turns out he just didn't have much to say to us ordinary people and is brilliant and well adjusted to this day as an aerospace engineer."

"I didn't talk until I was almost 4 and one grandmother thought I was deaf while the other believed I was brain damaged."

"I was one of those kids. My own career was mostly spent in high end computer science, including AI... I have a long string of patents as well... Me. The late talker."

I don't have a child who talked late.... to tell you the truth, I had no idea late talking children were even a real phenomenon until I found out Sowell had written a book about it.

When I wrote about it, and posted it to my page, I feel like I got to experience a taste of what Sowell must've experienced when he wrote that column back in the 90s.

I've written a lot of big pieces as a writer, but this little story about an obscure book Sowell wrote about his late-talking son may do more real good in the world than anything I've ever written.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: my headaches
preview: i dont have words to describe how bad they are
html:
I've suffered with migraines for as long as I can remember. I think they may have started in my teens. Roughly once a month or so I get a real doozy. It's like torture, I don't know how to describe it in words. On these days, I am essentially incapacitated. I can't think, I can't work, I can't watch tv, I can't read, I feel nauseous, I can't sleep... I just have to be there, suffering... 'til it's over. It's hell.

It sometimes happens at the worst times too. At critical events in my life, it likes to show up and wreak havoc.

But then maybe a month ago, after another brutal migraine, I decided to go to ChatGPT. I started describing my symptoms as clearly and with as much detail as I could. I started learning about the differences between cluster headaches and migraine headaches, and a potential solution called Triptans. Got a prescription from my doc as fast as I could.

Then a few nights ago, I felt one coming on... that familiar dread creeping in for a night of pain and suffering. I popped one of those bad boys down my throat... and you know what? It worked! I could not believe it.

I don't want to jinx it, but if this does work reliably, I can't tell you how much of an upgrade this is for my life. No more monthly torture sessions. I'm finally free of this hell!

Here's what I can't stop thinking about now... I have a new doctor. She's great. I've only had her for a few months, and she wrote me up the prescription without hesitation. However, my old doctor, who just retired, has known about my headaches for decades. Not once did this option ever come up. I'm trying to wrap my head around why, and I can't come up with anything.

But ChatGPT was there. It knows just about everything... It's read all the medical journals, it can do research on the internet about 1000x faster than I ever could, and it can talk to me in as much detail as I need. I can ask whatever stupid questions I want without feeling any insecurity about it.

It's not that it's smarter than my doctor (though it might be!). It's just that it isn't in a hurry. I don't have a 15-minute time limit in its office.

What an incredible time to be alive.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: communism is cool

html:
Communism is cool, face it. The kids are into it. Great artists preach it. I can still remember my own Che Guevara shirt I used to wear as a teenager.

I was a fan of the band Rage Against the Machine. Still am... kinda. They are communists. Progressives. But I repeat myself...

I really can't stand them as human beings, but I'll be damned if they're not cool! When Tom Morello gets up there and starts going wild on his guitar, while Zac yells into the microphone next to him... My head starts involuntarily banging. I can't help it. Their music rocks.

And that Che Guevara shirt... I loved it. I felt kinda edgy wearing it. I didn't know the first thing about Che. It didn't matter; I liked Rage, and Rage said he was cool. So he was cool.

Communism has been flattered like this in the arts for generations. So much so that you are probably numb to it. You hardly even notice it anymore, like a fish swimming in water.

So how do we make it uncool? Well, that's up to the kids. It always has been. You and I don't get a vote. The democracy of cool belongs to the kids, and the kids alone.

And kids aren't watching TV or even listening to music the way that we used to. They're playing video games, doomscrolling social media and watching streamers.

And some of these streamers are massive. The biggest of them pull live audiences that dwarf cable news. Millions of young men, hanging on every word.

Hasan Piker is one of the biggest in America. An open communist.

Another is a man who goes by the name asmongold. One of the biggest streamers alive. Not a communist. Not even a political guy, really, just a gamer with millions of young men glued to him every night. He's been forced into the political sphere because he's starting to see the same thing you and I see. He sees the predator/prey dynamic, and the predatory nature of people like Hasan and his audience.

He's one of ours. He's an asset. Keep an eye on him.

If you want a good introduction, watch his reaction to Marco Rubio's speech here.

It's time to make Communism so uncool that it hurts.
