subject: are some people better than others?
preview: i still wrestle with this one... last night I made you wrestle with it too.
html:
Last night, I sent you guys a yes-or-no question. A test that I learned from Michael Malice.

"Are some people better than others?"

I didn't expect such a huge response, but I got it. The question really fired you guys up. I received more replies than I am able to handle. I read every single one of them, and am still reading them as they come in. If I didn't respond to you, I'm sorry; I just had too many, but know that I read what you wrote and appreciate the feedback.

But there was a recurring theme among your replies. Those of you who answered with a flat yes thought it was a great question and very revealing. Those of you who answered with a No, or a speech about equality and God... well, you were more uncomfortable with it. You didn't think it was a very good question; you gave me a lot of reasons as to why, but one of them stood out above all.

Almost everyone who disagreed with me said some version of the same thing... 'In the eyes of God, no one is better than anyone else.'

For me personally, I struggle with the question, but if you ask me to answer right away with a yes or no... My answer is yes. A flat yes is closer to what I intuitively believe than a flat no. That's just the truth. But I'd also be lying if I didn't tell you that I struggle with that answer as I reflect on it afterwards.

Here's a follow-up question I want to leave you with...

How do you think a progressive would answer that question? Do you think they would have a similar answer to you, or a different one?

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: a simple question
preview: are you right-wing or left-wing?
html:
A couple of days ago, I talked a little bit about one of my favorite authors, Michael Malice.

I mentioned some of his pithy quotes that have really helped me understand how people operate and think politically.

He has another tool I've found quite useful. It's a simple test to see if someone is left-wing or right-wing.

It's a simple yes-or-no question. It works best if you ask someone in a live conversation, where they don't have time to pause and think. The idea is that you have to answer it right away... and through that answer we can determine if you are left-wing or right-wing with 100% accuracy.

Are you ready? Here's the question:

Are some people better than others? Yes or no.

....

Okay... have your answer?

Now, let's find out what you are...

If you answered Yes with no qualifications... Congratulations, you are right-wing! If you answered with no, or went off on a speech... you are left-wing.

Here's the reasoning: Reality has a hierarchy, whether you admit it or not. Are some people better at hockey than others? Yes. Are some people better looking than others? Yes. Are some people better people than others? No matter how you slice it, some people are better than others.

A proper right-winger has no problem acknowledging this reality. A left-winger, on the other hand, feels the need to give a speech about equality.

They do this because they think that's what you're SUPPOSED to believe. And they're right, according to the progressive orthodoxy.

But the truth is, they're just setting up their own hierarchy. The man who says no one is better isn't being humble. He thinks he's better than you for saying it. It's a moral hierarchy that they construct for themselves, where they get to be at the top.

That's the logic.

What do you think? Is it a good test?

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I'm working relentlessly on my upcoming Charlie Kirk piece. That's all I'll be doing until it's done. Just wanted you to know that.

subject: Lindsey Graham
preview: I didn't think I would feel this way
html:
So, by now you've heard. Lindsey Graham is dead. Passed away suddenly on Saturday evening after a trip to Ukraine. There's video of him speaking on camera just a day before his death, and he seems fine. Healthy, even.

It's quite a shock to a lot of people. Even the President was choked up... and here's the part that caught me completely off guard. So was I. I was sad to hear Lindsey Graham had died! I couldn't even believe it myself.

You see, I was a libertarian through most of my political life. Until very recently. And every libertarian builds their reputation on bashing people like Lindsey Graham. The "warmongers," as we would call them.

Lindsey was a total hawk on foreign policy. I don't think he ever met a foreign conflict he didn't want to drag America into. To a Libertarian, this is a grievous sin. Worse than being a communist or a socialist. Worse than supporting the welfare state, worse than Mamdani and AOC. Lindsey Graham represented the worst of the worst.

I don't see it that way anymore. It's not even a choice I made. It was an involuntary reaction I observed in myself... When he died on Saturday, I was sad. Legitimately bummed out about it.

So now I have to ask myself... why?

Well, the first thing I noticed is that all of the progressives I keep my eyes on could barely contain their glee. They were dancing on Lindsey's grave much like how they were dancing on Charlie's. That's a red flag for me. When I see my enemies dancing on someone's grave, I immediately assume the person in the ground must have done something good.

If there's one thing I've learned, it's to never, ever, give the progressives the benefit of the doubt when they're grave-dancing.

But that's not why I was sad. If anything, this stuff made me mad. The reason I was sad is that, lately, I've come to realize that my highest political value is loyalty to the MAGA alliance. Not my principles, or my policy preferences... the alliance that stands against a total progressive takeover of everything. Building and strengthening this alliance, to me, is the only political project that matters right now.

Lindsey understood something the libertarian never will. He was playing a team sport. He showed up for the Alliance, cheerful and determined, and he never stopped fighting for the win, even standing beside people who hated half of his positions and said nasty things about him.

Here's what Lindsey said about Blake Masters when one of Blake's donors asked:

Senator Graham why are you helping Blake, given how much you two disagree on foreign policy?

And according to Blake, Graham responded with this:

“So Blake’s wrong about Ukraine... who gives a shit? We aren’t here to talk about how correct I am all the time, we’re here to talk about getting the Senate majority. Because I want to be chairman of my committees!”

That's why, to my own surprise, I'll miss him. I think we lost something with Lindsey. I cannot believe I'm saying this. The old me would've never believed you if you told him this.

Stay close,

~ Clay

subject: what do i need to say
preview: to get you to do what I want
html:
Michael Malice is one of my favorite writers, and someone who has greatly influenced my own perspective. Have you heard of him?

His book "The White Pill" is one that I highly recommend. It's a history of the Soviet Union.

It's not a dense account of historical details and facts; it's a story that will punch you in the gut over and over, like a great movie. I will admit, I was moved to tears at several points in the book. The whole point is to show you that even the most brutal, seemingly permanent totalitarian regimes can be defeated by ordinary human resilience. There is always a reason to have hope...

But I'm not writing this email to sell you on a book...

I wanted to bring up Michael because he is particularly good at using his high-functioning Russian brain to come up with pithy phrases that have really helped me understand how political games work, in reality.

Here is one of my favorites. Write it down... ruminate on it. Keep it in your back pocket.

"What do I need to say to get you to do what I want?" ~ Michael Malice

You know how when you're in a political argument with someone, you expose a brazen hypocrisy, and they seem completely unaffected by it? Almost like they don't even notice it?

Well, the phrase above explains the mode they are operating from. The goal isn't to be correct; it's to get you to do what they want. So... when you're busy getting angry at them, telling them off in the comments, being offended by what they said, spending your precious time writing a thoughtful reply... think about it. Are you just giving that person what they wanted? Are you being played?

As I started to ask myself that question, I started to realize just how much time I was wasting talking to people who were not actually listening to a word I said. I was being played constantly.

"They don't use language to communicate but to manipulate." ~ Michael Malice

This is what you're up against. You're not in a debate; you're in a fight with someone who fights dirty.

So, see it clearly. Know what you're up against. Identify the traps and navigate around them... and remember...

There is always a reason to have hope.

Stay close,

~ Clay

P.S. I am currently deep in my Charlie Kirk piece. It's all I will be working on until it's done. This will be the most serious piece I've ever written. My life will be consumed by it until it is done... just wanted you to know that.

P.P.S. This whole email was about people who won't tell you what they want... so I'll do the opposite. I want you to support me, so I can keep writing full-time. No ads, no sponsors, ever. I am 100% reader supported, which means you're the only thing keeping the project alive. If it's worth something to you: send a tip, or become a member.

subject: it's just envy and resentment
preview: it's not any more complicated than that
html:
I woke up at about 8 a.m. this morning and went for a walk with my dog in a sunny field. It was beautiful. I turned on a podcast. The Tom Woods Show. You may remember me going after Tom in my Thomas Massie piece.

Well, I'm still a listener. I keep my eye on Tom. He still does a lot of good work, despite some of my frustrations with him.

He had a guy named Keith Knight on the show to discuss his recent video on Democratic Socialism. Keith made a monster 4-hour-long video taking apart every single argument the Democratic Socialists make, with precision.

It's excellent; I skimmed through it... I can tell he spent a lot of time on it. The interview with Tom Woods is excellent too.

You know what else it was? A waste of time. Infotainment for libertarians and nothing else.

Why do I say this? Well, if you've read me for a while now, you should already have a sense of it. The libertarian thinks he's in a debate, when he's really in a fight. The libertarian spends his life making 4-hour rebuttals to people who never intended to listen. Keith and Tom even address this in the interview, right at the beginning. No one who needs to listen to it will...

So what's the point of making it, then?

The truth is, you can't take anything the Democratic Socialists say at face value. They don't actually believe anything. It's just envy and resentment pretending to be an economic theory. It doesn't go any deeper than that.

You're effectively dealing with a criminal who wants to rob you, but instead of pointing a gun in your face, they develop a whole 'theory' where they have the moral right to demand the government put its gun in your face.

That's it. That's what "Democratic Socialism" is. It's not any deeper than that.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I appreciate all the prayers that were sent to me last night. It means a lot, and I will need them as I continue to work on my piece about Charlie Kirk.

subject: almost bought a guitar today
preview: then i didn't
html:
I've had my eye on this guitar on Facebook marketplace for a while. I messaged the seller a week ago, telling him I wanted to meet up and try it out. Well, today we were finally able to arrange it.

I drove over to his house, cash in hand, fully intending to buy it. I sat down, I started to play it... and I just wasn't feeling it. I can't even explain it. The guitar was beautiful; there was nothing wrong with it. The seller was a good guy, totally trustworthy. I just didn't fall in love with it, and I'm not going to spend good money on a guitar I don't love.

I've been stewing on it all day since... the old me would've settled. Would've bought the guitar, set it up, and probably would've been reasonably satisfied with it. The new me doesn't think like that. I either love it, or I don't do it. I don't have the time or the money for things I don't love anymore.

And I love writing. I love that you love my writing. And because of that love, I will throw out completed pieces that don't meet my standard. That don't make me feel that thing I need to feel before I show it to you. The thing I wanted to feel when I picked up that guitar is the same thing I need to feel when a piece is completed.

I'm working towards meeting that standard for you

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. I'm going to be deeply embedded in all things Charlie Kirk for the foreseeable future. I will be writing to you every day through the process. Send some love to my wall, I read every one.

subject: i watched a judge flinch
preview: he had to watch a close up of charlie's assassination
html:
Yesterday I told you that I'm working on another piece about Charlie Kirk. That's true, I am. But today, I just couldn't find the right words to write, and so I didn't push myself. If there's one thing I've learned in my short career as a writer, it's that you cannot force inspiration. The readers will sense it, and so will I.

I don't want to attach my name to anything I had to force. The realness of what I write is what's most important to me, and I think it's what's most important to you as one of my readers.

You have to wait for it to come, and it shows up when you aren't expecting it.

So, today, I just kind of took it easy. I lifted weights, went for a nice walk in the sun, listened to some Rolling Stones.... had a much-needed nap. Just letting my head clear a bit.

Then I got back on the computer in the evening... and I see that the preliminary hearings have begun for the Charlie Kirk murder trial. Everyone's talking about it. Then one clip shows up in my feed that brought me back to September 10th, 2025.

Do you remember when you first saw it? The clip of him being shot. I do. Vividly. I gasped... I said "no, no, no, no" repeatedly. I talked to my Dad about it, and he was hopeful. He hadn't seen the video; he just heard Charlie had been shot. I wanted to share in his hope, but I knew what I saw. There was not going to be a happy ending.

I'm recalling all of this because today, in the hearings, the judge had to watch the close-up of Charlie being shot in the courtroom. His reaction is on camera. He flinches. You can see the repeated "no, no, no" all over his face.

I don't know what to do with all this. I feel as though a message is being delivered to me... the inspiration to continue this article... but I just need to put it together.

So that's where I'm at tonight. Patiently waiting for that spark to hit, so I can write an article I'm proud to show you.

stay close,

~ Clay

p.s. here's the clip of the judge I am referring to.

subject: an exceptional country
preview: thank you america for leading the world
html:
Happy 250th Birthday, America!

Thank you for being the best neighbor a country could ask for.

Let me tell you a little about myself. I am Canadian. Sorry, eh? I have lived within a couple of hours of the US Border my entire life. My grandfather fought in World War 2 alongside Americans. I’ve done business in America. 90% of my readers are American. I have friends and family there.

Our two countries have had one of the strongest relationships any two nations have ever shared in the history of the world.

And the world loves to dunk on you. They blame you for everything wrong on the planet. They tell you you're backwards, behind the times, in need of catching up.

Well, America. It’s not you who is backwards. It’s us. We all live in your shadow, and we are better off for it.

The rest of the world won’t say it, but I will, because it’s plainly true for those who have eyes to see.

You carry the world on your shoulders in a hundred ways, and here's one nobody will admit.

Health Care.

That’s right. You’ve probably heard it all, if you’ve spent any time online. There’s been award winning Hollywood movies about it, even. Remember Michael Moore’s “Sicko”? He actually tried to convince people that Cuba’s health care system was morally superior to America’s.

I’m not kidding. This isn’t hyperbole. And you know what? He convinced a lot of people. He even convinced a much younger version of me… for a while.

But believe it or not, the morbidly obese communist in a baseball cap wasn’t telling you the whole truth. Neither are the people of the world who’ve bought into the kind of propaganda he’s selling.

You want to know the truth about America’s contribution to health care?

America has won more Nobel Prizes in Medicine than any nation on earth. There isn’t a close second.

America invents more than half of all the new medicine on earth. More than every other country on the planet combined. The drug that saves your Canadian life, the treatment that saves your European kid… odds are it was born in an American lab.

Americans are a tiny slice of the world's patients, but they foot roughly half the world's medicine bill. Every "free" system, including Cuba's, including Europe’s… including mine, is riding on it.

They like to say things like “America is the only developed country without universal health care”, when the truth is, America is the one pulling above its weight and subsidizing revolutionary health care products and services for the entire world.

America’s health care system has its faults, and is far from perfect… but it is the most compassionate and innovative health care system in the history of this planet, and that’s not a bad start.

God Bless You America. Here’s to 250 more years of excellence.

~ Clay

subject: Don't Give Thomas Sowell the Medal of Freedom
preview: he needs an army, not a medal
html:
🎧 Audio version is available on the website here

Don't Give Thomas Sowell the Medal of Freedom

"Thomas Sowell is a genius. Listen to him." ~ Charlie Kirk, 2020

I hear it all the time. Rarely does a week go by without someone messaging me about how I should start a petition for Thomas Sowell to receive the Medal of Freedom. People send me their own petitions, their own videos and articles making the case, asking me to share it… and I often do!

I get it. You want to honor the man. You want to show everyone how great he is, and how much you respect him. I feel the same way. He's given us so much, let's give him a little something back, right? Let him know it was all worth it.

And yet… with all the asking, all the petitions, all the years, there's still no medal, and no real reason to believe it's going to happen any time soon.

Why do we even care? Why is it so important to us?

I've been asking myself this question a lot lately, as the calls to honor him with the Medal of Freedom intensify. I'm as guilty of this as anyone. I've written my own piece making the case, and it went viral. If I shared it again today, it'd almost certainly go viral again.

Others have done bigger numbers than I have with the same idea, but they didn't achieve anything either.

But let's imagine for a second that we were successful… that the Trump Administration hears our call and honors it. They invite Thomas Sowell to the White House to receive the Medal of Freedom.

What would that look like? Picture it. Thomas Sowell standing there. Ninety-six years old, surrounded by the very class of people he spent sixty years exposing for exactly what they are. And now they want him to stand beside them and smile for the camera…

What makes you think Thomas Sowell even wants this "honor"?

I can't speak for him, and I would never try. I have no affiliation with him, and I doubt he even knows I exist. But, I can speculate as someone who has spent an unseemly amount of time consuming his work.

Everything I've watched and read tells me he wouldn't care about this medal. Not even a little. In fact, I think he would be annoyed by the suggestion that he would have to go to DC and mingle with the political class to receive it. It wouldn't even surprise me if he'd turn it down.

Have you seen what Thomas Sowell writes about these people? Seriously, what makes you think he wants to be honored by them, or spend any of his precious moments at 96 around them?

If it were possible to enforce a ban on lying, a ghastly silence would fall over the city of Washington.
~ Thomas Sowell • The Thomas Sowell Reader, 2011

Are you ready for a hard truth?

The calls for him to get the medal were never really about him. It's about you… and me. It's about making us feel good, like we are "doing something". It's pure ceremony. Pageantry. There's no power in it. In terms of realpolitik, it's completely unserious. The more I think about it, the amount of time we spend on this reveals why our side loses everything.

Because here's what we do… we chase the recognition instead of power. Ceremony over conquest. We would rather be told we were right than actually win.

If you want to see exactly what this medal is, look at who already has one. George Soros. Hillary Clinton. Megan Rapinoe… to name a few.

Are these the kinds of people you would put Thomas Sowell next to? Are we honoring him by giving him the same award Hillary Clinton already received? Are we really begging for him to be an equal with Megan Rapinoe?… Is it possible we're actually insulting him and his legacy with this gesture? Doesn't he deserve something greater?

The funny thing is, he has been offered greater things… do you know how he handled them?

Let's go back to 1981. Ronald Reagan was just elected President, and he wanted Sowell in the room. He put him on his Economic Policy Advisory Board. This wasn't just a room full of no-name bureaucrats, this was the big leagues. George Shultz, Alan Greenspan, Art Laffer and Milton Friedman himself. The most influential economic minds in the country, advising the President directly.

A seat like that is what an entire career is supposed to be building toward.

Do you know what Sowell did?

He went to one meeting. Then he resigned.

Why? He told us himself. He cited his mentor, Milton Friedman:

Some people can contribute more by staying out of government

One day… that's it. He didn't need any more information than that one single day to know it wasn't for him.

That's who he is. He never wanted a seat at their table.

So think about what we're actually doing when we beg the political class to recognize this man. Our hero. We're begging the people whose table he walked away from to hand him a ribbon. Sure, it's a nice gesture, but it's really not that important.

You know what is important? Power.

"The most basic question is not what is best, it's who decides what is best."
~ Thomas Sowell • Knowledge and Decisions, 1980

Every political question comes down to this. We spend so much time arguing about what the correct policies are, we don't stop to consider whether we have the power to decide any of it. What's the point of having correct opinions, if you have no power to implement them?

While we're spending our time circulating petitions, let's talk about how the other side honors their heroes. Do they ask for permission? No. They take territory, claim it as their own and then force you to obey.

Take black history month, for example. When's the last time you saw Thomas Sowell honored by anyone who celebrates black history month? Why is that?

Black history month, just like the Black Lives Matter movement and Saint George Floyd himself, are sanctified by the regime. They are weapons. Tools used to control you. A leash put around your neck. And the second you pull against it, they give it a tug. "Racist!" "Uncle Tom!"… Get back in line…

"The word 'racism' is like ketchup. It can be put on practically anything, and demanding evidence makes you a 'racist.'"

~ Thomas Sowell • A Political Glossary, 2012

So why is Thomas Sowell never honored? Because it was never about black excellence. If it were, he'd be the face of it, right next to Clarence Thomas and Ben Carson… but these aren't the right kind of blacks, for some reason.

If a black Supreme Court Justice and a literal brain surgeon who made medical history do not qualify… what does that tell you?

It's really about the leash.

It was never about racism, it was always about power.

So let's talk about power. Real power isn't in a medal. It's in who gets to decide who's sacred. Who gets to say a man is holy, that attacking him is a sin and that honoring him is mandatory. That is real power, built through the conquest of the institutions.

The progressives understand this intimately. Our side does not.

Ask yourself… what power was there in elevating George Floyd to Sainthood? Well, now the regime gets the power to excuse riots, sanctify disorder, and make criticism socially punishable.

What power was there in elevating Martin Luther King to a martyr?

The power to decide what is good and what is evil for an entire generation.

That's real power. Compare that to your little fantasy about a Medal of Freedom ceremony. We don't have to imagine what that would look like… we just had one.

Charlie Kirk received the Medal of Freedom posthumously. They had a ceremony. I watched the whole thing live. It was very nice. Erika Kirk was there, she received it for him and gave a very moving speech. Charlie's parents were there. My heart sank just looking at them. You can see the pain in their faces. They're never going to get over this… neither am I. Neither should you.

These people who are coming around shooting people and calling them fascists are so ignorant that they don't even know what the fascists were doing. But Charlie Kirk went around talking to people, trying to convince them. Fascists don't do that. Fascists shoot people.

~ Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

America should not get over Charlie Kirk, just as it did not get over MLK.

One of these men was honored with a medal. The other with a Nation.

Our enemies have their eye on the prize, and they're playing for keeps. We get distracted by things that don't matter. To them, throwing a Medal to a political ally is a trivial matter. An afterthought. Something they can do on a whim. To us, it's something we expend endless energy begging for.

Do you see the difference? It's time to stop begging, and start taking.

So stop staring at the medal. Stop putting so much energy into trying to get petitions started for it. It's not a priority for me, I'm pretty sure it's not a priority for Thomas Sowell, and it shouldn't be a priority for you. I'm sorry to put it so bluntly, I know your heart is in the right place, but it's time to get serious.

And so, here we are on the precipice of a new age. New revolutionary technologies are emerging, old powers are being disrupted, and grand new opportunities are in front of us, but you need clear eyes to see them… and you can bet that our friends, the progressives, are out hunting for these opportunities right now too.

So how do we beat them this time? Well, I'll tell you this. It's not with ceremony and medals. It's not going to be that easy.

You don't honor these great men of history with trophies, you honor them by using their legacy to take power from their enemies and give it to their friends, and the descendants of their friends.

We honor Charlie Kirk and Thomas Sowell by pursuing the progressives like we are pursuing an indictment. We remove them from the institutions, and replace them with our own people. With people who think like Charlie and Thomas.

But I'm going to be real with you. I'm not going to sell you a fantasy. We might lose. In fact, that is the most likely outcome. But, so what? We are in pursuit of the good, the true and the beautiful. We are correct. Thomas Sowell is correct. Charlie Kirk was correct.

But they lost. That's the tough pill that we have to swallow. We're losing too. The progressives still own the institutions, even in a Trump administration.

"I do think that there is a very serious chance that we are doomed."

~ Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

That's not exactly what you wanted to hear, is it? Well, so what. Toughen up. We're going to fight anyway. Thomas Sowell has carried this fight on his shoulders for more decades than I care to count. He lost. He hasn't stopped, even well into his nineties.

It's not over. We're not dead, yet. It's our duty to honor the fight that these great men have fought, by continuing when they cannot. This is harder than any medal. This has real costs. Look at Charlie.

So, if you're still here, you're still breathing, and you want to know how you can honor the 96 year old man whose birthday we are celebrating? Get to work. Stop begging. Improve yourself, find your edge, and start accumulating wins, however small.

Start thinking like a predator, not prey.

Wherever there were people who were vulnerable, for whatever reason, those were the people who were preyed upon.

~ Thomas Sowell • C-SPAN Q&A with Brian Lamb, 2005

And so, this is the lesson. The harsh reality. Politics is not a debate club. The "marketplace of ideas" is not a marketplace at all. It is a battlefield. You are in a fight for the future of your country, and whoever wins gets everything.

The winner gets to decide who your grandchildren learn about, and who they never hear of. They get to define what is good and what is evil for the next hundred years, and raise future generations in their own image.

We either take it from them, or they keep it. There is either regime change, or the progressives take this century just like they took the last one. Those are the stakes.

So, what are you going to do about it? What can you do about it?

You'll have to figure that out for yourself, but I can tell you exactly what I'm doing.

I'm following in the footsteps of the best teacher I ever had. A man who doesn't even know I exist. I am internalizing the lessons he gave us, just as he internalized the lessons of great thinkers before him.

Sowell ignored the noise, put his head down and just kept writing for decades. Through that work he has inspired millions, including one of the greatest Supreme Court Justices in history.

And so, I'm going to take my own shot at that. I left my software engineering career to write full time. I'm going to put my head down and write, every day, just like Sowell did. I am developing my own doctrine, I call it "Stop Being Prey".

You will have to find your own path, but whatever it is, you don't get to sit this out. You either figure out how to stop being prey or figure out how you're going to submit to your predators. There is no third option.

Thomas Sowell is 96. He doesn't know you exist. He'll never know you signed a petition for him to get a medal. So get over it and start fighting.

He lit the flame, now it's our responsibility to carry his torch into the fight for the future.

At the end of his most recent interview, Sowell didn't reach for his own words. He reached back, to a man who came before him, and read this.

If I could think that I had sent a spark to those who come after, I should be ready to say goodbye.

~ Oliver Wendell Holmes • read by Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

stay close
~ Clay

p.s. If this piece moved you, send it to someone who needs to read it. Here's a link that works anywhere: stopbeingprey.com/medal-of-freedom

p.p.s. If you want to be a part of my work, and hang out with my supporters and me on the inside... here's the door.

subject: i found the motherlode
preview: more thomas sowell quotes are coming
html:
It's always weird the day after I release one of my big pieces. I've been working so hard on it for so long that I almost feel lost when it's done. I don't quite know what to do with myself.

Today I've kind of been taking it easy. Last night, we had a thunderstorm. My dog doesn't like those very much at all. He kept me up most of the night. And so, I had spent a good chunk of the day today napping.

I feel good now, ready to get to work... but on what? Well, to write the Sowell piece, I did a bunch of deep research into the man. I re-watched a ton of his interviews, re-read his columns. All kinds of stuff like that. I've been deep in Sowell's work for the last week. You know what I discovered?

There are a ton of GREAT Sowell quotes from interviews that have never been transcribed properly and mined. All kinds of gold that has never been made into memes and images for the internet age.

Can you guess what I'm going to do next?

I already built the Watch page for ReadSowell.com. Where I'm collecting all of his great interviews and putting them in one easy-to-use spot. Next, I'm going to transcribe them all properly, with top-tier paid transcription tools, and then start unearthing more viral gems for you guys to read and spread out into the world.

Seems like the right thing to do for the time being. I talked a lot in the piece about how we should honor the man going forward. Well, this is my way of doing that.

Expect to see some fresh quotes on the page coming soon.

subject: happy 96th birthday thomas sowell!
preview: do not give him the medal of freedom
html:
🎧 Audio version is available on the website here

Don't Give Thomas Sowell the Medal of Freedom

"Thomas Sowell is a genius. Listen to him." ~ Charlie Kirk, 2020

I hear it all the time. Rarely does a week go by without someone messaging me about how I should start a petition for Thomas Sowell to receive the Medal of Freedom. People send me their own petitions, their own videos and articles making the case, asking me to share it… and I often do!

I get it. You want to honor the man. You want to show everyone how great he is, and how much you respect him. I feel the same way. He's given us so much, let's give him a little something back, right? Let him know it was all worth it.

And yet… with all the asking, all the petitions, all the years, there's still no medal, and no real reason to believe it's going to happen any time soon.

Why do we even care? Why is it so important to us?

I've been asking myself this question a lot lately, as the calls to honor him with the Medal of Freedom intensify. I'm as guilty of this as anyone. I've written my own piece making the case, and it went viral. If I shared it again today, it'd almost certainly go viral again.

Others have done bigger numbers than I have with the same idea, but they didn't achieve anything either.

But let's imagine for a second that we were successful… that the Trump Administration hears our call and honors it. They invite Thomas Sowell to the White House to receive the Medal of Freedom.

What would that look like? Picture it. Thomas Sowell standing there. Ninety-six years old, surrounded by the very class of people he spent sixty years exposing for exactly what they are. And now they want him to stand beside them and smile for the camera…

What makes you think Thomas Sowell even wants this "honor"?

I can't speak for him, and I would never try. I have no affiliation with him, and I doubt he even knows I exist. But, I can speculate as someone who has spent an unseemly amount of time consuming his work.

Everything I've watched and read tells me he wouldn't care about this medal. Not even a little. In fact, I think he would be annoyed by the suggestion that he would have to go to DC and mingle with the political class to receive it. It wouldn't even surprise me if he'd turn it down.

Have you seen what Thomas Sowell writes about these people? Seriously, what makes you think he wants to be honored by them, or spend any of his precious moments at 96 around them?

If it were possible to enforce a ban on lying, a ghastly silence would fall over the city of Washington.
~ Thomas Sowell • The Thomas Sowell Reader, 2011

Are you ready for a hard truth?

The calls for him to get the medal were never really about him. It's about you… and me. It's about making us feel good, like we are "doing something". It's pure ceremony. Pageantry. There's no power in it. In terms of realpolitik, it's completely unserious. The more I think about it, the amount of time we spend on this reveals why our side loses everything.

Because here's what we do… we chase the recognition instead of power. Ceremony over conquest. We would rather be told we were right than actually win.

If you want to see exactly what this medal is, look at who already has one. George Soros. Hillary Clinton. Megan Rapinoe… to name a few.

Are these the kinds of people you would put Thomas Sowell next to? Are we honoring him by giving him the same award Hillary Clinton already received? Are we really begging for him to be an equal with Megan Rapinoe?… Is it possible we're actually insulting him and his legacy with this gesture? Doesn't he deserve something greater?

The funny thing is, he has been offered greater things… do you know how he handled them?

Let's go back to 1981. Ronald Reagan was just elected President, and he wanted Sowell in the room. He put him on his Economic Policy Advisory Board. This wasn't just a room full of no-name bureaucrats, this was the big leagues. George Shultz, Alan Greenspan, Art Laffer and Milton Friedman himself. The most influential economic minds in the country, advising the President directly.

A seat like that is what an entire career is supposed to be building toward.

Do you know what Sowell did?

He went to one meeting. Then he resigned.

Why? He told us himself. He cited his mentor, Milton Friedman:

Some people can contribute more by staying out of government

One day… that's it. He didn't need any more information than that one single day to know it wasn't for him.

That's who he is. He never wanted a seat at their table.

So think about what we're actually doing when we beg the political class to recognize this man. Our hero. We're begging the people whose table he walked away from to hand him a ribbon. Sure, it's a nice gesture, but it's really not that important.

You know what is important? Power.

"The most basic question is not what is best, it's who decides what is best."
~ Thomas Sowell • Knowledge and Decisions, 1980

Every political question comes down to this. We spend so much time arguing about what the correct policies are, we don't stop to consider whether we have the power to decide any of it. What's the point of having correct opinions, if you have no power to implement them?

While we're spending our time circulating petitions, let's talk about how the other side honors their heroes. Do they ask for permission? No. They take territory, claim it as their own and then force you to obey.

Take black history month, for example. When's the last time you saw Thomas Sowell honored by anyone who celebrates black history month? Why is that?

Black history month, just like the Black Lives Matter movement and Saint George Floyd himself, are sanctified by the regime. They are weapons. Tools used to control you. A leash put around your neck. And the second you pull against it, they give it a tug. "Racist!" "Uncle Tom!"… Get back in line…

"The word 'racism' is like ketchup. It can be put on practically anything, and demanding evidence makes you a 'racist.'"

~ Thomas Sowell • A Political Glossary, 2012

So why is Thomas Sowell never honored? Because it was never about black excellence. If it were, he'd be the face of it, right next to Clarence Thomas and Ben Carson… but these aren't the right kind of blacks, for some reason.

If a black Supreme Court Justice and a literal brain surgeon who made medical history do not qualify… what does that tell you?

It's really about the leash.

It was never about racism, it was always about power.

So let's talk about power. Real power isn't in a medal. It's in who gets to decide who's sacred. Who gets to say a man is holy, that attacking him is a sin and that honoring him is mandatory. That is real power, built through the conquest of the institutions.

The progressives understand this intimately. Our side does not.

Ask yourself… what power was there in elevating George Floyd to Sainthood? Well, now the regime gets the power to excuse riots, sanctify disorder, and make criticism socially punishable.

What power was there in elevating Martin Luther King to a martyr?

The power to decide what is good and what is evil for an entire generation.

That's real power. Compare that to your little fantasy about a Medal of Freedom ceremony. We don't have to imagine what that would look like… we just had one.

Charlie Kirk received the Medal of Freedom posthumously. They had a ceremony. I watched the whole thing live. It was very nice. Erika Kirk was there, she received it for him and gave a very moving speech. Charlie's parents were there. My heart sank just looking at them. You can see the pain in their faces. They're never going to get over this… neither am I. Neither should you.

These people who are coming around shooting people and calling them fascists are so ignorant that they don't even know what the fascists were doing. But Charlie Kirk went around talking to people, trying to convince them. Fascists don't do that. Fascists shoot people.

~ Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

America should not get over Charlie Kirk, just as it did not get over MLK.

One of these men was honored with a medal. The other with a Nation.

Our enemies have their eye on the prize, and they're playing for keeps. We get distracted by things that don't matter. To them, throwing a Medal to a political ally is a trivial matter. An afterthought. Something they can do on a whim. To us, it's something we expend endless energy begging for.

Do you see the difference? It's time to stop begging, and start taking.

So stop staring at the medal. Stop putting so much energy into trying to get petitions started for it. It's not a priority for me, I'm pretty sure it's not a priority for Thomas Sowell, and it shouldn't be a priority for you. I'm sorry to put it so bluntly, I know your heart is in the right place, but it's time to get serious.

And so, here we are on the precipice of a new age. New revolutionary technologies are emerging, old powers are being disrupted, and grand new opportunities are in front of us, but you need clear eyes to see them… and you can bet that our friends, the progressives, are out hunting for these opportunities right now too.

So how do we beat them this time? Well, I'll tell you this. It's not with ceremony and medals. It's not going to be that easy.

You don't honor these great men of history with trophies, you honor them by using their legacy to take power from their enemies and give it to their friends, and the descendants of their friends.

We honor Charlie Kirk and Thomas Sowell by pursuing the progressives like we are pursuing an indictment. We remove them from the institutions, and replace them with our own people. With people who think like Charlie and Thomas.

But I'm going to be real with you. I'm not going to sell you a fantasy. We might lose. In fact, that is the most likely outcome. But, so what? We are in pursuit of the good, the true and the beautiful. We are correct. Thomas Sowell is correct. Charlie Kirk was correct.

But they lost. That's the tough pill that we have to swallow. We're losing too. The progressives still own the institutions, even in a Trump administration.

"I do think that there is a very serious chance that we are doomed."

~ Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

That's not exactly what you wanted to hear, is it? Well, so what. Toughen up. We're going to fight anyway. Thomas Sowell has carried this fight on his shoulders for more decades than I care to count. He lost. He hasn't stopped, even well into his nineties.

It's not over. We're not dead, yet. It's our duty to honor the fight that these great men have fought, by continuing when they cannot. This is harder than any medal. This has real costs. Look at Charlie.

So, if you're still here, you're still breathing, and you want to know how you can honor the 96 year old man whose birthday we are celebrating? Get to work. Stop begging. Improve yourself, find your edge, and start accumulating wins, however small.

Start thinking like a predator, not prey.

Wherever there were people who were vulnerable, for whatever reason, those were the people who were preyed upon.

~ Thomas Sowell • C-SPAN Q&A with Brian Lamb, 2005

And so, this is the lesson. The harsh reality. Politics is not a debate club. The "marketplace of ideas" is not a marketplace at all. It is a battlefield. You are in a fight for the future of your country, and whoever wins gets everything.

The winner gets to decide who your grandchildren learn about, and who they never hear of. They get to define what is good and what is evil for the next hundred years, and raise future generations in their own image.

We either take it from them, or they keep it. There is either regime change, or the progressives take this century just like they took the last one. Those are the stakes.

So, what are you going to do about it? What can you do about it?

You'll have to figure that out for yourself, but I can tell you exactly what I'm doing.

I'm following in the footsteps of the best teacher I ever had. A man who doesn't even know I exist. I am internalizing the lessons he gave us, just as he internalized the lessons of great thinkers before him.

Sowell ignored the noise, put his head down and just kept writing for decades. Through that work he has inspired millions, including one of the greatest Supreme Court Justices in history.

And so, I'm going to take my own shot at that. I left my software engineering career to write full time. I'm going to put my head down and write, every day, just like Sowell did. I am developing my own doctrine, I call it "Stop Being Prey".

You will have to find your own path, but whatever it is, you don't get to sit this out. You either figure out how to stop being prey or figure out how you're going to submit to your predators. There is no third option.

Thomas Sowell is 96. He doesn't know you exist. He'll never know you signed a petition for him to get a medal. So get over it and start fighting.

He lit the flame, now it's our responsibility to carry his torch into the fight for the future.

At the end of his most recent interview, Sowell didn't reach for his own words. He reached back, to a man who came before him, and read this.

If I could think that I had sent a spark to those who come after, I should be ready to say goodbye.

~ Oliver Wendell Holmes • read by Thomas Sowell • Uncommon Knowledge (Hoover), 2025

stay close
~ Clay

p.s. If this piece moved you, send it to someone who needs to read it. Here's a link that works anywhere: stopbeingprey.com/medal-of-freedom

p.p.s. If you want to be a part of my work, and hang out with my supporters and me on the inside... here's the door.

subject: thomas sowell is even better than I realized
preview: and I already thought he was the man!
html:
The day after tomorrow Sowell will be a 96 year old man. Isn't that incredible? What a gift it is to still have this man with us, and still doing interviews with a sound mind! His most recent one was back in January.

By the way, you can find that video, as well as nearly every other interview he's ever done on my new watch page on ReadSowell.com.

I'm deep into my Sowell piece right now. It will be coming out either tomorrow or the day after. We will see. While writing it and doing deep research on the man, especially tonight, I am realizing that he is so much cooler than I ever thought, and I already thought he was pretty cool!

I always thought of him as an economist. A free market guy who could explain to those silly socialists how the world really works. And he is that, don't get me wrong. He's one of the best to ever do it.

But he's actually something much better than just an economist. Good free market economists are a dime a dozen, really.

Sowell is into real, cold power analysis. While he's certainly expressed sympathies with libertarianism, he's not driven by it as a core value. He was never an ideologue who centered his politics around a morality play.

Everybody else, left and right, argues about what the right answer is. Sowell's deepest question was never "what's right." It was who gets to decide, and who pays when they're wrong. There are no right answers, there are only tradeoffs... to paraphrase him.

The man is a proper predator. Always was.

The best teacher I ever had, and he doesn't even know who I am.

God bless him,

~ Clay

p.s. I'm working tirelessly to get this piece right. I won't stop until it's done. This one is very important to me, and I am a little nervous about how some people might respond. That's usually how I know it's going to resonate.

subject: have you tried virtual reality?
preview: me and my 75 year old dad play together.
html:
Hope your Friday is going well!

Tonight, I spent some time in virtual reality with my Dad and my friend Steve. We play this mini golf game; it's a really fun way to stay connected.

My Dad has never been a gamer. Videogames weren't his thing, but a few years ago I bought a Quest 2 VR headset for myself and showed him the minigolf game, and he totally fell in love with it. You know what he did? He immediately went out and bought a headset of his own.

At the time, I was living about 5 hours away from him. My Dad and I did not see each other very often, and to be honest, when we would get on the phone on rare occasions, we didn't have much to say to each other other than the same old things we've talked about dozens of times before.

But with these new VR headsets, we finally had a reason to talk. It's almost as if we were in a room together. We would regularly start playing mini-golf every single week, and it has genuinely improved our relationship. It keeps us connected, having fun together, and gives us a reason to talk without it feeling forced.

So, if you love someone, and you want to connect with them more... find something you can enjoy together. It helps!

That's all.

~ Clay

subject: that feeling of utter dread
preview: the conversation that started this whole thing
html:
The year was 2015, and there I was in my house, feeling utter dread as I saw another text alert come in from my cousin on my phone. It was the length of an essay. I stared at it for a while, I didn't even want to open it. We were in a political argument that had been going on for days at this point, and it was only elevating in its intensity.

Let me tell you a little about my cousin. I'll call him Matt. Growing up, Matt was like a brother to me. One of my best friends. Regular sleepovers, hangouts and brutal mini-stick hockey tournaments. Every family event was a treat because I knew he'd be there, and we'd have the best time getting into trouble together.

As we grew older, into our late teens and early adulthood, we always remained close but not quite as close as those childhood years. In all honesty, Matt was just a more ambitious guy than I was. He's an impressive person, ridiculously competent at anything he puts his mind to. Even when it comes to guitar, both of us played since our teens… but he is leagues ahead of me in terms of skill.

He has a more impressive career than me, he's always been better with women and he can command the presence of a room, I can't. This is all easy for me to admit, because it's all plainly true. But there's one area where I cannot concede to him, and that's on our understanding of politics and economics.

You see, my cousin has a finely tuned sense for status and power. I'm not even sure that he's consciously aware of that. It's more of an instinct.

He is a progressive, and a very serious one. Entirely embedded in a culture that rewards you for believing the right things, and never once asks whether they're true. In fact, it encourages you to push back hard on anyone who does ask.

So back to that text he sent me. Can you see why I was feeling intimidated? Why I was staring at the notification dreading what was waiting for me when I clicked?

Well, I eventually worked up the courage to click the damn thing, and there it was. Another essay that he clearly banged out one-handed on his lunch break.

That was the thing about Matt. He would fire back at me within the hour, and it'd take me the whole day to answer him. And I mean the whole day. I wouldn't work, I barely slept, I stressed. I googled things, I'd go deep into statistics, economics and philosophy. If I noticed a contradiction, it'd keep me up at night until I'd felt I resolved it.

And none of that mattered.

He could bat down my facts in a heartbeat, and move the conversation towards whatever he wanted it to be about. He would shame me for my opinions, and put me on defense where I felt I had to constantly defend myself. I was literally losing money, not working, obsessing over how I was going to respond to him.

"I'm right about this!" I'd tell myself. "He's wrong!" "Why am I losing!?"

I didn't figure it out. I took the L. In the end, I ghosted him. I just stopped replying. He was in the process of shaming me for believing I should legally be able to put more than five rounds in my rifle, and I'd had enough.

But the truth is, I couldn't let it go. I still haven't. It's been over a decade and I still think about that argument almost every day. Crazy right? Well, that's who I am. And here's what I didn't understand back then: losing that argument was the best thing that ever happened to me. It just took me ten years of pain and work to realize it.

The thing is, in that fight, I wasn't unarmed. I'd been reading Sowell for a while, and at one point in our argument I had sent Matt one of his quotes that astutely addressed the exact thing we were arguing about.

He waved it off. Moved past it as fast as he could. I didn't push. I let him regain control of the conversation.

That moment really stuck with me. That little shrug. The dismissal. That's the thing I never let go of. That shrug is the reason all of this exists. It's the reason you're reading this story right now, and the reason I run the largest Thomas Sowell Quotes page on Facebook.

I couldn't stop thinking about how I'd folded. The more I sat with it, the more I felt ashamed of myself for it.

Sowell never did that. He never let anyone put words in his mouth, or get away with shrugging off one of his points. Nobody could wave him off the way Matt had waved me off. He wouldn't let his opponents intimidate him, shame him or take control of the conversation. He was an example of how to win. That's what I wanted!

So I started relentlessly consuming everything he ever wrote and posting his words on Facebook. I wanted to see if there was anyone else out there who saw what I saw, and it turns out there's quite a few of you. As of writing this, I'm up to about 200,000 followers on the page and growing. I regularly reach upwards of 20 million impressions per month.

My God Matt, what have you unleashed?

But here's the thing, for all those years, the page was only ever his words. Never mine. I was just the megaphone, I was not a voice.

It took me ten years to see what really happened in that fight with Matt. Every time he pushed, I backed down. Every time he reframed it, I let him. I folded. In the end, I went quiet, tucked my tail between my legs and ran. I behaved like prey. Matt operated like a predator.

I'd love to tell you that I went on a hero's journey in those ten years. But I didn't. Mostly, those years were filled with confusion, frustration, and getting things wrong. Not the ideas. The ideas I had were mostly right. After all, I was spending a huge chunk of my time reading all the great economists from the last century. But that wasn't enough. It had nothing to do with why I'd lost that fight to Matt.

While I was buried in economics books and political philosophy, Matt was out there conquering the world, building relationships. He was acquiring real power and status. I was learning how to see the world correctly. Two totally different things.

But then, last September, something happened. Charlie Kirk was assassinated. I wrote this on the Sowell quotes page that day.

Everything changed today.

We live in a different world from the one that existed yesterday.

Can you feel it?

Those were my words, not his. And writing them that day, while we were all in shock, something in me knew I couldn't go back to hiding behind quotes.

And so, I began writing more regularly on the page, under my own name. The response was something I didn't expect. My own words started going viral. My writing was outperforming most of the Sowell quotes I was posting. I still don't quite know how to process that.

But all that reach brought something with it. Progressives started showing up in my comments in droves. Some wanted to argue with me. But a lot of them were there for my audience, to hunt my readers the same way Matt once hunted me. To dominate them, shame them, put them on the defensive and extract their energy.

At first, I didn't even engage. I watched. I studied them, how they operated, how they laid traps, and drew my readers into them. And not just the trolls, the real ones. Academics. Professionals. People with credentials and serious jobs.

I started noticing patterns. They were behaving exactly the same way Matt behaved with me.

And so, once I felt I understood them, I stepped in. I started engaging, testing everything I'd spent a decade learning against the real thing. Every exchange was an experiment.

I began to quickly realize I was onto something. I was able to see all of their traps immediately, navigate around them, name exactly what they're doing with precision and put them on defense.

And it wasn't a one-off. It became a constant. Hundreds of these exchanges, all of them public, all of them still there to read. This is where my doctrine actually got built, not in a book. In live combat, in the comments. I was getting my reps in.

Now, I can argue their side better than they can. I can make the case for a $20 minimum wage stronger than the professor who teaches it. But ask one of them to honestly argue my side? They can't. They have no idea how someone like me actually thinks. For all their talk about empathy, they've never spent a second developing it for the people they disagree with politically. They never had to. The orthodoxy does their thinking for them. This is their Achilles heel.

Now I have my doctrine. The 7 Rules.

So that fight I lost to Matt? He wasn't special. He was rep number one. I've run that gauntlet a thousand times since.

The truth is, if Matt opened up that same argument with me today, over text, it wouldn't be a fight. I'd be toying with him.

Face to face, in a room? He'd probably still get the upper hand. That's his arena. But in a war of ideas, where you've got time to think and nowhere to hide? That's my territory now.

But this was never really about Matt. It's about the one thing that fight taught me, the thing it took me ten years and a lot of pain to finally understand. You don't have to fall for their traps. You can learn to see them clearly, and when you're ready, start planting your own.

So that's what I do now. It's what all of this is. Stop Being Prey.

That fight I lost in 2015 was one of the best things that ever happened to me. It taught me how the game really works. The difference between being effective and being right. And now, I see it everywhere. The game is clear to me, and I can make it clearer for you.

We've got a lot of work ahead of us, you and me.

stay close,
~ Clay

p.s. In yesterday's email I talked about tearing a thing down and rebuilding it. Well, that was my website. The new version is live, and you just read my new about page.

p.p.s. I rewrote my Rules of Engagement, the playbook for winning these arguments, and made the whole thing public. Free, right on the main page.

p.p.p.s. All my best writing now lives in one place too, ready for you to read and share. The stuff I'm proud to attach my name to. The Gimme Shelter essay is finally public, I renamed it "It's Just a Shot Away."

p.p.p.p.s. I also built something I'm calling The Wall. Think of it as a guest book for this fight. If the project means something to you, put your mark on it and stand with the rest of us. (A dollar to post, which keeps the whole thing running.)

p.p.p.p.p.s. One last thing, and it's the big one. The Guild is ready. It's where you bring your real battles, work through them with the room, and get my advice directly. I want you in there.

subject: tear it all down
preview: that's how I work
html:
I don't like to tweak things or spend too much time trying to fix something that is clearly broken.

I'm much more of a "tear it all down, and start from scratch" kind of guy. Always have been. I can't tell you how many times I threw out entire acts of my Thomas Massie piece and started over from scratch. You wouldn't have liked the versions I threw out as much as you liked the final version, I promise you. And there was no fixing them. They were fundamentally flawed. They had to go.

It was painful, I worked hard on them, and they were genuinely good in many cases... Didn't matter, they didn't work. They didn't fit the overall vision. Gone.

Many people don't have the conviction to do this, I've noticed. It's not easy. It's painful, even. Killing something you love and care about.

I've noticed this attitude is seldom rewarded in politics. In fact, people usually react in horror when they encounter it. What explains that?

Here's what I think it is... Private Ownership. I own this thing. It's mine. I can kill it tomorrow if I want, or I can spend the rest of my life growing it. The choices and their consequences are entirely on me.

Now ask yourself... who owns the Government? Who bears the ultimate responsibility for its decisions? Nobody. Not one single person.

When it fails, no one's name is on it. No one gets fired. None of the decision-makers lose a dime. Everyone dodges the responsibility and points at someone else. The media distracts the public with the next story, and everyone moves on. Taxpayers foot the bill. Pay or go to jail.

When MY thing fails, it's all on me. So I fix it, or I kill it and move on. The government has no 'me.' So nothing ever gets fixed. It just... continues and expands. The classes that control the state socialize the losses to the classes that don't.

“No society ever thrived because it had a large and growing class of parasites living off those who produce.”
~ Thomas Sowell

So, this weekend I did that thing... where I tear something down and rebuild it. I'll show you tomorrow.

stay close

~ Clay

p.s. that Sowell quote is on a Tshirt, by the way. Wear it in the wrong room, and you'll find out real fast who the parasites are.

subject: fatherhood
preview: the ultimate responsibliity
html:
Happy Father's Day!

Is there any responsibility more profound than bringing children into this world? I don't think so.

I watched the JD Vance interview on Megyn Kelly's podcast today. It was just something I turned on casually while eating lunch... I didn't expect it to move me... but it did.

It was right at the end of the interview... they were talking about Charlie Kirk.

Vance talked about flying out to be with Charlie's widow, Erika, right after it happened. She told him, "I wish we had more kids"...

A few months later, Usha Vance was pregnant with their fourth. You could hear JD's voice break as he explained this to Megyn. I haven't been able to get it off my mind since.

Maybe it hit so hard because of the day. Today is Father's Day. I spent it with my own dad. Still here. I'm lucky. I thank God for this gift every day. I know how valuable it is because of someone else I spent the day with today... my niece.

Her Dad died less than 2 years ago.

So no. There's no responsibility more profound than this. Not because anyone told me. Because today I sat across from a man who's still here, and a girl who'd give anything for one more day with hers.

If your dad is still around, spend time with him as often as you can. Don't wait for a better reason than that. He's here... that's enough.

If your Dad isn't around anymore, I'm sorry. Remember the good times.

If you are a Dad, well, Happy Father's Day to you, and God bless you.

~ Clay

subject: the most basic question
preview: thomas sowell's most powerful quote
html:
I've read thousands upon thousands of Sowell's words over the years, but this one sentence below sticks out in my mind more than any of them.

“The most basic question is not what is best, but who shall decide what is best.”
~ Thomas Sowell, Knowledge and Decisions (1980)

The more I think about it, the more I realize this is the base layer of the "Stop Being Prey" framework I'm developing. Sowell is saying, your ideas don't really matter. Power decides what ideas matter.

And the tragedy of it all? Sowell lost. His ideas were better, but they lost anyway. Power decided that Paul Krugman gets the Nobel Prize. Megan Rapinoe gets the Medal of Freedom. The progressives and the Keynesians decide monetary policy. There are literal Marxists still teaching in the universities. The people that Sowell spent decades analyzing, dissecting, and destroying with precision won. He lost.

I know that's painful to hear, but is it wrong? Reply and let me know.

I'm going to let you sit with that tonight. I'll be writing something about Sowell over the next week.

~ Clay

p.s. Tonight I'm going to keep building. If you like my writing, and my predator/prey framework in particular, you're really going to like how I'm reorganizing my website. I'm getting serious about the doctrine, and about building something that is going to help you win.

p.p.s. If you want to give me a little inspiration while I work through the weekend... put a tip in my jar. This whole thing is reader-supported. It's just you and me.

subject: i laughed out loud on page one
preview: page two had me reaching for a pen
html:
You may have noticed by now that I have a tendency to take the works of great men and internalize the lessons they try to teach us. In the same way the Rolling Stones drew on Muddy Waters and Chuck Berry to eventually write the apocalyptic anthem that is Gimme Shelter, I'm trying to do the same sort of thing with my writing.

I take inspiration and internalize the lessons from great writers before me, and I try to come up with my own 'sound' as it were. I guess writers call this their 'voice'. My voice isn't really mine. It's every writer who ever moved me, ran through me, and poured back out.

You may have already noticed one of those voices in my work. The late, great Scott Adams. I'm a big fan. I've mentioned it before, but I was there for countless Simultaneous Sips in the morning. I'm sure many of you were there with me.

If you read the Gimme Shelter essay 2 days ago, you'll know how I interface with music. Songs just kind of come to me, and I obsess over them. Like someone or something put them in front of me for a reason. I consume them until I have every little nuance internalized like the back of my hand. Well, I do the same thing with thinkers and books.

And a book just called to me. I have to sink my teeth into this one, the same way I have to listen to "Gimme Shelter" over and over. I just read the first two pages and it confirmed it. Scott Adams's "Reframe Your Brain."

I have to tell you, I didn't think this whole writing thing would be as stressful as it is. But it is stressful. I think it might have something to do with how I've framed it in my mind... and I think this book is the answer. Somewhere in this book is the answer.

I read the first page. It made me laugh out loud. There’s a story that Scott tells about walking his dog Snickers, and how frustrated he would get at how they just wanted to sniff everything. Well, Scott reframed it as going out for a sniff, and suddenly he started to enjoy it more. It changed his expectations. He compared his dog sniffing the same spots every day to us checking our social media feeds. Brilliant! So he started naming the different sniffing spots. There was Facebark, Twigger, LeafedIn, Treemail and Instabush… and then… “Obviously, The garbage receptacle into which people flung their dog poop bags was TikTok.”

That’s where I laughed. Did it get you too? The man was such a great writer. I wonder how many times I’ll laugh like that by the time I’m done the book.

That’s just the first page!

And then I turned to the second page… and this time I wasn’t laughing. This time, I was reaching for my brand new Parker Jotter pen to take down a note in my notepad. A breathing exercise that Scott Adams learned from Dr. Andrew Huberman.

It's simple. You take two sharp breaths in through your nose, one right after the other. Then you exhale slowly through your mouth. That's it. Apparently there are all kinds of scientifically verifiable benefits to doing this regularly... and I can tell you I felt better immediately after trying it. Give it a shot!

So next time I'm stuck in traffic, or in a long lineup at the store... instead of getting frustrated, I'll just take it as an opportunity to practice breathing.

All this from just 2 pages and maybe 3 minutes of actual reading. If this ratio holds up, this will be the most valuable book I’ve ever read, by far.

Want to know the exact moment this book started calling to me? It was when I was trying to record my guitar for the ‘Gimme Shelter’ video I’m making. There's about five minutes of playing that I have to record straight... and I've been aiming for perfection, which I'm slowly realizing is not possible.

So, instead of getting frustrated that my dog barks while I’m trying to record… maybe I’ll just leave that in. Maybe you’ll actually enjoy the thing more, with little imperfections like that? Makes it less perfect, but more real.

I can’t guarantee that my boy will bark in the final version, but now I’m almost hoping that he does. Why not? That’s the reframe. It was a frustration, and now it’s a desire.

The book is working, just two pages in. Incredible!

That’s it. That’s what I wanted to tell you about tonight. Scott Adams, and Reframe Your Brain.

Join me in saying a prayer for Scott tonight. God bless him.

Lots more coming soon.

stay close

~ Clay

p.s. throw a tip in the jar if you appreciate my work.

p.p.s. better yet, join the inner circle and be one of the people figuring this out right alongside me. I’m starting to love my lounge, and the people who come to hang out in it.

subject: it's just a shot away
preview: an older essay of mine keeps coming up
html:
I wrote an essay on April 29th that's become one of my most requested. It's called "Gimme Shelter", and it's about how the Rolling Stones song is defining this current era for me.

People keep asking me to put it somewhere they can share it. I haven't done that yet, but I plan on it.

Since I started my youtube channel, I've also been told that it would make a great YouTube video. I agree. Subscribe to my youtube youtube.com/@stopbeingprey and click the little bell so you get my stuff as soon as its uploaded.

If you joined the list after April 29th, you don't know what I'm talking about... and so I'm going to paste it into the email below.

stay close,

~ Clay

GIMME SHELTER

I go through phases with music...

Obsessive ones... a song... an album. Sometimes a whole artist. I'll get hooked for a stretch, anywhere from a month to three months, and play that one thing on repeat. Ten,.. maybe twenty times a day some days. It's a little nuts... I know.

Then the era ends. I move on. A new one shows up.

And here's the thing... the songs find me... I don't pick them. They show up at moments in my life when something is shifting, when I need something I don't have words for, and I play them on loop until I figure out what they're trying to tell me.

Almost like something is trying to get my attention...

There've been a couple recently.

Around the time I was building ReadSowell.com, it was a French pop song called J'en ai marre by an artist named Alizée. I can't even explain why... it just hit. Something whimsical. Innocent. Fun.

That era was about rebuilding... Getting in shape. Taking my health seriously... becoming Christian... reconnecting with old friends. The kind of stretch where you decide you've had enough of how things have been going and you start actually putting the work in.

The era worked... Life got better.

Then a new one took over. Crash, by an artist named Rico Nasty. Another whimsical song... Fun. Almost playful.

This is the song I've been writing to. Some of the most serious pieces I've written. Charlie Kirk. The assassination attempts. Predator and prey. Heavy topics, all of them. All while a whimsical pop song plays in the background.

Strange, right?

The soundtrack was light. The work was heavy.

That era is ending now. I still love Crash. But it's not quite landing the way it used to. A new song is taking over... a new era is coming...

And this one... isn't whimsical.

It's from 1969.

Before I name it, I want you to do something. If you have a few minutes, pull it up. Put it on. Let it play before you read the rest of this. The words won't fully land if you don't.

The song is Gimme Shelter, by the Rolling Stones.

Released December 1969. The world it was written into was coming apart. Vietnam at peak... body counts on the news every night. The Manson murders four months earlier...riots... assassinations. The whole 'peace-and-love' era visibly cracking on television...

Keith Richards wrote the opening riff during a storm in London... said it felt apocalyptic. Mick Jagger called the song "a kind of end-of-the-world song, really."

The vocalist on the chorus is named Merry Clayton... she was pregnant. They called her in the middle of the night... she showed up to the studio in pajamas with a fur coat thrown over hair curlers and they put her in front of the mic.

Rape, murder, it's just a shot away. It's just a shot away.

She sang it three times. Sang isn't the right word... she screamed it... On the third one, you can hear her voice crack on the word MURDER. They kept that take... it's the take you hear today.

She miscarried later that night...

The album came out. Days later, the Stones played a free concert at Altamont... Hells Angels, hired as security, stabbed a young man named Meredith Hunter to death in front of the stage while the band played...

The peace-and-love dream cracked that night, on stage, with the world watching.

The song was the warning shot.

This is the song that is defining my life for the time being... and I think I know why...

Charlie Kirk...

One shot... On a college campus... At midday... In front of cameras.

This entire project. This writing. This email. ReadSowell. The book I'm working on... None of it would exist if Charlie were still alive.

That one shot changed my entire life, my entire world... It rewrote what I do with my time. It rewrote my priorities. It rewrote how I see the world.

Something in me broke and something in me started, both at the same time. I went from a computer programmer who posts Sowell quotes in his spare time, to a guy who can't stop writing about what he sees, because I see it now and I can't unsee it.

One shot did that... To one person. Me.

Now ask yourself something...

How many other lives got rewritten that day? How many priorities. How many worldviews?... How many people are walking around in a world that looks completely different than the one they were in the morning Charlie was killed?

I don't know the number. But I don't think I'm the only one... are you one, too?

And then there’s Trump…

Butler, Pennsylvania. July 2024. The shooter on the rooftop fired eight rounds… killed a firefighter who shielded his wife and daughter with his own body… wounded two others critically.

One of those rounds hit Trump in the ear… not near… not close. It hit him. The bullet drew blood. The only reason it hit his ear and not his skull is that he turned his head a quarter inch at the exact millisecond the shooter pulled the trigger.

Now ask yourself.

Was that luck the shot missed?…

And Butler wasn’t the only one. He keeps surviving.

But it’s not just Trump.

Cole Allen at the Correspondents’ Dinner. James Hodgkinson at a Republican baseball practice. Ryan Routh in the bushes at Trump’s golf course. Tyler Robinson on Charlie’s campus.

Different days. Different shooters. Same drumbeat in their ears.

Trump is Hitler. MAGA is fascist. By any means necessary. Delivered daily, for a decade. By a thousand voices. One tweet, one cable hit, one campaign speech, one Jimmy Kimmel monologue at a time.

None of them needed to write a manifesto... the manifesto was already written...

These are just the ones who acted on it… so far…

How many more Cole Allens are out there? It’s just a shot away.

Now... here's the part I really don't want to write... but we have to talk about it...

What if next time they don't miss...

What if it's JD... Stephen Miller... What if it's one of the senators... one of the governors... one of the podcasters... one of the writers... one of our people. Someone you watch every week. Someone you don't even know yet, but will be mourning before the year is out.

Somebody is going down... These people aren't playing... a pattern is emerging... A new era is here.

You can feel it the same way Mick and Keith felt it in 1969.

Brace yourself. This is the game.

Predators and prey.

It's just a shot away.

There's one more line in the song we need to talk about... comes near the end... same melody... same cadence... different word.

Love, sister... it's just a kiss away. It's just a kiss away.

A shot away from horror... A kiss away from connection... Same proximity. Different direction.

So while the shot is on the news... look up. Who's actually in the room with you right now?

Your wife. Your kids. Your brother. Your parents. Your friends. Me, even. The people you don't have to pretend around.

The shot is loud and far... the kiss is quiet and close.

That's where the shelter is. Reach for it. You're going to need it.

Now play the song... put it on repeat. Reply back and tell me what you felt... do you feel what I feel?

I want to know if you hear it the way I do.

stay close,

~ Clay
@stopbeingprey on X

P.S. Merry Clayton's voice cracking on the third MURDER is the take they kept. She gave it to them with the cost of her body. The song is sacred for that reason alone, before you even get to what it was warning about.

P.P.S. I'm not stopping... I will write to you every day... I am writing the book Stop Being Prey, I am building infrastructure for our community, and soon we will start stacking wins together. If you appreciate my work and want to help me keep the lights on in this era, you can tip me here

P.P.P.S. There's a membership behind all of this, and over 100 of you are already in. It's about to get a lot better, too. This is where we can actually talk and build together, away from the noise. If you want in, here's the door.
