subject: the marketplace of ideas is dead
preview: it never really lived. It was a trick. A mirage. A trap.
html:
I posted something on Facebook this morning. It's running. Last I checked, 1,900+ reactions, 300+ shares, 90 comments... The Kimmel Pivot, named.

But I want to talk about what's underneath the post... the doctrine that made me write it... the thing I haven't said directly to you yet.

I used to be a free speech warrior. At least, that's what I would call myself. "I'm a free speech absolutist!" I would tell people, with great pride!

I used to defend the marketplace of ideas like it was holy ground... I thought if we kept arguing, kept debating, kept showing up with the better facts, we'd win. The truth would carry... the market of ideas would correct itself eventually.

I have evolved.

I don't believe that anymore... and I'll go further. I think believing it has been the single biggest strategic failure of conservatism in the last fifty years.

The marketplace of ideas is dead... it never really lived. It's a battlefield. Always was, always will be. You MUST understand this if you want to be effective... If you walk into a battlefield thinking it's a debate club, you're going to get killed. That is literally what happened to Charlie. Take this seriously.

This is going to be a hard pill for a lot of you to swallow, but stay with me. See if I have a point... Let me explain...

The marketplace frame assumes a few things...

That ideas compete on merits...they don't... they compete on power, distribution, and saturation. A bad idea backed by every university, news network, and HR department beats a good idea backed by a podcast and a Substack. Every time. For decades. There's a reason Paul Krugman gets a job at the New York Times while Thomas Sowell is stuck with strangers on the internet like me, trying desperately to spread his words organically.

That participants are good faith... they're not. You know this. Half the people in the conversation are operators trying to win, not truth-seekers engaging in real curiosity. When David Pakman tweets "what happened to the First Amendment?" he's not asking... he's deploying a trap. When Destiny demands you debate him, he's not curious. He's hunting you and your people.

That truth wins eventually... It doesn't. The team that captures the institutions writes what counts as truth... Sowell has been right for fifty years on most economic questions... he hasn't won. Why? Because the universities didn't teach him. The textbooks didn't print him. The media didn't quote him. He was right, and he was buried. That's power.

That the arena is neutral... It isn't. By the time an idea enters the public conversation, the gatekeepers have already decided which ideas get respectability and which get marked as fringe. "Free speech" only exists where power tolerates it. The moment power decides something is harmful, it gets suppressed via informal sanction... cancellation, deplatforming, professional consequences... with the First Amendment fully intact.

Even Sowell, who taught me almost everything I know, may have made this mistake...

In 2015 he wrote about microaggression as a tactic to "stifle differences of opinion by declaring some opinions to be 'hate speech,' instead of debating those differences in a marketplace of ideas."

Notice the move. Sowell saw the failure (universities suppressing speech). He documented it brilliantly... but he kept the frame. The marketplace of ideas was still the ideal. The violators were just bad actors in an otherwise functional system.

I think the marketplace framing was the failure point. It was never a marketplace; that was a lie... A trap.

By 2015 the universities had been captured for generations. The textbooks had been ideological since before most of the people reading them were born. HR departments were already enforcing speech codes. The "marketplace" Sowell was defending didn't exist. The team with the better arguments had been losing since the 1960s... the team that captured the institutions had been writing the rules.

That's not a marketplace. That's a captured system operating under marketplace branding, while the right kept showing up to debate it.

Two days ago I told Destiny this directly on X.

He had been demanding that conservatives debate him in his preferred format on his preferred terms. The standard "marketplace of ideas" play. I told him:

The marketplace of ideas isn't really a marketplace at all. It's more like a battlefield. Conservatives are just starting to learn this. You have understood it for a while. That's why you're good at what you do.

Guess how he responded?... He blocked me...

Think about that.... what does that say about him? Why would he feel the need to block me for that?

The line named what he was actually doing. He's not in the marketplace finding truth...he's on the battlefield winning ground, collecting scalps... The "marketplace" framing is just camouflage that makes him look reasonable while he hunts. It's a trick. A trap. I exposed it, and he can't have that. So he blocks. He knows the game.

Yesterday I did the same move on David Pakman. Different style. He had tweeted "what happened to the First Amendment?" because Trump and Melania criticized Kimmel. I replied:

Yes... every time someone takes a shot at Trump, or murders one of his biggest supporters... Jimmy Kimmel is the real victim. Excellent point, David. You're definitely not a political operative crafting a narrative. You're just doing honest analysis. Very impressive!

That's not debate. That's not marketplace participation. That's battlefield combat dressed in mockery.

And it works because there's nothing to debate. He's not making an argument. He's running a play... naming the play is the move.

They have no answer for this... It is our job to make them answer...

Here's what changes when you stop using the marketplace frame.

You stop debating in good faith with people who aren't.

You stop asking permission from referees who already work for the other side.

You stop investing in procedures the institutions already abandoned.

You start noticing who has power and how they're using it.

You start fighting on terrain you can win.

You start protecting your own people instead of throwing them into rigged debates.

You start building infrastructure instead of writing better arguments for an audience that was never going to hear them.

You become a predator instead of prey. You start stacking wins and become dangerous. An asset to our team.

The marketplace of ideas is dead... it probably never lived... it was just a mirage planted in our brains by our predators.

The battlefield was always the actual terrain.

Conservatives are just starting to figure this out... Progressives have known it for over fifty years.

Catch up. Stop Being Prey.

stay close

~ Clay

P.S. If you enjoyed this letter, send it to someone who needs to read it. They can join the list here: readsowell.com/join

P.P.S. I write full time, every day. No sponsors. No paywalls. The framework behind this email took years to build... today took six hours to write. If the work helped you see something clearly, and you have the means, you can support it here... Truly grateful to everyone who has.

P.P.P.S. I'm on X now. x.com/stopbeingprey

subject: the chess board
preview: First you have to see the board correctly.
html:
A reader emailed me yesterday morning. Subject line: Re: your poll. What do you have in mind that the Republicans could do that would be considered serious and effective?

It's a question I've been receiving quite regularly from readers... What would you suggest we do?

Kim's email is just one in a stack of dozens. They aren't asking outlier questions. They're telling me, quietly, what most Trump supporters already feel. They believe Trump wants to fight... but they see most Republicans as another obstacle in his way.

The poll I ran said it plain. Around one thousand readers in the Sowell Dispatch voted. Roughly nine in ten said no, the Republicans won't get serious... one in ten said maybe.

So the audience already has the diagnosis... what they want is a tool to do something about it.

Why are nine in ten readers convinced their own side won't act?.. They're sensing something they can't quite articulate yet. This morning, I'll try to give them the words.

Here's the part I have to be honest about...

I'm not going to solve this in one email. Just accept that going in... I don't have a five-point plan that ends the activation network and rebuilds the right-wing bench by Friday. Anyone telling you they do is selling you something.

What I can do is show you the chess board.

What we see from most Republicans is closer to professional wrestling than to politics. Have you ever seen a video of a grown adult who still believes wrestling is real, and you think "oh god, that's sad"? That should be your reaction when you see someone who believes the Republican opposition is real... There is a term for it, it's called kayfabe... the maintained illusion of conflict with pre-determined outcomes. Most Republicans are doing kayfabe.

This morning... we're going to fix that.

Picture a chess board.

The king is Trump.

Not because of personality, not because of vibes. Because of geometry. Lose the king, you lose the game. The whole position depends on him standing....those are the stakes, and the people who keep taking shots at Trump understand this.

Trump is the only thing standing in the way of a total Democrat-neocon takeover of everything, all the time, forever.

This is why the activation network spends every waking hour producing the conditions that get him killed. Not because he's the worst Republican. Because he's the king, and they want to win the game.

Trump himself was on 60 Minutes this weekend telling the interviewer "if I was a king I wouldn't be dealing with you." He knows what he is. He also knows what he isn't. Wartime register from the king himself.

Asked about being shot at, he said "I wasn't worried." Three words. Asked why he didn't get out faster, he said he "wasn't making it that easy" because he wanted to see what was going on. The king's nervous system.

So who is actually defending the king? Who is his praetorian guard?

Around the king, you have pieces with real moves.

JD Vance. Heir apparent. The only person on the board who could keep the project going if the king fell tonight. That's why every cleanup-crew operator is already pre-positioning to delegitimize him.

Stephen Miller. Deputy chief of staff for policy. The personnel guy. In a regime, the personnel guy is the most powerful operator after the king. Whoever controls hiring and firing controls the floor. They hate him because he's effective, and he doesn't flinch. He just proved his courage under fire, same as the king has done multiple times. He's a predator. A real one.

Susie Wiles. Chief of Staff. The gatekeeper. In a regime, whoever decides who reaches the king has more power than most cabinet pieces. She has spent a year keeping snakes out of the room.

Kash Patel. FBI. The only person who can pull classified files into the open. The cleanup crew knows what's in those files.

Scott Bessent. Treasury. The financial war is the war. If the dollar war goes badly, every other piece on the board is fighting on broken terrain.

Behind them: Hegseth at Defense refusing press capture, Tulsi at DNI quiet but effective, Vought at OMB controlling budgets, RFK Jr where he's useful. Rubio on probation, earning the benefit of the doubt.

Each one has actual moves. None of them are doing kayfabe.

Now flip the board.

Not every piece on your color is on your side.

Some pieces look like Republicans, vote like Republicans, raise money as Republicans. But every move they make at the critical moment serves the other side... they're captured.

Mitch McConnell. The archetype. The regime's manager of the Republican Party. Every move is press approval and donor maintenance.

Susan Collins. Lisa Murkowski. The perpetual-squish caucus. Always announce concern. Always vote with the cleanup crew when it counts.

Mike Johnson. Speaker. Folds at critical moments.

John Thune. McConnell's heir. Same function.

Candace Owens. Different specimen, same function. She has reach. She has audience. She has charisma. But the moves she's been making lately pull right-coded discourse away from the actual fight and into terrain that distracts. Truther narratives. Single-issue obsessions. The activation network doesn't need her to mean to do this. The function is the same either way.

How do you spot one in real time? How do they treat Trump. That's the signal. I disagree with plenty Trump does. There are people he keeps around I wouldn't. But he's the last stand. Watch what each piece does when Trump is under fire. Don't listen to what they say. Watch what they do.

One more case I want to name. Some of you have asked me about him.

Thomas Massie. This one is hard. Massie may be the closest person in Congress to my actual policy views. Principled, intelligent, acts on conviction. I genuinely respect him.

But the more I watch the votes, the more I notice the same pattern. At critical junctures, his principled vote ends up weakening the king at exactly the moment the king needs the bench to hold. The king loses the vote. The cleanup crew gets their headline.

I'm not putting Massie in the captured column. But the loyalty question is real. Function over motive, even when the motive is sincere.

Massie's case points to something bigger. There's a whole category of people who are good people in their own minds... I was one of them.

The 2008 Ron Paul libertarian operating system... Anti-state on principle, anti-war on principle, anti-establishment on principle. I was there... a lot of you reading this were there. A lot of the most important figures on the new-right and MAGA came out of the Ron Paul revolution.

The test was whether you updated, or whether you are stuck.

Some of us evolved. Some of us didn't. The ones who didn't are now stuck in what I'm calling the loser libertarian operating mode. Rigid principle defense in a moment that requires sober reading of the actual situation.

In my heart I'm still mostly libertarian. The framework gave me half the tools I use to think clearly about anything. But libertarians, as a class, do not have loyalty. They have principles. And when principles bump against tribal coalition discipline, the principles win. Every time.

Which sounds noble. In wartime politics, it makes you toothless. Worse, it can make you a defector.

The motive is purity. The function is paralysis. In a moment when the king is the only piece between us and a permanent Democrat-neocon takeover, paralysis is working with the enemy.

Trump is the signal, libertarians are noise.

One more thing. The cleanup crew is going to spend the week trying to convince you the rhetoric isn't responsible. They'll produce screenshots showing the shooter didn't follow this person, didn't watch that one, didn't even like the other. The conclusion they want you to reach: the activation network theory is wrong.

Don't fall for it.

The activation network does not require fandom. It requires saturation.

A radicalized person does not have to follow any specific voice on the left. He has to absorb the worldview the institutional center has spent a decade broadcasting until it feels obvious. The framework comes from the saturation. The execution comes from the radicalized self-purifier.

Three months before the attack, the actor Mark Ruffalo called Trump a "rapist pedophile" on his platform of millions.

Cole Allen used the exact same words in his manifesto.

Not paraphrase. Not similar framing. Identical language.

Allen did not need to follow Ruffalo. Ruffalo helped put the language in the air. Allen breathed it in. That is saturation.

And Ruffalo isn't an outlier. Days before the attack, Jimmy Kimmel scripted, network-approved, and broadcast a parody on ABC where he looked at Melania Trump and said "you have a glow like an expectant widow." James Carville, the architect of Bill Clinton's 1992 campaign, told his podcast this week "I do not want that man to die. I want to watch him suffer."

These are not radicals. Network television. Establishment Democrat strategist class. Hollywood A-list. The activation network is not a fringe. It is the mainstream.

Watch for the dissociation move. It will run all week. Now you can name it when you see it.

Now back to Kim's question.

What does serious response look like?... Here's the test, and you don't need to predict, you only need to watch.

In the next 72 hours, every piece on the board is going to move. Watch what they do. Not what they say. What they do.

The serious pieces will use the powers they actually have. Personnel firings. Budget redirects. Investigations opened. Files declassified. Press attacks refused. Wartime register maintained.

The jokers will issue strongly-worded letters and disappear by Friday.

The snakes will quietly position against the king while still calling themselves Republicans. Watch their actual moves, not their cable-news clips.

The loser libertarians will spend the week explaining that actually, both sides, the real issue is, technically the principle requires... they want you to think they're the smart ones in the room. They're not.

Kim doesn't need me to tell her who's serious. She has the chess board now. She can see who's worth listening to and who isn't... She can sense when someone isn't communicating with her best interest in mind, when they're using words to manipulate her rather than to communicate. It becomes very clear once you know what to look for.

Most people reading this opened the email feeling helpless. The country is under attack. The press is captured. The jokers are useless. The snakes are everywhere. What can one person do?

You can see the board.

That's not nothing. That's the first move out of prey. The reader who can sort the board can name the moves while they're happening. The reader who can name the moves can't be played by them.

Once you see the board, you stop falling for the traps. You start identifying the real operators. You can develop real strategy.

Find your champions. Identify the snakes. Protect your prey.

stay close,
Clay

P.S. A few readers have asked how to support the work. ReadSowell.com/donate. It helps me keep the lights on. No subscription, no pressure. The work is going up either way.

P.P.S. I write every day, no exceptions. If you value this letter, send it to someone who needs to read it. They can join the list here: readsowell.com/join

subject: she just wanted to go home
preview: What the cleanup crew is about to spend this week telling you.
html:
Erika Kirk hid under a table last night while gunfire went off in the next room. What was going through her mind in that moment?

Bret Baier saw her there. Kash Patel consoled her... On her way out, on video, she said "I just want to go home." while wiping tears from her eyes.

Charlie was assassinated seven months ago... we all saw it in 4k resolution. It involuntarily replays in my mind every day. He was debating college students at Utah Valley University when Tyler Robinson shot him from a rooftop. Erika went home that night without him. Last night she went home without him again.

This is not a metaphor. This is what predator/prey looks like in flesh. A widow under a table. A credentialed engineer with a shotgun... A country where this keeps happening to the sitting president.

We need to talk about what's actually happening.

The man who showed up

The man who charged the security checkpoint last night is Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California. He has a Caltech engineering degree. A NASA fellowship at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. A master's in computer science. He worked as a mechanical engineer. He was named Teacher of the Month in LA County in December. He donated $25 to Kamala Harris last October.

He brought a shotgun, a handgun, and multiple knives.

This is not a guy who snapped. This is the most credentialed shooter you could design in a lab. NASA. Caltech. Engineer. Teacher.... we need to talk about teachers, by the way... but that's an email for another day. He is the kid your grandkids are told to be like. The system produced him at full institutional capacity, with honors.

That's the part nobody on the right wants to look at. Because if Cole Allen is a lone wolf, you can shrug. If Cole Allen is a Cathedral product, you have to ask what the Cathedral is producing...

How it works

Trump called him a lone wolf last night. Trump said it on camera. The man who reads this game better than anyone repeated the cleanup crew's phrase before the cleanup crew even had to say it. That is how dominant the move is. They have been running it long enough that even our side talks like them in the first hours.

Don't fall for it. These are not lone wolves. Even if there is no one giving orders. Even if Cole Allen never met any of the people I am about to name, never got an envelope, never got a phone call.

The cell does not need a chain of command. The cell is a feedback loop.

You already know who Hasan Piker is. I wrote about him three days ago. The New York Times put him on a podcast recently and let him defend stealing and the murder of healthcare executives. On stream, on video, he said: "If you cared about Medicare fraud or Medicaid fraud, you would kill Rick Scott." He has publicly approved of past attempts on Trump's life. He still has every platform. He still has every podcast invite. He still has 2.9 million followers on Twitch.

I am not telling you Hasan ordered Cole Allen to charge a checkpoint. I do not know anything about Cole Allen's media diet. What I am telling you is this:

There is an industry of people on the left whose entire job is to find young men with nothing to lose and turn their pain into hate. Resentment into envy. Envy into permission. Permission into action. Hasan is one node. Another one is Destiny, you may have heard of him... The New York Times is the institutional layer that confers status on both. They do not need to coordinate. They do not need a meeting. They produce the same output independently because they are running the same program.

Cole Allen is what comes out the end of that program when it works. He is not the first. He will not be the last. Prepare yourself.

These are activated cells. Even if it's not explicitly so.

What they're going to tell you this week

By the end of today there will be a story for everything you saw. Each story is a move. Each move is designed to make you doubt your own eyes.

Move one: lone wolf. Trump used the phrase last night. So did Fox News. So did the Washington Post. The story is that this was a guy who snapped. No network. No ideology. No consequence. The Caltech mechanical engineer with the NASA fellowship who brought a shotgun and a handgun and a stack of knives to the same hotel where Reagan was shot in 1981 is going to be filed under "mental health." Cole Allen's master's thesis will not be discussed. His Kamala donation will not be discussed. Why he chose the President of the United States as a target out of every other person on the planet will not be discussed.

This is the most useful frame for the cleanup crew... It severs the wire between activation and execution. No wire, no question about why the rhetoric exists... the loop runs again.

Move two: false flag. Hasan Piker was on this within minutes... because of course he was... Karoline Leavitt had said earlier in the night that "shots will be fired tonight" as a normal political metaphor. Hasan time-traveled... How did Karoline KNOW? The implication: Trump staged it. The Secret Service was in on it. The Republicans manufactured the attempt to make themselves look good for the midterms... By the time you read this, half of populist Twitter will be on this story. I see it everywhere on twitter/x.

The function of false flag is to make the witness a rube... you saw what you saw. The cleanup crew tells you you're stupid for seeing it. The frame works because conspiracy thinking is satisfying, and "everyone is in on it" requires no further updating to your model. Once you accept it, every new fact confirms it... Loop runs again.

Move three: mock the widow. Erika Kirk has been visible for less than twelve hours and the mockery is already running... Crisis actor. Fake tears. She's in on it... The image of a thirty-year-old widow under a table seven months after burying her husband, sobbing "I just want to go home," is too sympathetic to leave standing... they have to destroy the image. So they overlay it with ridicule until people associate her face with the joke, instead of the grief... that is the move... Loop runs again. See the pattern?

Move four: invert the protective husband. Stephen Miller covered his pregnant wife with his body when the shots went off. The footage is on Twitter... A man, in a tuxedo, shielding the woman he loves and the child she's carrying, in a ballroom under fire. It is one of the most beautifully human things you will see this year.

Within hours the cleanup crew was reframing it... He hid behind his pregnant wife. Coward. Used her as a shield. The actual image is too dangerous to leave standing... If you let it stand without comment, every man who sees it understands what masculinity is for. So they invert the meaning until the protective instinct reads as cowardice... Loop runs again.

Four moves... they will run all four this week, simultaneously, contradictorily, on the same audience. The shooter was a lone wolf and it was a false flag... the widow is in on it and nothing happened... the husband is a coward and there was no shooting. Coherence is not the point. Saturation is. The goal is to make you tired enough that you stop trusting your own eyes.

Trust what you saw. Trust your gut.

That is what the cleanup crew does after the activation produces. See it clearly. Name it.

A note on "they"

When I say "they keep trying to kill him," somebody on the soft middle tells me that I shouldn't say they... Not all Democrats are like this... I know... but an awful lot of them are.

"They" is the network. Hasan and Destiny and the New York Times and the editors and the donors and the institutions that confer status on people who call for the murder of senators on stream. "They" is what produced Cole Allen, Tyler Robinson, and the Butler shooter. "They" is not your aunt who voted for Kamala. "They" is the people who train your aunt's friends' kids to pick up a weapon.

That is what "they" means. That is what last night was.

The widow's request

Erika Kirk wanted to go home last night. She wanted Charlie. She wanted the man who would have held her and told her she was safe. He was killed seven months ago by a different shooter, trained by the same machinery, mocked by the same crowd currently calling her a crisis actor.

She is going to spend this week being told her grief is fake. Stephen Miller is going to spend this week being told his protective instinct is cowardice. Cole Allen is going to spend this week being told he was a lone wolf with mental health issues. The cleanup crew is going to spend this week telling you that if you noticed any of it, you are the crazy one.

You aren't crazy... trust what you saw.

When they run the moves on your feed this week, name them out loud. Lone wolf. False flag. Mock the widow. Invert the husband. Watch for the ones I haven't named yet. Once you can see the pattern, the moves stop working.

Progressivism in 2026 is an ideology of murder. They are not joking about power. They will not stop until somebody makes them.

Angry letters will not be enough.

Trump is the signal. The Republicans loyal to him are serious. The ones who show disloyalty are jokers.

Some are showing loyalty with plans to betray. Snakes in the grass.

He can't do it alone. He's not going to be president forever. The fight outlasts his term and we are going to need more than one serious man on our side.

Trust what you saw.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: She was right
preview: She named something I've been quietly worrying about
html:
Yesterday someone in my comments called me out for the way I post people's names when I dunk on them publicly...

She wrote:

"I don't feel comfortable with the way you post someone's name, when you repost their post to discuss your viewpoint. I think it would be better to redact the name when you do this."

My first honest reaction was that she was right. I've had the same thoughts myself... many times. As I've been publicly humiliating progressives who come onto my page, I've sat with that doubt.

I worry about dunking on people who don't deserve it. I worry that some of my followers can be quite nasty to them, and I don't approve of that. I can't control them... I don't want to target anyone... I don't want to hurt them, that's the truth.

I wrestled with all of this for the 100th time before I wrote her a reply.

Here's what I came back with...

The people I do this to come into my memorial posts for Charlie Kirk and effectively spit on his grave. They call Thomas Sowell an Uncle Tom on nearly every post... they're nasty to me, they're nasty to my followers... they're not commenting in good faith. They're treating us like prey.

They're a predator who came here to hunt us... to make us angry, to disrupt our lives.

So I make an example of them. And honestly, I think it's a public service.

Here's what I mean...

If we let these people behave this way without accountability, they keep doing it. They go on hurting people... bullying... silencing.

By making a display of them, taking them apart publicly with grace, we cause embarrassment. Embarrassment is a kind of pain. The pain is a disincentive... it makes other people watching think, "I don't want to be that guy."

These people don't really have political opinions. They're not on your level. Do not treat them as equals. This might sound harsh, but it's the truth and you know it.

They're dogs barking. Making noises hoping to get a treat. Social rewards. Status. They'll say anything for a treat. That's why they can say one thing one day and the opposite the next, and it doesn't bother them at all. Call them a hypocrite all day long if it makes you feel better, but understand that it means less than nothing to them.

Right now the system rewards them for hurting us. After Charlie was killed, CNN, NYT, NPR, Politico, and Vanity Fair all booked Hasan Piker to interpret the moment. A man with a documented record of calling for political killings, given a treat by every major outlet. They reward this stuff. Bullying. Silencing. Shooting us. Charlie.

What I'm doing in my comment threads is taking the treats away. I'm replacing them with discipline. Because that's actually what they're asking for... and if we don't, our people keep getting hurt.

This isn't Democrats versus Republicans anymore. Those were the days of yore. Democrats are something different now. Trump is something different.

This is predators and prey. This is competition to be the apex predator in the political sphere. The ones who write the rules, or the ones who follow them.

So when this person raised her concern, I took it seriously. I keep doing this because the people I do it to come here looking for prey. The only thing that stops them is when the audience watches them embarrass themselves and decides they don't want to be that.

Grace is always part of my equation.

Not so much part of theirs.

stay close.

~ Clay

P.S. I gave the woman who challenged me grace, and I didn't name her in this email. The people who spit on Charlie's grave won't get the same treatment. That's the rule.

P.P.S. The list is for the readers who'd rather be writing the rules than barking for treats. ReadSowell.com/join. Daily writing. The stuff I can't put on Facebook.

P.P.P.S. This is my full-time work now. If you got something out of today, you can throw a few bucks toward keeping the lights on at ReadSowell.com/support-donate. No pressure. Just there.

subject: About your son...
preview: Yesterday wasn't what I expected. It was something else.
html:
Yesterday I shipped the longest piece I've ever written. Twenty-five hundred words on Hasan Piker and the licensed-opposition racket. Hours of work. Hours of stress. Hours of consuming his content to get the diagnosis right, and feeling disgusting the whole time. Letting that man-child into my brain for research is not something I want to repeat.

When it went live, I expected a certain kind of day. You've been good to my recent work. I expected the same here. I expected the viral lift. I expected to feel like I'd hit something big.

Part of that happened... share ratios were strong. Walter Kirn reposted something I wrote in the conversation around the piece, which for those who don't know him is a real literary signal. Look him up, he's great! The email list responded. The piece traveled.

But it didn't go viral the way some of my other work has. I sat with that disappointment for a minute.

Then the messages started coming in.

Not from fans. From mothers.

Mothers I don't know... Mothers who read what I wrote and immediately thought about their sons.

One woman told me she was hoping her son would message me. Even just to argue. That would be the first sign he was listening.

A piece that didn't go as viral as I'd hoped, but found its way into family conversations where a mother is trying to pull her son back from the edge... that's not content. That's intervention.

Some of you reading this are those mothers. You know who you are. I read what you sent... I'm going to do the work. You have motivated me like nothing else. I see myself in your sons. I see my own mother in you... I get it.

One more thing I noticed about the Hasan post... normally, my posts bring a line of progressives into the comments. Every Sowell quote. Every article. They show up in droves to call him Uncle Tom, to call me an idiot, a racist... to argue. That's the baseline. Every day, every post.

Not on this one. Hundreds of comments. Not one progressive defender of Hasan. Not one!

That's another signal. The silence says the piece went somewhere they couldn't follow.

To those of you who read the Hasan piece to the end...

You're serious people.

Statistically, almost nobody reads 2,500 words of online writing to completion. Especially when the subject is a man whose name makes everyone feel a little sick. You read it anyway. You passed a filter without knowing there was one.

Which means you're the kind of person I have to tell the rest of the story to...

A few of you, I've been messaging with privately over the last few weeks. I told some of you this would be ready this week.

It's not this week.

I want to tell you what's actually happening. And why you've earned the inside view.

You've heard me mention Stop Being Prey. It's been in my sign-offs. It's been in the P.S. of emails. Most of you know the name. What I haven't given you yet is a fuller picture of what I'm working on.

Because Stop Being Prey isn't just a book. It's a community first. The book is what will come out of it.

Here's what I mean. I'm building a platform... a place for readers who want to stop being commentators and start being operators. Training materials... frameworks. The behind-the-scenes work I can't post publicly on Facebook. Real-time tactical work. Doctrine being built live.

And while that's happening, the book gets written. The predator-prey frame expanded into full doctrine. The archetypes of who's hunting our people. The tactical toolkit for recognizing them. The strategic framework for what we do about it.

But I'm not writing it first and then showing it to you. I'm writing it inside the platform... with you watching. With your examples, your questions, your real conversations shaping what goes in and what gets cut. When the book is done, the people who were in the room with me will have helped make it.

That's the deal.

The center of gravity is a Discord.

For those who don't know, a Discord is a group chat platform. But the Discord I'm building is not a chat room, exactly. It's an operator training ground.

You've had the conversation before. Maybe at Thanksgiving. Maybe with your nephew. Maybe with a neighbor, a coworker, the mother of your grandkid's friend. Someone said something progressive-coded. You felt the blood pressure rise... you knew they were wrong... you couldn't find the words. Or you found them three hours later in the shower, when it was too late.

That conversation is the battle. That moment at the dinner table is the real war. For most of my readers, you walk into those moments alone. Improvising. Hoping you won't blow it. I've been there. I've relived those moments in my head more times than I care to admit.

The Discord is where you don't walk in alone. This is where we get each-others backs.

You bring the conversation into the room... you get real-time strategy. The trap they were laying, named. The tool for disarming it. The rhetorical move that would have worked. The archetype you were facing, so next time you see one, you recognize it instantly.

It's where we talk about the mission. Where we shine lights on their traps, and plan our own. Where we coordinate when a post needs signal-boosting. Where the serious readers of this work become the people who carry it into the world.

Two kinds of people will come through this door.

The first wants to train. They'll watch me write the book live. See the edits. See the pieces I delete. Watch me dismantle real progressives in real comment threads, narrated, so they learn the moves. They'll get the behind-the-scenes on every public post, why I wrote it the way I did, what I was going for. They come to learn the work.

The second is for people who want to go deeper. More serious. More committed. Same training, but a smaller room. Tighter community. More direct access to the work. They come to win, and to help each-other get better.

There's a third tier past that. Officers. More on that later.

I'm not talking prices today... Just telling you the structure that I'm currently building towards.

Let me be straight with you about money...

I'm going to charge for these tiers, and I'm going to make money if I do this right. I'm not apologizing for that. I'm a capitalist. Sowell is a capitalist. Charlie Kirk built something huge and made money doing it and deserved every dollar. The people who do this work take real risks and need to fund the next round.

But pricing isn't just about making money... prices are important. They are signals. They define the incentives.

The email list stays free... forever. Every day, new writing, to everyone, no exceptions. That doesn't change.

The paid tiers exist for control.

A free Discord would get flooded. Spambots. Communists who want to disrupt. Unserious people who drain the energy out of every conversation. Paid access filters the room. What you're buying isn't just content. You're buying the absence of the people who would ruin it.

Now let me tell you what I'm actually scared of.

What scares me is Charlie...

Charlie Kirk built something real. He reached young men. He got in the way. And the machine responded the way it responds when a rising figure becomes inconvenient enough. As this grows, the risk grows with it. I knew that going in.

The danger is real.

Which is exactly why Stop Being Prey has to be a platform, not just a newsletter. A platform has members. A platform has a community. A platform is harder to erase than one writer working alone. The project exists because the danger exists.

Quick honest note... I don't have other income right now. I've stopped taking other work. This is what I do, full time.

If the work has been meaningful and you're able, there's a link: readsowell.com/support-donate. Keeps the lights on while I finish building the room.

Here's what isn't changing... The Sowell page on Facebook stays. Quotes every day. That's home. ReadSowell.com keeps being what it is. Destination. Quotes database. Timeline... This email list keeps coming. Same cadence. Same voice.

What's changing I'm building a new room... stopbeingprey.com.

It's dead right now. Don't go there. There is nothing there. You'll be disappointed if you click it today.

But... you might want to check it again next week. Or the week after. At some point soon, something will appear. You'll be among the first to see it.

Also I'm on X now. @StopBeingPrey. The Hasan piece is there as an Article if you're on that platform. Come say hi. I don't have much a following there yet, but I have plans. This is where a lot of our predators like to come out to play... I want to play to.

To the mothers who messaged me: I see you. I'm working. The room is coming.

To the serious readers who made it through yesterday's piece: you're the reason this is worth building.

To those who've donated along the way: thank you. You've kept the lights on, and I don't forget who showed up early.

stay close.

~ Clay

P.S. If you're reading this wondering "is Stop Being Prey for me," stay. I'll tell you when it's ready.

P.P.S. Keep the lights on: readsowell.com/support-donate.

subject: Hasan...
preview: This is not what I planned on writing today
html:
I was going to write you a short note today.

Not this... nothing like this.

I was going to write two or three paragraphs. A quick private email. Something about a pattern I wanted to name for you. A man I'd been watching, who represents something bigger than himself. A real predator.

Then I started writing.

Then I started researching.

Then I kept finding things.

Hours into this I realized I wasn't getting out of it in two paragraphs. The case was bigger than I thought... and uglier.

I've been in this man's world for two days now... I've listened to his clips, I've read his defenders, I've watched the glossy press treatment... I've absorbed the grift.

I feel dirty.

That's the honest reaction... like I need a shower... like some of it is on me now.

I kept thinking about Charlie...

What I wrote ended up being too long to send as an email. So I posted it to Facebook instead.

If you want to know what I found, it's there. The whole thing. Every receipt. The shape of the machine he serves. Why he's licensed and you're not.

[LINK HERE]

I don't know if you'll get through all of it. It's heavier than I usually ask. But it matters. Especially now.

stay close.

~ Clay

P.S. If it hits you, share it. One person. Just one. That's how this list went from a thousand to eight thousand in a month. It works.

P.P.S. He's funded by grievance. I'm funded by readers. If you want to be one: readsowell.com/support-donate.

subject: stay with me
preview: They came to me as prey. They're leaving armed.
html:
Something is happening here. I didn't expect it. I'm still adjusting to it.

This list was well under a thousand people just a month ago. Today it's over eight thousand, and the growth is only accelerating. Multiple articles I've written over the past month have gone seriously viral... tens of thousands of reactions, thousands of shares and comments, and millions of impressions

I get letters every day from readers who have been reading Thomas Sowell for forty years telling me I'm filling a gap they didn't know was there. I also get messages from readers who never heard of Sowell before they found me and are now reading him every day, spending hours going through the quotes organized on readsowell.com and buying his books.

You are serious people. Real ones. I've talked to CEOs and blue-collar workers. Students. Young parents. Legendary academics in their seventies and eighties. Military men, law enforcement professionals, church leaders, doctors, lawyers. The list goes on. One thing keeps coming up. My work has helped them handle the people in their lives who try to intimidate them, control the frame, push them around. They came to me as prey... they're leaving armed.

It's overwhelming. I have the smartest, most thoughtful readers in the world, I'm convinced of it. Having your attention is the great honor of my life.

I won't waste it.

I also get my share of hate... quite a bit of it. It used to bug me, it doesn't anymore. I revel in it. I handle it. I make content from it... I expect a lot more of it. I expect it to get much worse as I get better at this and more eyes land on my writing. It's just part of the work.

You may have noticed that I write under just my first name... Clay. This isn't an accident. Paine published Common Sense anonymously. The Federalist Papers were published under the name Publius. I'm not claiming their level. I'm noting the tradition... writers who go after entrenched power don't always get to keep their private lives private.

That's a risk I've accepted. It's only a matter of time before a motivated ideologue decides to come for me. I'm very good at embarrassing these people. Too good... that's the real threat. It's why they hated Charlie Kirk so much. Not his politics... because he was persuasive. Because he was good at showing people how progressives actually think and behave, while delegitimizing their ideas in front of the world. They can't tolerate that.

I'm going to keep doing it anyway.

Here's what I'm doing with what you've given me.

I'm not just building an audience anymore, I'm building infrastructure.

A library of arguments. Weapons. Live demonstrations of the work in action. A community of serious people who can deploy them effectively. A membership where the most committed of you can stand shoulder to shoulder. A book that consolidates all of it into something nobody can take off a platform.

This thing needs to be bigger than me. Bigger than Thomas Sowell even. His ideas have to outlast him... not as ideas alone... but as a mobilizing force.

I'm asking for your patience. This takes time.

But here's what I'm telling you...

If you stay with me, we're going to be taking our spaces back. Your spaces. Your home, your workplace, your comments section, your dinner table. All of it. We're organizing now. I'm training operators who will take what I do on the page and carry it further than I can reach.

We're going to stop being intimidated by people who have been intimidating us for sixty years. We're going to stop being quiet. We're on offense now. It's time to stop losing... To stop being their prey.

That's power.

Not volume. Not rage. Not retweets. Not votes. Power. The kind that changes what gets taught, what gets built, what gets named, who gets cited, who gets silenced, who gets remembered.

I know where this is going. You don't have to see it all yet. They've run the Alinsky playbook on us for sixty years. I'm writing ours.

"The most basic question is not what is best, it's who decides what is best."
~ Thomas Sowell

That's going to be you. It's going to be me. It's not going to be them anymore. That's the mission.

You just have to stay close.

~ Clay

P.S. If you're in, reply and tell me. One word is enough.

P.P.S. This is my career now, full-time. Writing for you. Nothing can stop me. But you make it louder, farther, sharper: readsowell.com/support-donate

subject: "so you're saying Hitler was a progressive?"
preview: yes, in a very real sense, that's exactly what he was.
html:
A young man asked me that exact question yesterday.

Well, he didn't really ask it... it's more like he sneered it at me, as though the idea was so absurd it couldn't survive daylight.

He'd just read my article about Clarence Thomas. About his speech at UT Austin last week, where he cited Sowell by name, called progressivism retrogressive, and connected it to the mass graves of the 20th century. It's going viral as I write this.

[Here's the Link]

The comments have been rolling endlessly. A lot of great feedback and praise from readers. There's also a lot of noise, people arguing, being nasty to each other. You know, normal internet stuff.

Then come the evangelical progressive mobs to try to enforce some narrative control. Uncle Tom slurs. Calls to demote me from "writer" to "racist." Angry enough to stop pretending they were the reasonable ones. Dozens of accounts calling me and my readers ignorant, stupid, and racist.

Our moral betters have arrived to teach us a lesson with their superior empathy and compassion!

Whatever... I've been at this for ten years... this is just another Monday for me. It used to make me mad, now all I see is prey coming into my territory to hunt.

But this young man's question stopped me.

I get it... Calling Hitler a progressive sounds absurd on its face. Hitler wasn't exactly a gender studies major worried about having the correct pronouns in his bio, right?

I gave him the benefit of the doubt. He's probably sincere. Maybe he'd never heard anyone make the argument out loud and was testing it.

Either way, the question deserved a serious answer. This is exactly the type of inquiry I welcome and love to explore in public.

So I took my time answering him yesterday evening. I did my research. Sent him what I thought was a solid reply.

Then he deleted his comment. Took my reply with it. I didn't save it anywhere.

Fine. I went to bed annoyed.

But the argument kept running in my head.

At 2am this morning a donation notification woke me up on my ipad. Eight pounds, from someone in the UK. God Bless You. Couldn't get back to sleep. Sat at my desk thinking about the reply that got nuked, and how much more there was to say anyway.

Decided I'd send it to you instead. With interest.

Five hours and three false starts later, now you're reading what came out of it.

I wanted to get it right.

What mode of government did the Nazis actually run? What did they do once in power? Planned economy. Centralized bureaucracy. An expert class designing society top-down for what they called the common good. Dissent crushed in the name of collective progress. A vision for a reborn nation, and anyone who resisted was backwards, irrational, or in the way.

Now ask yourself who else that description fits. Seems familiar, right?

Here's the reply I sent him before he nuked it. More or less:

Yes, in a sense, absolutely.

Hitler and his architect, Albert Speer, were urban planners at heart. Grand visionaries. They sat in a Berlin office drawing blueprints for a reborn Germany. The Autobahn. Welthauptstadt Germania, Speer's model of a rebuilt Berlin with a dome bigger than St. Peter's. Planned cities. Reorganized the countryside. The whole machine optimized from the top-down.

They had a welfare state. Price Controls. Public works. State-sponsored health programs. Strength Through Joy vacation societies for workers. Hitler was a vegetarian who pushed animal welfare laws. They talked constantly about worker dignity.

The party's full name was the National Socialist German Workers' Party.

That name wasn't a mistake.

Nazism was right-wing socialism. They organized their socialism around race instead of class. That's the only real difference from the Marxist flavor. Central planning. Expert class. Managed society. Dissent crushed in the name of the greater good.

Same Grandfather. Different Uncles.

That's roughly what I said to him as I recall.

Honestly, I had more to say anyway. I don't leave my best writing in Facebook comments, I save it for you guys. That's where the real signal belongs.

Let me give you a tool... a weapon, actually... something you can use to stop progressives cold. I promise you, they have no plan to handle this... they've never read their own documents. You can have some fun with it!

You ready?

Read the 1919 Italian Fascist Manifesto sometime. It's short, you'll read it in a few minutes. The perfect length for your next trip to the bathroom with your phone.

It calls for an 8-hour workday. Minimum wages. Women's suffrage. Progressive income taxation. National health insurance. Federal regulation of major industries. Workers' compensation. Worker representation in industry.

Does that sound like a right-wing document to you?

It was authored by literal fascists, and it reads like a modern progressive platform.

Let that sit for a minute.

The twentieth century wasn't left versus right. It was managerial regimes versus free people. Stalin, Mao, Hitler, Mussolini, and the American administrative state are cousins in a family tree, not opposites on a spectrum. Same confidence that an expert class designing society top-down will produce a better world than free people making their own choices.

That's what Clarence Thomas read into the record last week. Not that Bernie Sanders is literally Hitler... that the family tree is real. Direct lineage, it's time we said so.

Keep it. Use it. Next time someone scoffs at the idea that Hitler and the fascists were progressives, you have the case. It's not hard to make when you look at the documents. You have the receipts. Make them read the Fascist Manifesto with you, and then make them tell you exactly where they disagree with it. That's it. That's all you have to do. Now watch them squirm as they realize you're the predator, they're the prey.

Don't be afraid of these people, they don't know what they're talking about. There are exceptions, but they are exceedingly rare in my experience.

The weapon I just handed you is one of many I've been building. Arguments worth preserving. Frames worth deploying. Historical cases stress-tested and ready to use. The predator-or-prey frame. The pattern behind every character assassination of a conservative since Bork.

Right now they're scattered across posts and emails and comment threads. Some get nuked by young men who can't sit with a real answer.

I'm fixing that. Organized. Permanent. Yours to reach for when you need it.

More on that in the coming weeks.

For now, carry this one into the next conversation that demands it.

The young man won't.

stay close.

~ Clay

@StopBeingPrey on X/Twitter

subject: why they can't tolerate sowell
preview: his life proves theirs is a lie. that's the whole reason.
html:
Yesterday morning I opened my phone, went to the page, and there he was.

A guy I'd never seen before. Name: Kzadir. Comment under one of my posts... a Sowell quote about how many white Europeans were enslaved by Barbary pirates. The comment had nothing to do with the quote. One sentence.

"What has Thomas said or done for black empowerment? It's so easy to support or apologise for white folk. It pays more money too."

Let me ask you something before I tell you what I did with it.

Have you seen that sentence before?

Not that one specifically. The template. The structure. The move.

If you've spent any amount of time observing how black Americans who step outside the progressive line get attacked, you have. A hundred times. Different words, same engine. "He's a sellout." "He's an Uncle Tom." "He's a boot-licker." "He writes what white people pay to hear." I read these things every day, countless times, in my comments section.

Kzadir didn't invent that accusation. He was reciting it. From memory. Like a man who's heard it said so often he assumes it's true.

He's an NPC.

I honestly have no idea if Kzadir is a real person or a bot. That's the nature of the NPC meme... they operate in the exact same way. It's impossible to tell. Many real human beings behave exactly like bots on the internet, and in real life. They just run scripts.

And here's the thing... someone else wrote the script he was running.

That's the whole story. Who wrote it? Who benefits from it? Who keeps reprinting it in textbooks, on television, in classrooms, in Twitter algorithms, in Facebook comment threads?

The answer is not a secret... you've been watching them your whole life.

The people who write the script are the people who need black Americans to stay inside a single approved opinion. They've built an entire industry around it. They credential each other through it. They employ each other enforcing it. They excommunicate each other for violating it. They have names for their heretics, and the chief among those names is Thomas Sowell. My hero.

Kzadir showed up to do the excommunication, the way a dog shows up for a treat. He got something else.

Here's what I said to him.

Kzadir. Sowell literally inspired the career of Clarence Thomas. A sitting Supreme Court Justice. One of only two black men in American history to hold that seat.

And you have the nerve to come onto this page and say he doesn't do anything for black empowerment?

Do you hear yourself?

Then I told him, let's talk about what you actually mean by "empowerment."

BLM raised over ninety million dollars. Patrisse Cullors, the co-founder, bought a six million dollar mansion with donation money. Paid her brother eight hundred and forty thousand for "security." Paid her kid's father nine hundred and sixty nine thousand.

The 2020 riots caused between one and two billion dollars in damages. Record-setting. Multiple deaths, including the murder of David Dorn, a seventy-seven-year-old retired black police captain.

That's the "empowerment" industry Kzadir is defending. The grift that profits off black suffering while buying mansions.

Then I told him he could get on my list if he wanted to upgrade the quality of his thinking... or keep embarrassing himself in public. Either way, I win.

That's what fit in a Facebook comment.

Here's what didn't fit.... but you should know.

In 1975, a young angry black man read a book called Race and Economics. He'd been drifting left his whole life. Reading the Marxists. Pretending to be a revolutionary.

Fifty years later, that same black man writes the Supreme Court opinions that shape the entire American legal system. This month he stood at the University of Texas and cited Sowell by name from the stage. Called progressivism retrogressive. Said the Declaration of Independence is the wall between Americans and the mass graves the twentieth century dug for every country that traded Locke for Hegel. He said it clinically. He said it publicly.

That's not a man Sowell wrote for money to entertain. That's a man Sowell inspired. Lifted up.... Empowered.

And David Dorn... BLM got him killed. It's gotten a lot of blacks killed, if you think about it. That's the real dark truth behind 'Black Lives Matter', it is an extremely destructive movement for blacks, most of all. Tragic and shockingly evil.

Dorn was seventy-seven years old. black. Grandfather. Retired Saint Louis police captain. He came out of retirement the night of the riots to help a friend defend a pawn shop from the looters BLM had incited into the street. He was shot and left to die on the sidewalk in front of the store.

No statues. No murals. No Democrats kneeling in kente cloth. No televised funeral. No Saint George Floyd treatment.

The movement that got him killed was raising record-breaking donations that same week. Quite a grift, isn't it? Portraying themselves as the real victims the whole time.

So here's the question. Sit with it...

Which one was defending black empowerment? The man whose books inspired a Supreme Court Justice? Or the movement that bought mansions with donation money while black grandfathers died in the street?

The Bible has a line about recognizing a tree by its fruit. Pick your tree. Look at the fruit.

I'm writing about Clarence Thomas's recent UT Austin speech on the facebook page later today. If it lands, share it. The people I need to reach haven't heard any of this yet, and the algorithm is not going to put my work in front of them. You will.

Because here's what they can't afford. Sowell's life proves theirs is a lie. Clarence Thomas's life confirms it. Every reader who opens a Sowell book is a link in their chain that breaks.

Break another one.

~ Clay

subject: The sequel
preview: There's always one. His name is Brooks.
html:
Yesterday I shipped a post you might have seen on Facebook. A woman named Lyss wrote something ugly on my Charlie Kirk memorial post. I clicked her profile. She was a normal mother with a beautiful little daughter in her photo. And she wrote "Gums McBigot" about a murdered father in a public thread, while her kid's face sat two inches away from her words. A very sad thing. I prayed for her and especially her daughter last night, and I hope some of you did as well.

I wrote her a long reply. It might be the highest-engagement comment reply I've ever posted, and the crazy thing is, it was nearly a thousand words. It wasn't some quick hit for engagement. That's not normal for Facebook. But then, you guys aren't a normal audience. Literate, decent, and patient enough to read long work. That's rare. I know how lucky I am.

Here's what I want to tell you, because it's harder to explain on Facebook.

Something I didn't expect happened.

On posts like that, I usually get progressives piling in. They tell me I'm wrong. They call me names. They pick fights. I usually enjoy it. They make my case for me. I get my reps in, and I make training content from it. Frankly, I think I might have the best job in the world.

Yesterday, they didn't come. Not one of them came to argue with me or sling insults. That's rare, extremely rare for my page in particular. This usually means their coalition read the post, read my reply, and decided not to send more bodies.

Except one. There's always one. His name is Brooks.

I just published a new post about Brooks on the page. Full exchange plus my reply. You should read it. It's long, get yourself comfortable first.

Here's why Brooks matters more than Lyss:

Lyss was cruel. Everyone knows how to recognize cruelty. You don't need a book to see a Lyss coming.

Brooks, on the other hand, is sincere. He's a normal father with a tender Father's Day tribute to his own dead dad on his timeline. He's someone you'd be glad to have as a neighbor. And he wrote four paragraphs of boilerplate about Charlie Kirk, absorbing phrases that have been circulating on his side of the internet, writing them back out as if they were his own conclusions. Even though what he said was vile, he said it politely. No venom. No anger. That's what makes the disease so hard to see, and so hard to cure.

He didn't notice he was doing it.

Lyss and Brooks ran different scripts, but they both ran scripts.

This is what the book is actually about. Not evil people. Ordinary, decent people who stop thinking for themselves and let the tribe do it for them. The mob, so to speak.

Brooks is the case study. Lyss is the shock.

The reply I wrote him is probably the most important piece I've written this month. It applies the framework to a sincere case. A man who isn't being cruel, just running a script. And it shows what the book is going to help people do, for themselves and for the people they love who are getting lost.

It's on Facebook. Full text in the comments under the post.

[link to main-page post]

Brooks isn't the exception. Brooks is the rule. The book I'm writing will be the cure. That's my mission.

~ Clay

subject: Three moves. Order matters
preview: How I dismantled Adam yesterday without losing the room
html:
Yesterday you watched me do a thing on the page.

A commenter named Adam came at me with a standard leftist move: wage labor is just like taxation, both involve force, therefore both are theft, therefore capitalism is theft. Clean argument. Popular one on the left. You've seen it before, probably more than once.

I didn't insult him. I didn't dodge. I engaged him sincerely.

I dismantled the argument. Specifically. Three points, numbered. Then I mocked him once, lightly... then I released him. Told him to answer the questions in his own head, not back to me. Signed off in a state of perfect peace. I'm not sure if Adam can say the same.

Later, I took a screenshot of our conversation and wrote a post about what I'd just done. Named the three moves. Dismantle, mock, grace. Gave you the sequence.

The exchange is still on the page. You can read it.

Here's the part I didn't fully explain in that post. I'll explain it now.

The sequence is not optional.

Grace without the dismantle is weakness. If you skip the dismantle and go straight to grace, you look like somebody who wanted to avoid the fight. The audience smells it. The opponent smells it. You smell it on yourself later, when you're re-living the confrontation inside of your own head.

Dismantling without grace is crude and comes off as mean-spirited. You look like a brawler who can't stop hitting. You win the exchange and lose the audience. The thoughtful people watching you decide you're not the kind of person they want to be seen aligning with.

Here's the critical lesson: Dismantling earns you the right to offer grace.

Grace then becomes a demonstration of power, not a retreat from it. You could have kept hitting. You chose to stop. That's dominance wearing the costume of mercy. That's what predators do when they're not hungry.

Jordan Peterson has a version of this. His reading of "the meek shall inherit the earth." The Greek word doesn't mean weak, it means a trained warhorse. Power under command. Sword sheathed, not absent.

Same structure, different vocabulary. I use predator language because it's more honest about what actually happens in online conflict. But we're pointing at the same thing. Strength that chooses not to strike is the only kind that holds.

I'm telling you this because I'm going to do it again. And again. And again.

You're going to see me engage hostile commenters on the page nearly every day. Some of them will be real opponents worth a real reply. Some of them will become the next Randall, where they come for my throat, and I turn the engagement into a donation moment and a teaching tool in one move. Some of them I'll just heart-react and walk away from, and I'll explain that technique another time (it is more powerful than it looks).

The point is not that I'm good at this. The point is that these moves are learnable. I'm going to get my reps in, and you're going to watch me.

What you see on the page is the highlight reel.

What's coming in the community will be the training ground. The case studies I can't post publicly because they're too specific. The walkthroughs that name names I won't name here. The stuff I learned the hard way, broken down slow enough that you can actually use it.

Different format. Different function. Public is where I perform. Private is where I coach.

And soon. In the next few months, as the book comes together and the membership side of what I'm building goes live, I'm going to start teaching you to do this in your own life.

Starting with where most of you feel it sharpest: your comment sections.

The stranger who drops a one-liner that eats at you for three days. The ex-friend who keeps showing up in your threads to correct you in front of mutuals. The cousin who argues with you on Facebook but won't say a word at the dinner table. The debate-bro who keeps tagging you into fights you didn't start.

Same muscle works offline. The relative at Thanksgiving. The coworker chipping at you in a meeting. The authority figure using soft pressure to make sure you never quite say what you think.

Facebook is where I practice. For a lot of you, Facebook is where the actual fight happens.

~ Clay

subject: I caught myself being prey today
preview: Let me walk you through the twenty seconds I lost this morning.
html:
I had a consultation with an accountant this morning, about my book and this whole thing we're doing here. First meeting. He was over 15 minutes late, I was nervous, I'm not even sure why... eventually we connected.

He asked me about the book.

And I soft-pedaled it.

I gave him a half-version. Watered down the frame. Didn't quite say what the book actually does or who it's for. Why? Because I noticed a communist star in a picture on a table beside him, and some small part of me decided I'd better not make him uncomfortable. For all I know, that's just some art he picked up on a vacation. Or a gift from a friend. I assigned a meaning it likely doesn't have, out of anxiety. Prey behavior.

I caught it afterward. Sat with it. Felt a bit of shame.

That's the move. The one I write about every day. Predators don't need to attack you to control you. They just need to put out a vibe. You do the softening yourself. You pre-edit your thoughts to fit what you think they want to hear. You shrink to fit the room.

I did that. With my own book. In a room where the other person wasn't even pressuring me. Just one decoration on a shelf and my own anxiety about politics.

That's prey behavior. I teach against it. And I still did it.

Here's the part I want you to sit with.

I have the prey instinct in me. All the time. Every day. I fight it constantly. Anyone who reads me and assumes I've figured this out or transcended it is wrong. I haven't. I'm IN the fight with you. I slip. I catch myself. I slip again. I catch myself faster. That's the work. I'm still figuring all this out. You are watching me figure it out in real time. I've learned all of this stuff the hard way.

If you're a Christian, you already understand how this works. We are sinners by nature. We don't escape that by declaring it. We confess it, we pray against it, we rise and fall and rise again, and the life is in the discipline. The saints aren't the ones who stopped sinning. They're the ones who never stopped praying.

The predator life works the same way. You don't become predator once and coast. The prey instinct doesn't go away. It adapts. It hides. It dresses up in new costumes: humility, politeness, "being reasonable." You have to meet it every day, name it when you see it, and refuse to let it run you. It is a critical part of who you are. It is the animal in us. The beast, some call it. The part that battles with our soul.

And you have to admit it's in you. You are not Him. You are fallen.

That's the part I think a lot of my readers resist. They think admitting they have prey instincts means they're weak. It's the opposite. The weakness is pretending you don't have them. The strength is naming them and showing up to the fight anyway. Awareness is the key. You have to be brutally honest with yourself. You have to admit things you don't want to admit about yourself.

The work doesn't end. I had a moment today where my prey instinct ran me for about twenty seconds. I caught it. I named it. I'll rehearse the fix this weekend so next time it's ten seconds. Then five. Then I catch it before it happens.

That's the work. Every day. Same as prayer.

Notice. Then stop.

~ Clay

subject: I turned a hater into $300
preview: And I want to show you how we do it again
html:
Two days ago I made a decision to exercise some power. To set an example.

A guy named Randall walked into my comments calling me an idiot. Pseudo-intellectual. Greedy. Nobody wants to read my wall of words. Nice guy. Thought he was going to be my predator.

By nightfall I had turned him into about $300. Made a public spectacle of him. Had strangers lining up with messages addressed to him personally, with dollar signs attached. One man dropped $100 with "say hi to Randall for me." A woman sent $1 with "decades of research vs. one insult, tough choice."

By nightfall Randall had blocked me and disappeared. Our budding friendship is off to a rough start!

That was not a fight. That was a demonstration. Complete and total domination. Everyone who watched it knew what they were watching. Especially Randall. That's why all he could do is put his tail between his legs and run. Some predator, huh?

I'll be honest with you. I feel for Randall. He's probably just some lost kid who walked into the wrong room. I've had my ass handed to me in public debates before. It's not fun. At the time I thought it was the worst thing that ever happened to me. Turned out to be one of the best. It sharpened me. If Randall has any ability to self-correct, this will sharpen him too. I pray for him. I mean that.

Here's what I want you to see.

Randall thought he was the predator when he walked into my comments section. He walked in aggressive, confident, dismissive. He thought that was power. It wasn't. I laid a trap, and he walked right into it. Prey.

Power is not aggression. Power is control of the outcome. Randall controlled nothing. Not the audience. Not the frame. Not the narrative. Not the money. I controlled all of it. Every piece. From the moment he commented, he was already inside something he didn't build, couldn't see, and couldn't escape. He didn't see any of it until it was too late. These are our enemies. This is who conservatives are losing to. Isn't that embarrassing?

That is the difference between a predator and prey who thinks he's a predator. Most of the loud, aggressive people in your life are Randalls. They mistake volume for power. Once you can see that, they never look the same again.

And here's the part that should keep you up at night. What I did to Randall is what progressives do to conservatives every single day. They control the frame. They control the institutions. They control the narrative. They lay traps. And most conservatives walk in swinging, thinking volume is power, and never once realize they're already inside something they didn't build, can't see, and can't escape. See: January 6th.

That is what I'm teaching you to see. That is what the book is about. And that is what I want to build with you.

I have the stage. You have the ammunition. I can't turn Randall into $300 without you. You can't turn Randall into $300 without me.

And there are a lot more Randalls out there.

They're in my comments right now. They're in yours too. The loud ones. The confident ones. The ones who mistake volume for power and have never once been shown what real power looks like, and where they really belong in the world.

We're going to show them. Regularly. I will find them. I will set the stage. And when I do, I want you there with a dollar and a message.

This is not a one-time thing. This is how we operate now. Every Randall who walks in becomes a demonstration. Every demonstration funds the book. Every chapter of the book teaches more people to see what you're learning to see right now.

The game is on. And we're playing for real now.

I'm going to be honest with you because I think you're smart enough to sense it, and I know you can handle it. I'm not a charity. I'm a writer building a weapon. The book is the weapon. These people can sense that I'm on to something and that's exactly why they come into my comments swinging.

I have a life. I have expenses. I have responsibilities. Every dollar you send on a Randall day buys me more writing time instead of having to worry about something else. That is the deal. You fund the weapon. I build it. You get to read it. And we use it together.

Your dollar is your word. It's your way of saying "I'm with you. Keep going." Even $1. That's enough. I'm not asking for your money. I'm asking you to grant me the power to publicly humiliate our predators.

Stop being prey.

~ Clay

subject: I accidentally wrote my masterpiece yesterday morning
preview: I didn't plan to add to the library this fast.
html:
I may have just accidentally written one of my masterpieces.

Yesterday morning, I launched a library section on ReadSowell.com with two of my best pieces. I didn't expect to add a third one this fast.

That same morning, I sat down to write what I thought would be a quick Facebook post. Maybe a couple paragraphs. By the time I looked up, I realized that I had written a manifesto.

It's the frame I've been building toward for months. The one that's going to be the spine of my book. I finally synthesized it and got it right.

Are you Predator or Prey? That's it. That's the entire frame. Once you see it, every political fight you've ever lost starts to make sense. Every relative at Thanksgiving. Every annoying coworker. Every politician who looked good then got himself eaten. Every conservative who thought being polite was a strategy.

Read it here. This framework is the missing piece conservatives need to stop losing. And it's resonating. Look at the engagement, the shares, the comments. I've struck a nerve, and I'm just getting started.

It is a long read. It will take you a few minutes. I want you to read it slowly, because there is a moment in the middle where you will either feel relieved or accused, and that moment is going to be central to the book. It's a filter for the real ones.

After you read it, ask yourself the question I asked at the bottom.

Are you with me?

~ Clay

subject: I built something this weekend

readsowell.com/library

A permanent home for the good stuff. The pieces worth keeping. The ones that you guys told me were special. Something you can actually share with people. A link you can text to a friend or post on your wall instead of trying to describe what some guy named Clay wrote to you at 6am on a Tuesday.

Both pieces are up right now.

"We Pray for Our Prey." If you read one thing I've ever written, read that. According to many of you who wrote to me, it's my most powerful piece yet. It also helps give you an idea of the book I'm writing. 'Stop Being Prey'

I wonder how many people picked up a Sowell book for the first time that week? More than a few, I can tell you that. You guys should see some of the messages I get, especially from young people who are just discovering Dr. Sowell's work right now. This weekend. Because of something I wrote, and you shared.

It's incredibly motivating.

That's what we're doing here. I can't do it without you.

stay close,
