subject: I need to tell you something...
preview: should have told you sooner
html:
I'm becoming a real writer. I'm still not used to saying that, but it appears to be the new reality that I find myself in, and I can't tell you how grateful I am for it. It feels right to write.

I realized, very recently, that this is my life's purpose. I've been working towards this my whole life and didn't know it. I need to write. People need me to write. I have something to say, and people need to hear it. This is not hubris. This is real.

I have figured out something about the way progressives operate and how to explain it to others that just has not been done yet. And it needs to be done. Must be done. Or we're dead. Is that hyperbole? Well, where's Charlie?

Before I go any further, I need to tell you something I've never said publicly.

I'm Canadian....

I know...

I'm sorry, eh?

The person who has been writing to you about Thomas Sowell, about predators and prey, about conservatives losing easy battles, about the civilization we love and the people trying to tear it down... he's a leaf, from inside the bowels of Canuckistan.

Still with me? Good. Because this is important.

I should have told you sooner. I'm telling you now because what I'm about to say requires you to know where I'm standing.

Canada has been totally captured by our predators.

I see it every day. I see "elbows up" signs all over my neighborhood. If you don't know what that means, I envy you. I see people I love talking about Trump like he's the next Hitler. I see people who have been clamoring for gun control, taking legal guns away from their own citizens, claiming we might have to go to war with America at some point. It's delusional. It's sick.

What the CBC, our state broadcaster, is doing to the minds of these people is a crime. I genuinely believe that.

And the conservatives? The ones who are supposed to be fighting back?

They're doing nothing. Worse than nothing. They're capitulating. They're getting absolutely dominated. And when I talk to conservative voters up here, they think they're still in the fight. They actually believe that.

The Liberals have taken a full majority. They've captured every institution. They run the public schools. They run the regulatory agencies. They run the big banks. They run the universities. The police, the prisons, the military... They run the entire government now. Every single element of it.

And you talk to a Canadian conservative, and they think because Pierre Poilievre gave a good speech one day, and gave us the most boring Joe Rogan episode of all time, he's standing up and fighting.

You know what's sad? He used to actually show some teeth. Some of you might remember the famous clip where he stood there eating an apple while a CBC journalist tried to corner him with the usual disingenuous, bad-faith questions they're trained to ask. He just chewed and smirked and dismissed him on the spot, made fun of him, and showed the audience what he was doing with grace and good humor. It was predator behavior. Real predator behavior. The good kind. I was an early supporter of his because of moments like that.

And now? He won't even criticize Mark Carney on the biggest podcast in the world.

"I won't criticize him on foreign soil. We have a mutual respect."

That's a verbatim quote. What happened? Who put him on a leash? Who owns this pet?

It's embarrassing. I feel actual secondhand embarrassment watching these people talk about politics now. They have lost. It's over. There is no democratic solution for them now. And they don't see it, or they don't want us to see it. I'm not quite sure which.

Here's what I do know... Pierre Poilievre is now behaving like prey. And he's leading his people into a lion's den. That's the conservative plan. That's how they plan to win. Follow the prey into the predator's territory and hope for the best. How's that working out, so far? Such serious people, these Canadian Conservatives. Real power players.

Mark Carney is a predator, straight out of the City of London and Davos. Look at him smile, he literally has fangs. The man was born for this. He doesn't care if you call him a hypocrite. He doesn't care if you catch him in a lie. It doesn't register on his radar, at all. You are nothing to him. He knows he has power over you, and he knows he can bend you to his will. And he does, every day. Just like Trump can bend his haters to his will, Mark Carney does the same to the Canadian Conservatives. He can push their buttons, make them angry on a whim, and he can lead them right into all of his clever little WEF traps.

Canadian Conservatives, you are his prey and you don't even know it. He's got you. You fall for every trap he sets. You just walked him into a majority government.

And you think you're fighting. Do you not feel, even a hint of embarrassment?

I say this because I love my country. I say this because someone has to. Not to be cruel. Because you need to hear it. You've lost. It's over. And until you see that clearly, you cannot begin to fix it.

I need you to understand something about Canada and America. My grandfather fought in World War II alongside Americans. I have American friends and family. I've done business in America. Our two countries have had one of the strongest relationships any two nations have ever shared in the history of the world.

And these people are throwing it away. Right now. Over a cartoon version of Donald Trump that the CBC painted for them. They are willing to destroy a relationship that was forged in blood, built over generations, and held together by shared values, because their state broadcaster told them to be angry about the orange man.

These people are a danger to me. I believe that. I don't know what to do about it other than write and tell you what's happening up here.

There are great Canadians. A lot of them. But we are outnumbered, and we are overwhelmed. Pray for us.

I write for them.

That is why I'm writing the book. That is why I need you.

I don't have a First Amendment. There is no guaranteed right to free speech where I live. There are hate speech laws. There are tribunals. There are complaints that can be filed against a writer for saying things that make someone uncomfortable. The legal framework exists to punish me for the things I write to you every morning.

I write them anyway.

But I need you to understand what that means. The only thing that protects a writer like me is an audience that would notice if he disappeared. You are that audience. Every time you open these emails, every time you share these posts, every time you subscribe or tell a friend, you are not just supporting a writer. You are making it harder for anyone to quietly shut him down.

That is what you are to me. Not just readers. A shield.

subject: Professors are not impressive people
preview: I will teach you how to make them look like children in front of an audience
html:
Professors are not stupid, usually, but they are not quite as smart as they think they are, either. This is their Achilles heel.

To be clear... Not all, not all, not all... but most. There are brilliant exceptions. Some of them are reading this email right now. But those exceptions prove the rule. They don't disprove it.

Let me explain what a university professor actually is in 2026.

They are the high priests of an institution that does not educate. It lectures. It pronounces. It hands down approved conclusions from above and punishes anyone in the room who pushes back. A university professor does not have to persuade anyone of anything. He has grades. He has tenure committees. He has the entire institutional weight of the university behind him. He doesn't win arguments. He doesn't have to. He simply declares, and the room obeys, or the room gets punished.

That is not intelligence. That is authority without accountability. And it produces a very specific kind of person: someone who has spent decades being "right" without ever once being seriously challenged.

These are the people training our predators. This is their weakness. Study them, and you will become an undeniable weapon, I promise you.

You see their disciples everywhere. The activists burning down your cities. The ones worshipping statues of Saint George Floyd and calling you a racist for not kneeling. The ones who call Kyle Rittenhouse a racist mass murderer. The ones who celebrated Charlie Kirk's murder and mock you for mourning him. The ones who wish Donald Trump didn't turn his head at the last second in Butler.

These are the shock troops of the progressive cathedral. Trained by our esteemed professors.

They show up at your Thanksgiving table with rehearsed talking points and a condescending smile. They show up in my comments every single day, extraordinarily confident with their fancy degrees.

They all came from the same place. The same lecture halls. The same professors. The same ideology, handed down like scripture from tenured clergy who have never had to defend a single one of their ideas in the open air. They aren't ready for the fight we are going to bring to them. I promise you. They aren't ready for you, if you follow what I'm telling you.

You might think I'm exaggerating. I'm not. Open Marxists are teaching in elite Western universities right now. Marxism. The ideology responsible for more deaths than any other in human history. Can you imagine if we had serious tenured Nazi professors? "Real Nazism hasn't been tried." People would burn the building down, rightfully so. But somehow we tolerate and fund professors who preach the ideology that actually won its war and killed a hundred million people in the process.

And I'm supposed to be impressed when one of these people walks into my comment section? Please. I'm disgusted. They make me sick.

I see them and their disciples regularly. They come in with their credentials and their confidence and their rehearsed positions. They have never been in a room where someone looked them in the eye and said, "Which specific claim are you referring to?" They have never had someone say, "That is a technique, not an argument, and I'm going to show everyone here how it works."

I say those things, with grace. And they crumble. Every... single... time. This is what I do for fun now. I hunt them. It's my new hobby.

I am a college dropout. I spent my twenties smoking too much weed and playing too many video games. Not proud of that, but it's the truth, and you should know it. I have no credentials, no letters after my name, and no institutional authority. And I take these people apart with total ease.

Not because I'm smarter than them. Because I see what they are doing. I see the technique underneath the confidence. I see the authority underneath the argument. I see the predator underneath the professor and his legions of trained disciples.

They come to my comments looking for prey. They think you are prey. They find something else. Me. And soon, they're going to stumble upon you and regret it, too. You're going to make my job even easier. I can already see some of you applying my lessons in there.

That is what my book is about. That is what Stop Being Prey will teach you to do. Not theory. Not philosophy. The actual skill of seeing predators for what they are and making them wish they had never walked into your life, gracefully.

I will teach you how to toy with them like a cat with a mouse. And you will enjoy every second of it.

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: ChatGPT lied to them. I had the source
preview: and I am only going to say this once
html:
Last night, a fellow writer reached out to me privately. She told me it was killing her that I might be using AI to write. We went back and forth for a while about the implications of AI for writers. By the end, she told me she appreciated me and that we were pondering the same questions. Best argument I have had in a while.

But her message forced me to think about something I keep seeing and have never addressed publicly.

People come into my comments and tell me my Sowell quotes are fake. They paste them into ChatGPT, ask it if the quote is real, and ChatGPT tells them no. It tells them that I'm lying to them. So they come back to me with righteous indignation, all confident that I am a fraud who needs to be exposed, and they're the hero that's going to swoop in and show the world what I'm up to.

Then I pull up the source. Book. Chapter. Page number. They either apologize or they disappear.

This happens to me constantly. Every day, just about. And I'm telling you about it because I need you to notice what is actually going on. The people using AI to check my work are the ones being lied to. I am the one with the source.

That is the AI problem in a nutshell, as I see it. Not that someone might be using a tool to help them write. It's that millions of people are trusting a tool they do not understand to think for them, and the tool is lying, and they cannot tell. Frankly, I believe public schools, universities, and the media are the real culprits here. They trained the masses to be obedient to political narratives, not how to think.

Our enemies understand this, intimately. They are using these tools without hesitation. They are in your feeds, in your comments, reaching more people every day with less substance than you or I would ever accept. And what is our side doing? Standing on principle. Refusing the tool. Blaming the tool. Losing, gracefully, with our 'principles', the way we have been losing my entire life. I'm sick of it, and I bet you are too. I know you are, that's why you're still reading this.

I am not interested in losing gracefully. I never was.

Here is the only thing I will say about AI and my work. This is my voice. I chose these thoughts, I chose these words. I decided they should be organized this way and given to you for a purpose that originated inside my own head. If that is not enough for you, nothing I say will be. If it is, then the question was never worth asking.

I think you can tell the difference. That is why you are here.

"By their fruits ye shall know them."

stay close,

~ Clay

subject: We pray for our prey
preview: That is what makes us different from them.
html:
We pray for our prey.

That is the line I did not know I was going to write until this morning, and it is the one that explains everything I have been trying to tell you for two weeks.

Here is what I mean.

On Easter Sunday a man named Nathan showed up on my tribute to Charlie Kirk and called a murdered father evil. On Easter Monday he came back with more of the same. Louder this time. Meaner. Three new names. Zero new evidence. When I dissected him in public, he did not bring an argument. He brought more volume.

At the end of my reply to him, I wrote one sentence: “I’ll pray for you.” I meant it. I still mean it today.

And that sentence is the whole thing.

We must become predators out of necessity. Charlie is dead. Trump has been shot at. Strangers are walking into tribute posts on Easter Sunday to sneer at the corpses of murdered fathers, and mock the people mourning them. The old framework of civility and debate died with the people who trusted it. Someone has to teach what comes next. That is the work I am doing now.

But there is one thing that separates what we are becoming from what they already are. One thing. It is not technique. Technique can be learned by anyone. It is not intelligence. Intelligence does not protect you from becoming a monster. It is not even courage.

It is grace.

We pray for them. They do not pray for us. They never will.

That single beat, the prayer for the prey, is the difference between a monster with a weapon and a disciplined man with a conscience who happens to know how to hunt.

Because we pray for them, we are free.

Free from having to hate them. Free from needing their approval, their agreement, their acknowledgment, or their surrender. Free from spending our minds trying to convince men who were never going to be convinced. When a Nathan shows up and cannot cite a page, cannot defend a claim, cannot change his mind under any evidence, you are not in a debate. You are being recruited into a hunt, and your mind is the bait.

You do not owe him your time. You do not owe him your energy. You owe him exactly one thing, and it is the same thing you owe the rest of them.

A prayer. And nothing else.

And because we pray for them, when we do choose to engage, we engage without becoming them.

When the fight is worth fighting, when the audience is worth protecting, when the predator is hurting someone you love, you do not walk away. You stay. But you do not match his energy. You do something he is incapable of. You shine a light on his trap, let the people watching see exactly what he did, take him apart with composure, and walk away bigger than you arrived. That is what I did to Nathan over Easter. That is what I did to three more of them yesterday. Go look at my page. The dismantlings are still live.

And then, after all of it, you pray for him. Because that is what makes you different from him. Because that is the thing he cannot do. Because that is the thing he cannot understand, and the thing he cannot answer.

This is what I am training you to become.

Not a peaceful man who never fights. Not a raging man who always does. Something different. A disciplined predator who walks away when the fight is unworthy and hunts back when it is, and prays for every single one of them, every time, no matter which.

A hunter who prays for his prey.

A gentleman with a light.

A man the Nathans have never met.

That is what Stop Being Prey is. The book. The community. The whole project. I am training a class of people these predators have never seen before, and the thing that distinguishes us from them is the one thing they will never learn to do themselves.

You are not running from them anymore. You are not matching them either. You are learning to stalk them with a smile and a prayer.

Start today.

Stay close,

~ Clay

subject: I've got butterflies writing this one
preview: Something happened on my Charlie Kirk tribute yesterday.
html:
I’ve got butterflies writing this one.

I don’t get them often. Figured you should know that going in.

Yesterday I posted an Easter tribute to Charlie Kirk. A picture of me wearing the Freedom shirt he was wearing when they killed him. First Easter without him.

I quoted the motto of the Mises Institute: “Do not give in to evil, but proceed ever more boldly against it.”

I said that’s what Charlie did every day of his life.

A man named Nathan read the whole thing. Then he wrote this:

“Do not give in to evil while praising kirk is crazy work.”

Read that again.

Nathan didn’t show up to disagree. He didn’t show up to debate. He showed up on the tribute post of a murdered father, on Easter Sunday, and called him evil. Using the exact line I had just quoted from Mises. On his first Easter in the ground.

I sat with it for two hours this morning. Sipping my coffee. Should I delete it? Ignore it? Lose my temper? None of those work. Men like Nathan show up on sacred ground precisely because it’s sacred. They are counting on you to flinch.

It is pure, animalistic, predatory behavior. I will keep calling it that. Not as a metaphor. As a description. Once you see it clearly, you stop getting caught by it.

So I did something else. I wrote this back:

“Nathan, you’re a father. You love your kid. Anyone can see that from your profile.

That’s what makes what you just did so bizarre. Let me walk you through it.” click to see the full reply

Here is the move:

You don't fall for the trap. You don't argue. You don't match his energy. You name the predator. You shine a light on his trap. You let the people watching see it with their own eyes. Then you pray for him.

That is the whole thing. It is not complicated. It is just hard. Every animal instinct in us wants to lash out at him. That's the prey in you. It's in all of us.

Now here’s the part I actually need to tell you.

(And if you joined this list in the last few days, welcome. You picked an interesting weekend to show up. This is the email where you find out what you signed up for.)

For ten years I ran the largest Thomas Sowell page on Facebook without writing in my own voice. I posted his words. I thought my job was to be a vessel for his.

A few weeks ago I started writing my own posts. Just to see what would happen.

The response broke something open. Every piece of my own writing lands harder than the quotes. Readers I had never heard from are sending me letters. The list has doubled in a week.

You've been telling me I was wrong.

Thomas Sowell already gave us everything we needed. Forty books. A lifetime of scholarship. A foundation that will outlast all of us. He did his part. More than his part. But he is 95 years old, and the cultural street war of 2026 is a different kind of fight than the one he spent his life preparing us for.

This fight is ours.

And nobody on our side has written the manual for it, certainly not to my satisfaction. Sowell wrote the library. I am writing the field manual. Saul Alinsky wrote Rules for Radicals for the left. I am writing my answer to it. For us. Not a rant. Not a revenge book. A playbook for regular people who are sick of getting bullied at the dinner table, in the comment section, in the group chat, and even on a tribute to someone they love.

That is what Stop Being Prey is. A field manual for protecting the people you love from people who mean them harm and think they know everything. Predators.

But it is more than a book. I am building a place. A community where I train regular people to do what I just did to Nathan, in their own lives, at their own tables. Real conversations. Real breakdowns. Me in your corner when you need backup on an argument that matters. I write code for a living. I am building the whole thing myself, on my own platform, so nobody can pull the plug on us.

Nathan is just the first proof of concept. There are more of him in your life. At your Thanksgiving. In your family group chat. In the comments on your mother’s Facebook post. You don’t have to be their prey. Neither does she.

It's time for conservatives to stop being prey. Become the apex predator. Better than they are. They use power to destroy. We will use it for the good, the true, and the beautiful. That is how we honor the life and sacrifice of Charlie Kirk.

That’s the butterflies. That’s why this email had to go out today.

Stay Close

~ Clay

Tu ne cede malis sed contra audentior ito
Do not give in to evil but proceed ever more boldly against it

subject: Well done, Mr. Sowell.

Happy Easter. I hope you're with people you love today.

Now let me tell you something that kept happening this week that I can't stop thinking about.

A man named Mike left a comment on one of my posts.

"Well done, Mr. Sowell."

He thought Thomas Sowell wrote it. He didn't. I did.

Maria thought the same thing. So did Lisa. Three people, same mistake. They read something I wrote and assumed it came from one of the greatest thinkers of the last century.

That's either very flattering to me or very insulting to Dr. Sowell. I'll let you decide.

Thomas Sowell. Harvard. Columbia. PhD in economics from the University of Chicago. Taught at Cornell and UCLA. Published dozens of books. Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford.

Me. College dropout. Small town nobody's ever heard of. Writes code. Runs a Facebook page.

And three of you thought I was him.

I've been running this page for ten years, posting Sowell's words, watching them spread, and staying out of the way. A few weeks ago, I started writing my own thoughts. And something changed.

You responded differently. Harder. Faster. More shares. More comments. More of you showing up in my inbox saying "how do I see more of this?"

So I listened.

You're not just sharing quotes. You're fighting. At work. At dinner. With your brother-in-law who says something you know is wrong. You feel it in your gut. But you can't find the words. So you say nothing and stew on it at 2am. Or you say something and walk right into the trap they set for you.

Either way, you lose.

I've been there. I've made every mistake you've made. Probably worse. And over time, I started seeing the patterns.

You're not asking me for a show. You're not asking me for videos. You're telling me to write.

Right?

I'm a capitalist. And a capitalist listens to the market.

I have a plan. I'm not ready to tell you all of it yet. But it starts with writing. And it ends with you never losing one of these arguments again.

Stay close.

Clay

subject: Andy Witham
preview: I found his phone on a ledge.
html:
There's a beat-up copy of 1984 sitting on my desk right now.

It's been there for a few days. I keep looking at it.

Not because of Orwell. Because of the kid who gave it to me.

I was living in Hamilton, Ontario. Found a cell phone on the ledge by my driveway. Picked it up, called a number in the contacts, told them I had their friend's phone.

A few hours later, this kid shows up at my door. Young. Sweet. Maybe autistic, I'm not sure. Had a woman with him. Sister, friend, I don't know.

He was grateful in a way you almost never see. Not polite grateful. The real kind. Like returning his phone was the biggest thing anyone had done for him in a long time.

We talked for a while. One of those random nights where you meet someone and think, "I could be friends with this person."

I never saw him again.

Before he left, he handed me his copy of 1984. Told me he was an anarchist. I said I'd always meant to read it. Inside the front cover he'd written: "To the Angel Sapien who returned my cellular device. Thank you. Andy."

I looked his name up a few years later. I'm pretty sure I found his obituary.

Here's what I keep thinking about:

Andy called himself an anarchist. If he were still around, I think he'd be furious about Trump. Probably would have fallen into the whole Antifa thing. Might have been one of those people I watch clips of and shake my head at.

And I'd still miss him.

That's the thing nobody on our side wants to say out loud. The people we're up against aren't all predators. Some of them are confused kids who fell down a rabbit hole and never found their way out. Some of them are sweet, lost people with terrible ideas and horrible mentors. Some of them are Andy.

I spend a lot of time teaching you how to spot traps. How to stop being prey. How to fight smarter. I mean every word of it.

But every once in a while I look at that book on my desk and I remember that the kid who gave it to me would probably hate everything I post.

And he was one of the kindest people I ever met.

I don't know what to do with that. I just know it's true.

Clay

P.S. If you've got an Andy in your life, someone good who got lost along the way, keep them in your thoughts today.

The tell is always the same. They never say "good point." They don't even pause to think for a minute. They just reclassify. Move the goalposts. Shrink the evidence until it doesn't count anymore. Anything to avoid the two words that would end the conversation: "you're right."

I get a few Johns a day. Keeps things interesting.

subject: He asked. I answered. He panicked.
preview: He thought it was a gotcha
html:
I posted this Sowell quote about free speech yesterday. Someone on my page asked, "Who isn't free to speak their mind?"

He thought it was a gotcha.

I said: Charlie Kirk. Went to speak freely on a college campus. Was killed for it.

His reply: "He was killed by some rando. What the fuck does that have to do with anything?"

Think about that.

He asked who isn't free to speak. I gave him a man who was murdered for speaking. And his first move was to dismiss it. Not engage with it. Not reconsider his question. Just wave it away and pretend it didn't count.

That's the tell. He wasn't asking a question. He was making a statement dressed up as a question. And when someone called his bluff, he couldn't handle the answer.

You see this pattern everywhere once you know what to look for. People who frame their position as a question so they never have to defend it.

"Name one example."
You name one.
"That doesn't count."
You name another.
"That's different."

The game isn't to find the truth. The game is to never be wrong.

"They don't use language to communicate, they use it to manipulate" - Michael Malice

Sowell wrote about this exact mentality as well. These aren't people seeking answers. They're people protecting a vision.

Clay

subject: He called me a boot-licker
preview: He walked right into my trap
html:
Someone told me last night that hunger is a form of tyranny.

I'm serious. I posted a Sowell quote about the left wanting to be our shepherds, and this guy fires back, saying that since you can't choose NOT to eat, not to pay rent, not to need health coverage, your freedom is basically a scam. You're not really free. You're just a boot-licker who doesn't know it yet.

His words, not mine.

Now, I find this kind of thing fascinating. Not because it's smart. Because it reveals something.

Think about what he's really saying here.

He looked at the basic conditions of being alive, the fact that survival takes effort, and decided that's oppression. As if nature owes him something. As if the fact that food doesn't fall from the sky means somebody, somewhere, is ruling him.

Hunger is not a ruler. Scarcity is not a boss. Nature doesn't become tyranny just because it refuses to feed you for free.

Free people figured that out thousands of years ago. You trade, you cooperate, you build something. Nobody has to be in charge of everything for it to work. But this guy can't see that. He sees the hard facts of life and immediately demands an administrator.

He can't imagine free men solving problems together. He can only imagine herds managed by shepherds.

Which is precisely what Sowell was talking about.

The guy showed up to argue against the quote and ended up living it.

Clay

subject: Capitalism helped the poor. The left just helped themselves.
html:
The left says they care about the poor, and they'll even say you don't if you don't support them.

But good intentions don’t build anything.
What actually worked was capitalism.

Markets.
Private Property Rights
Voluntary exchange.
Millions of people voluntarily solving problems for each other.

It isn’t perfect — nothing is.
But it’s worked better than any government program, by orders of magnitude.

If you stacked every government program ever created, they still wouldn’t touch what capitalism has done for the poor.

Sowell said it better than I ever could:

“No government of the left has done as much for the poor as capitalism has.” - Thomas Sowell

He wasn’t speaking from theory.
He saw the data.
And more importantly… he saw the consequences.

I had to put this quote on a shirt, because some ideas are worth repeating out loud and starting conversations with.

And if you want to see the full quote in its full context, it's all right here 👈

—Clay
